To address this challenge, we investigate a dynamic combinable attention-based spatial and channel reconstruction convolutional network (DCA-SCRCNet) that leverages redundant features in weak MI-EEG signals to optimize spatial distribution features and inter-channel interactions relationships. This optimization is achieved through weight-based feature reconstruction in the spatial and channel reconstruction convolution (SCRC) module. Importantly, dynamic combinable attention (DCA) enables DCA-SCRCNet to adapt to differences in the non-stationary MI-EEG signals individual characteristics by weighting input features and integrating local and global information. The processed features are then fed into the temporal convolutional network (TCN) for further extraction of long-term dependencies and finer timing characteristics. On the BCI Competition IV-2a dataset (BCI-2a), subject-independent and subject-dependent models yielded accuracies of 70.7 % and 90.5 %, respectively, demonstrating its efficient spatio-temporal feature extraction capability while reducing computational redundancy. On the PhysioNet dataset, the proposed algorithm achieved multi-subject validation accuracies of 92.7 % and 76.2 % for two and four-class classification tasks, respectively, surpassing current mainstream methods.

title: LMACV: A lightweight multiscale ACmix–VMamba framework for efficient multimodal medical image fusion
abstract: Current imaging sensors are incapable of simultaneously obtaining functional metabolic activity and structural tissue features, thus substantially limiting diagnostic accuracy in clinical practice. Multimodal Medical Image Fusion (MMIF) uses complementary data from MRI, CT, PET, and SPECT to improve diagnostic representations and promote precise tissue segmentation. Recent developments in deep learning, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and transformer models, have greatly improved the performance and flexibility of image fusion methods. Existing models, however, have two significant drawbacks. CNNs face the problem of long-range context due to the limitations of their small receptive fields. Conversely, transformers are ideal for capturing global dependencies but have a quadratic computational overhead, limiting their scalability. In this study, we present LMACV, a lightweight fusion framework that integrates grouped ACmix for local details and a Multi-Stage Visual State Space (MVSS) module—built upon VMamba—for efficient global modeling within a two-level multiscale pyramid. The design increases receptive field and representation hierarchy while maintaining linear complexity and low parameter counts. Experiments on medical image fusion tasks show that LMACV outperforms previous approaches in visual quality and quantitative parameters. Furthermore, LMACV exhibits better generalization in downstream segmentation and detection tasks.

title: MCCT-Net: A multi-perspective convolution and cross-connection transformer network for epilepsy detection
abstract: At present, the detection of epilepsy based on EEG has been a research hotspot. In this study, a novel network integrating a multi-perspective convolution and cross-connection transformer (MCCT-Net) was proposed to classify normal and seizure signals. Firstly, a preprocessing component which includes a channel selection, a filtering, and the Gramian Angular Field (GAF) transformation was used to transform the raw EEG signals into their corresponding clear GAF matrixes. Then, the matrixes were fed into the MCCT-Net which utilizes a novel multi-perspective convolution scheme to achieve broader and more comprehensive receptive fields than the classical 3 × 3 convolution. Additionally, a cross-connection was integrated into the transformer structure to amplify relevant features for obtaining the more focused and comprehensive information. Finally, the proposed method demonstrated strong performance on the CHB-MIT database, achieving an accuracy of 98.14 % with an FDR of 0.26/h in patient-dependent evaluation, and an accuracy of 97.01 % in patient-independent evaluation. On the Bonn database, the model achieved an overall accuracy of 99.31 %, a precision of 99.29 %, a sensitivity of 99.32 %, and an F1-score of 99.31 %.

title: A heuristic approach to HLCA-based feature extraction using a GRU model for Parkinson's disease detection
abstract: Parkinson Disease (PD) is heterogeneous in nature regarding motor and non-motor symptoms, and it is difficult to determine the severity and follow-up progression. The use of traditional clinical scales like UPDRS is subjective and resource-based, which is a necessity to have automated solutions. This study presents a novel HLCA-GRU model that integrates Heuristic Linear Component Analysis (HLCA) to reduce feature redundancy and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) to learn the temporal dynamics of speech and clinical characteristics in the Parkinson’s Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) dataset. The technique is compared to baseline models, such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and demonstrates better accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-scores. These findings suggest that the framework is utilized to provide credible early PD detection and progression classification, thereby advancing the development of useful clinical decision support systems. The novelty of this study lies in integrating heuristic feature optimisation with temporal sequence learning through the HLCA-GRU framework. This approach effectively minimizes feature redundancy while capturing longitudinal patterns, offering improved robustness and interpretability for early Parkinson’s disease detection and progression analysis.

title: TransformEEG: Towards improving model generalizability in deep learning-based EEG Parkinson’s disease detection
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is establishing itself as an important, low-cost, noninvasive diagnostic tool for the early detection of Parkinson’s Disease (PD). In this context, EEG-based Deep Learning (DL) models have shown promising results due to their ability to discover highly nonlinear patterns within the signal. However, current state-of-the-art DL models suffer from poor generalizability caused by high inter-subject variability. This high variability underscores the need for enhancing model generalizability by developing new architectures better tailored to EEG data. This paper introduces TransformEEG, a hybrid Convolutional-Transformer designed for Parkinson’s disease detection using EEG data. Unlike transformer models based on the EEGNet structure, TransformEEG incorporates a depthwise convolutional tokenizer. This tokenizer is specialized in generating tokens composed by channel-specific features, which enables more effective feature mixing within the self-attention layers of the transformer encoder. To evaluate the proposed model, four public datasets comprising 290 subjects (140 PD patients, 150 healthy controls) were harmonized and aggregated. A 10-outer, 10-inner Nested-Leave-N-Subjects-Out (N-LNSO) cross-validation was performed to provide an unbiased comparison against seven other consolidated EEG deep learning models. TransformEEG achieved the highest balanced accuracy’s median (78.45 %) as well as the lowest interquartile range (6.37 %) across all the N-LNSO partitions. When combined with data augmentation and threshold correction, median accuracy increased to 80.10 %, with an interquartile range of 5.74 %. In conclusion, TransformEEG produces more consistent and less skewed results. It demonstrates a substantial reduction in variability and more reliable PD detection using EEG data compared to the other investigated models. • This work presents TransformEEG, a novel hybrid convolutional-transformer model. • TransformEEG reduces performance variability in Parkinson’s Disease detection. • TransformEEG was evaluated on four public datasets comprising 290 subjects. • Data augmentation further enhance TransformEEG performance. • Classification threshold correction further enhance TransformEEG performance.

title: Feature semantic alignment network for rotating machinery domain generalization fault diagnosis with limited labeled samples
abstract: Existing research indicates that domain generalization-based fault diagnosis methods can effectively identify mechanical faults under unseen working conditions. Nevertheless, a notable constraint lies in its requirement for multiple source domains, each furnished with sufficient fault labels. In real-world applications, annotating industrial data is a time-consuming and expertise-intensive task that demands the involvement of specialists with domain-specific knowledge, presenting a significant challenge to mechanical fault diagnosis. To address this issue, this paper introduces an innovative semi-supervised domain generalization framework, named feature semantic alignment network (FSANet), for rotating machinery intelligent fault diagnosis under unseen target working conditions. Firstly, the FSANet constructs a feature consistency module to build the class-aware prototypes and subsequently align the posterior probabilities of fault feature with the pseudo-labels, facilitating the generation of more accurate pseudo-labels. Secondly, a semantic alignment module is established to guide the aggregation of samples within the same class based on the feature similarity with the class-aware prototypes, thereby improving the discriminability of fault features. Lastly, consistency regularization is adopted within the data augmentation to improve the confidence level of pseudo-labels and the generalization capability of the fault diagnosis model. Extensive generalization experiments on two datasets validate the superiority of the proposed method over existing state-of-the-art semi-supervised domain generalization methods.

title: ResKANNet: A residual Kolmogorov-Arnold network with multi-scale attention for brain tumor segmentation
abstract: Despite remarkable progress in brain tumor segmentation using deep learning, existing methods still struggle with the pronounced heterogeneity of tumor regions, particularly along irregular boundaries and within clinically critical enhancing subregions. Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs) provide adaptive activation functions for modeling complex data distributions; however, previous KAN-based approaches either underexploit their representational capacity through uniform deployment (U-KAN) or remain constrained to 2D segmentation tasks (TransUKAN). To overcome these limitations, we propose ResKANNet, a novel architecture that strategically integrates KAN modules into a residual U-shaped framework. The proposed model introduces three key innovations: (1) selective KAN placement at the bottleneck and first decoder layer—where feature transformation is most effective—rather than exhaustive deployment; (2) the first systematic fusion of KANs with residual connections to ensure stable gradient propagation in deep 3D segmentation networks; and (3) hybrid multi-scale attention mechanisms—EMCAM for skip connections and CBAM3D for decoder outputs—to refine boundaries at the decoder stage. Extensive experiments on the BraTS2018 and BraTS2021 datasets demonstrate that ResKANNet consistently outperforms nine state-of-the-art methods. On BraTS2021, ResKANNet achieves 90.95 % Dice (outperforming U-Mamba by 0.83 %) and 2.71 mm HD95 (0.76 mm better), with notable enhancing-tumor gains of 79.95 % on BraTS2018 (4.17 % advance over U-Mamba). Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of strategic KAN positioning. Overall, ResKANNet establishes the first systematic framework for KAN-based 3D brain tumor segmentation, demonstrating that selective KAN deployment combined with residual integration and decoder-focused attention significantly enhances segmentation accuracy and boundary precision, offering direct clinical value for surgical planning, radiation therapy target delineation, and treatment response assessment.

title: Timeseries transcriptomic profiling workflow of patients-derived colorectal cancer organoids enabling clustering, interpolation, and extrapolation
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a leading cause of cancer mortality, and understanding its temporal gene-expression dynamics is essential for improving therapy. Patient-derived CRC organoids provide a biologically relevant model that captures the disease’s architecture and genomics, yet their longitudinal transcriptomic profiles remain understudied. This study presents an integrated workflow for analyzing short time-series gene expression in CRC organoids. It combines Short Time-series Expression Miner (STEM) for clustering, Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) for uncertainty-aware interpolation, and autoregressive time-series modeling (ARIMA) for short-term forecasting. Applied to bulk RNA-seq data from CRC organoids, the workflow reduced noise, revealed biologically coherent gene clusters, and generated predictive trajectories extending two days beyond the sampling window. This standardized pipeline demonstrates how sparse transcriptomic measurements can be transformed into robust, uncertainty-aware predictions. The results bridge critical experimental gaps, enhance confidence in temporal sampling strategies, and lay a quantitative foundation for downstream therapeutic and mechanistic studies in preclinical oncology.

title: IFMXCN: Intellectual flow map-based explainable deep learning model for Alzheimer's disease detection using multimodal input
abstract: Alzheimer’s Disease is an irreversible progressive disorder affecting the cognitive functioning of memory and the respiratory system. The traditional Alzheimer’s Disease Detection frameworks often struggle to obtain optimal detection performance due to challenges, including the incorporation of diverse features, reduced explainability issues, computational complexity, and the requirement for a robust detection method. To overcome such intricacies, the research proposes an effective Intellectual Leading defense Optimized Flow map-based Mixed attentional Explainable Convolutional Neural Network (IFMXCN) model to perform disease detection by analyzing the multimodal inputs. The Mixed Attention enables the model to consider only the prominent features with no heavy parameter overhead issues. Image enhancement via the preprocessing of both the genetic data and the Magnetic Resonance Images enhances the detection process reliability through implicit handling of the inconsistent data and extracting the specific region using the Intellectual Leading defense Optimized-Fuzzy C-Means Clustering (ILDO-FCM) technique. Moreover, the incorporation of the gradient and eigen class activation mappings increase the model explainability in the disease detection process. Additionally, the model's hyperparameters tuning enables better identification of the subtle patterns. The results validate the superiority of the model by attaining an accuracy of 98.26 %, precision of 98.85 %, F1-score of 98.26 %, recall of 97.68 %, Macro F1-Score of 98.06 %, Micro F1-Score of 98.26 %, Weighted F1-Score of 98.65 %, for 90 % training using the ADNI dataset.

title: Cross-modal invariant learning with latent diffusion for reliable medical diagnosis under dynamic shifts
abstract: Robust and reliable medical diagnosis using artificial intelligence is crucial, yet real-world clinical environments present significant challenges due to dynamic covariate shifts affecting multi-modal data (images, text, tabular). Existing methods, including the single-modal robust classifier LaDiNE, often fail under these complex, multi-modal shifts, lacking mechanisms for cross-modal invariance, dynamic modality fusion, and fine-grained uncertainty attribution. To address this gap, we propose DyMoLaDiNE (Dynamic Multi-Modal Latent Diffusion Nested-Ensembles), a framework designed for reliable medical diagnosis under dynamic multi-modal covariate shifts. DyMoLaDiNE introduces four key innovations: (1) a Cross-Modal Invariant Feature Extractor leveraging multi-modal Vision Transformers and contrastive learning to derive robust latent representations, (2) a Dynamic Modality Weighting Mechanism that adaptively adjusts modality contributions based on instance-specific reliability scores, (3) a Robust Multi-Modal Diffusion Ensemble utilizing conditional diffusion models conditioned on multi-modal inputs and reliability scores for flexible, calibrated density estimation, and (4) Modality-Attributed Uncertainty Quantification to decompose predictive uncertainty by input source. Extensive evaluations on diverse datasets (MedMD&RadMD, MultiCaRe, PadChest, TCIA RE-MIND, BRaTS, Camelyon16, PANDA) demonstrate that DyMoLaDiNE significantly outperforms (p 0.005) state-of-the-art methods (LDM, CMCL, CGMCL, CIIM, DTTL, FFL, ALDM, LaDiNE) in terms of classification accuracy, robustness under dynamic perturbations, confidence calibration (ECE), and precise uncertainty quantification (CPIW, CNPV), while providing superior modality attribution fidelity. Ablation studies confirm the necessity of each component. DyMoLaDiNE represents a significant advancement in trustworthy, robust multi-modal medical AI. Code supporting this study DyMoLaDiNE .

title: An adaptive fault diagnosis framework with limited fault data for nonstationary processes
abstract: Conventional fault diagnosis methods typically require large-scale training data covering all possible operating conditions and complete fault data to establish an excellent fault classification model. In practice, it is intractable to collect various fault data in practical industrial systems and unknown faults may occur in the future. Besides, the data are generally nonstationary owing to varying demand, disturbances, etc. Against this background, this paper converts the fault diagnosis task into fault detection and fault location, using only limited fault data for online applications. For the fault detection phase, the proposed adaptive cointegration with hybrid feature extraction (ACHFE) method adaptively characterizes the long-term equilibrium relationships via adaptive cointegration analysis and extracts key features to efficiently distinguish actual faults from normal variations. The remaining features are further extracted by recursive principal component analysis and recursive slow feature analysis. The appropriate decomposition of the variables is beneficial in narrowing the scope of the fault variables. For the fault location phase, the multiscale partial symbolic transfer entropy method integrated with an attention mechanism is designed, which enables the identification of the fault root variables rapidly using only limited post-fault data. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is illustrated through a numerical case study and a practical industrial system.

title: Dual perspectives with consistency training on predicting drug–drug interactions
abstract: Predicting drug–drug interactions (DDIs) is essential for pharmaceutical research, aiding in the prevention of adverse effects from drug combinations. Our study introduces a novel Dual Perspectives with Consistency Training (DP-CT) method that harnesses both graph structures and SMILES sequences for deep learning-based DDI prediction. Unlike previous methods that focus on a single representation, our DP-CT approach leverages the strengths of both, enhancing predictive accuracy. We employ a Transformer for SMILES encoding and a graph neural network for graph representation, integrating them with point-wise and pair-wise consistency regularizations to ensure alignment and robustness of the encoded drug features. Our method has been tested on the DrugBank and TWOSIDES datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy, particularly in inductive settings, where we observed an approximate 8-point increase over existing methods.

title: Smart CSWin-UNet: Integrating prototype attention gate and mixture-of-experts skip connections for medical image segmentation
abstract: U-shaped architectures have become a cornerstone in medical image segmentation, owing to their robust feature-extraction pipelines and skip-connection schemes. Feature extraction typically relies on either convolutional neural networks (CNNs) or Transformer backbones. While CNNs benefit from strong inductive biases, their inherently local receptive fields hinder effective modeling of global, long-range semantic dependencies, especially in complex segmentation scenarios. Conversely, standard Transformers excel at capturing such global context but suffer from quadratic computational demands with increasing image resolution. Traditional skip connection strategies assume strictly exclusive correspondences between encoder and decoder stages and overlook the semantic gap between encoder and decoder features, which leads to semantic misalignment and degrades the segmentation of fine pathological structures. To overcome these limitations, we propose Smart CSWin-UNet, a hybrid framework that integrates the CSWin Transformer—leveraging cross-shaped window self-attention for efficient global context modeling—as its backbone. We augment this with two novel modules: the Mixture-of-Experts Skip Connections (MoSC), which dynamically route features via learned expert subnetworks, and the Prototype Attention Gate (PAG), a decoder-guided mechanism that adaptively aligns and fuses encoder–decoder features. Extensive experiments on multiple public datasets demonstrate that Smart CSWin-UNet achieves superior accuracy with reduced parameter counts.

title: MTCL: Multi-task consistency learning for semi-supervised 3D medical image segmentation
abstract: With the increasing use of semi-supervised learning in 3D medical image segmentation, this approach shows great potential in addressing the challenge of scarce labeled data. Effectively integrating multi-task learning to optimize the use of unlabeled data has therefore become a key issue. To address this, this paper proposes a Multi-task Consistency Learning (MTCL) framework, which achieves efficient learning and utilization of unlabeled data through a tripartite encoder–decoder architecture and a skillfully designed multi-task consistency learning strategy. The framework not only improves model performance on a single task but, more importantly, significantly enhances prediction accuracy on unlabeled data by establishing consistency constraints among image segmentation, signed distance map (SDM) generation, and image reconstruction tasks. Experimental results on publicly available 3D medical datasets including Left Atrium (LA), Pancreas-CT and PROMISE12 show that the proposed framework significantly outperforms existing mainstream methods. Notably, on the LA dataset with only 10 % labeled data, our method achieves the best performance across all four evaluation metrics, demonstrating its superior capability in capturing details and handling challenging regions.

title: EEG-based fusion approaches in multimodal emotion recognition: An in-depth review
abstract: Emotion recognition plays a central role in advancing HCI, healthcare, and affective computing. However, due to the rapid and dynamic nature of emotions, traditional unimodal approaches often fall short in capturing their complexity. As a result, multimodal emotion recognition has gained significant attention, with EEG emerging as a core modality due to its noninvasiveness, high temporal resolution, and direct neural activity. This paper presents a comprehensive review of EEG-based multimodal emotion recognition, focusing on sensors, fusion strategies, and benchmark datasets employed in state-of-the-art studies. Unlike previous surveys, this review makes three distinct contributions. First, it introduces a sensor-level categorisation that highlights device-specific constraints and opportunities for fusion design. Second, it systematically maps fusion strategies—including sensor-, feature-, and decision-level fusion—using structured comparisons that detail assumptions, data requirements, and computational costs. This methodological progression—from handcrafted pipelines to deep learning, hybrid, and transformer-based architectures—has also shaped multimodal emotion recognition approaches. Third, it provides an in-depth benchmarking of widely used EEG-based multimodal datasets, offering multidimensional comparisons across sample size, demographics, labelling schemes, stimulation protocols, and evaluation strategies. To contextualise these advances, a review of unimodal approaches is also provided. Together, these contributions establish a practical reference for designing robust EEG-based multimodal emotion recognition systems, selecting appropriate datasets, and ensuring consistency in comparative evaluations. The review also highlights key challenges and future opportunities, including dataset standardisation, cross-subject generalisation, and ethical considerations, to guide the next generation of research in this rapidly evolving field.

title: SeiFuD: A novel deep learning framework leveraging domain generalization for cross-subject seizure prediction
abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG)-based seizure prediction methods have the potential to significantly improve the quality of life for patients with epilepsy. However, due to substantial inter-individual variability in EEG patterns, most existing approaches rely on patient-specific models, which exhibit limited generalization performance when applied to unseen patients—especially under data-scarce scenarios. To overcome this limitation, we propose a domain generalization framework named SeiFuD (Seizure prediction via Feature Fusion and Disentanglement). Specifically, we first extract multi-scale time–frequency features from raw EEG signals and employ a spatio-temporal convolutional neural network to generate a robust and comprehensive fused representation. Subsequently, a feature disentanglement module decomposes the learned features into domain-invariant and domain-specific components. To enhance cross-patient generalization, we incorporate adversarial training to suppress patient-specific information within the domain-invariant features, thereby capturing seizure-related patterns that are transferable across individuals. The proposed method was evaluated on the CHB-MIT dataset and the TUSZ dataset, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 60.26 %, a sensitivity of 42.88 %, and a false positive rate (FPR) of 0.42/h on the CHB-MIT dataset, and an AUC of 63.76 %, a sensitivity of 47.44 %, and an FPR of 0.493/h on the TUSZ dataset. Moreover, interpretability analysis demonstrates that the model successfully identifies clinically relevant features associated with seizure onset. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of our approach in reducing interpatient variability and improving generalization performance, offering a promising solution for practical and scalable seizure prediction systems.

title: Metapath-based feature aggregated heterogeneous graph neural network for adverse drug reactions prediction
abstract: Abstract Backgrount: Predicting adverse drug reactions (ADRs) is crucial for drug development, discovery, and design. Although traditional pharmacological experiments can accurately detect the ADRs and have high reliability, the process is costly in terms of time and monetary. With the development and rise of computational methods, graph neural network (GNN)-based ADR prediction methods have gained attention recently since they effectively save research and development costs. Nevertheless, the performance of existing methods is often limited by the size and variety of data they can effectively handle. Furthermore, existing GNN-based methods cannot fully and accurately capture the complex structures and rich semantics of drugs and ADRs in bio-heterogeneous graphs. Result: In this paper, a novel more effective GNN framework named metapath-based feature aggregated heterogeneous graph neural network model (MFAHGN) is proposed for ADRs prediction to achieve more effective and accurate results. In MFAHGN, a drugs-ADRs heterogeneous graph is constructed by integrating multiple well-known biological databases. Then a high-quality feature learning method of drugs and ADRs is designed by using a delicately customized short metapath strategy to capture the complete semantic information of all metapaths, which avoids information decay along the long metapath and fully considers the mutual influence between various metapaths. Conclusions: Extensive experiments are conducted on two biological heterogeneous datasets across six metrics to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model. Medical literature validation confirms 80% of top predictions, including eight novel drug-ADR associations. The code is available at https://github.com/FJH886/MFAHGN.

title: DUFGNet: A dual-stream U-Net framework with frequency-guided channel attention and graph integration for epileptic seizure prediction
abstract: Effective prediction of seizures is essential for alleviating patient suffering and facilitating timely medical intervention. However, achieving reliable prediction remains challenging due to patient-specific variability and the complex evolution of epileptic EEG signals across spatial, temporal, and spectral domains. To address these challenges, we propose DUFGNet, a dual-stream self-supervised framework designed to model comprehensive spatio-temporal representations under conditions of limited labeled data. Specifically, a dual-stream U-Net is employed to extract features from two distinct perspectives: global interchannel dependencies and local intrachannel structures. Additionally, we develop a global–local feature integration module based on graph attention. It is coupled with a frequency-guided channel attention module. Together, these modules adaptively fuse multi-scale features across spatial, temporal, and spectral domains. Furthermore, we introduce a multi-task self-supervised learning strategy that incorporates two domain-specific pretext tasks. Extensive experiments on the public CHB-MIT dataset and a private Renji dataset demonstrate that DUFGNet achieves high performance, with accuracies of 97.11 % and 94.11 %, and AUC scores of 0.9955 and 0.9736, respectively. DUFGNet outperforms state-of-the-art supervised and self-supervised baselines using only 0.28 M parameters. Notably, even with just 1 % labeled data under extremely low-label conditions, it maintains over 85 % accuracy, demonstrating strong robustness. These results suggest that DUFGNet offers an accurate, lightweight, and label-efficient solution for seizure prediction, with significant potential for deployment in resource-constrained clinical or wearable settings.

title: WPANet: A physically consistent and interpretable framework for fault diagnosis via wavelet prior-guided algorithm unrolling
abstract: Accurate and interpretable fault diagnosis under time-varying conditions remains a major challenge for rotating machinery. To address this, we propose WPANet, a physically consistent and interpretable framework that integrates wavelet priors with algorithm unrolling. A multi-level discrete wavelet receptive expansion module is designed to enhance signal reconstruction by capturing fault-related impulse features with reduced computational cost. To improve temporal sensitivity and interpretability for time-varying scenarios, we unroll a time-enhanced iterative soft thresholding algorithm (TeISTA) as a dictionary learning solver, guided by wavelet-informed priors. Additionally, a gradient-sensitive convolutional regularization strategy is introduced to stabilize learning and align key kernels with physical characteristics. Experimental results on rotating machinery datasets show that WPANet achieves high diagnostic accuracy, robustness, and both intrinsic and post-hoc interpretability. This work offers a transparent and effective solution for intelligent fault diagnosis in non-stationary environments.

title: Quaternion-based inter-channel correlation learning for fine-grained medical image segmentation
abstract: Color medical image segmentation plays a pivotal role in various clinical procedures, such as image-guided surgery and endoscopic examination. Despite the progress of deep learning in this field, prevailing methods often handle RGB channels either in isolation or through naive fusion strategies, which inadequately capture the inter-channel correlations. Such limitations hinder the accurate identification of fine-grained color variations that are crucial for delineating subtle tissue or lesion differences. To overcome these challenges, we present MCTNet, an innovative segmentation framework specifically designed to exploit the chromatic complexity inherent in medical images. A core contribution of MCTNet is the Color Palette Structure (CPS) module, which adaptively adjusts inter-channel dependencies and enriches semantic color representation by independently applying linear transformations to the different components of quaternion representations. Additionally, we design a Cross-representational Spatial Attention (CRSA) module, which employs the attention weights extracted from shallow texture features and color features represented by quaternion to achieve the goal of effectively retaining fine-grained semantic information from shallow features during contextual feature fusion. We evaluate MCTNet on five public color medical image segmentation benchmarks: 2018 Data Science Bowl (cell nuclei), CVC-ClinicDB (polyps), ISIC 2018 (skin lesions), GlaS (glands), and DRIVE (retinal vessels). MCTNet achieves top mDice scores of 0.9288, 0.9518, 0.9001, 0.9073, and 0.8301, respectively, outperforming state-of-the-art models and demonstrating strong generalization across diverse segmentation tasks. Our code will be available at https://github.com/Chasingbetter/MCTNet.

title: A survey on multimodal risk classifier for chest diseases based on model optimization techniques
abstract: This review examines bioimpedance analysis methods and their applications in medical decision support systems, emphasizing noninvasive diagnostics across diverse clinical scenarios. Two main paradigms for forming descriptors in bioimpedance-based medical risk classifiers are discussed: model-based bioimpedance analysis and spectral bioimpedancemetry. The structures of classifiers utilizing these descriptors, including hierarchical architectures and hybrid neural networks, are analyzed for improved classification accuracy. Recent research demonstrates opportunities to enhance computer-aided diagnostic techniques for socially significant diseases and develop novel methods for oncological and functional state monitoring. Impedance mapping using a pair of electrode leads emerges as a robust method for tissue characterization and real-time functional assessment. Minimally invasive and catheter-based measurements enable precise evaluation of breast, lung, and cardiovascular tissues, offering superior spatial and temporal resolution compared with conventional approaches. Integration of bioimpedance descriptors with artificial intelligence allows real-time analysis, dynamic monitoring, and adaptive diagnostics. Challenges such as electrode-skin contact variability, model uncertainty, and weak signal detection in suboptimal scenarios are highlighted, emphasizing the need for continued research to improve robustness, resolution, and clinical utility. Overall, bioimpedance methods show substantial potential to advance medical decision support systems, improve differential diagnosis, reduce unnecessary invasive procedures, and guide future innovations in noninvasive and minimally invasive diagnostics.

title: Decoding natural images from EEG signals using a learnable multi-band spatio-temporal encoder
abstract: Decoding natural images from neural signals has long been a research goal. While recent advances in contrastive learning and generative models have improved visual decoding based on fMRI, fMRI’s high cost and low temporal resolution limit its practicality, driving interest in EEG-based approaches. In this study, we propose MB-ST, a novel EEG encoder that integrates a Frequency-Bands Decomposition Module for frequency-domain feature extraction and a Spatial-Temporal Feature Extraction Block for spatio-temporal feature learning. MB-ST employs multi-band learnable filters and multi-scale convolutional kernels to efficiently capture the complex structure of EEG signals. Extensive experiments on the THINGS-EEG dataset demonstrate state-of-the-art zero-shot visual decoding performance. We further validate the model’s real-time processing capability and cross-modal generalization on MEG data.Comprehensive interpretability analyses confirm both the model transparency and the biological relevance of the learned features.

title: FDDGNet: An information bottleneck-inspired feature disentanglement network for cross-subject EEG-based emotion recognition
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based emotion recognition has attracted increasing interest due to its non-invasive and objective nature in measuring brain activity. However, inter-subject variability in EEG signals remains a major challenge to developing generalizable emotion recognition models. In this paper, we propose a feature disentanglement domain generalization network (FDDGNet) to tackle the cross-subject emotion recognition problem by explicitly separating emotion-relevant features from subject-specific representations. Specifically, we first employ a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-based encoder to extract the latent features from the raw EEG signals. Subsequently, an orthogonal complementary project is introduced to decouple the latent features into orthogonal subspaces: emotion-relevant and subject-specific feature space, thereby enhancing the model’s capacity for emotion representation learning. Inspired by the concept of sufficiency in information theory, we propose a sufficient information bottleneck module that ensures the subject-specific feature space captures sufficient domain information while suppressing emotional leakage, thereby promoting clearer feature separation. Finally, the emotion-relevant and subject-specific features are concatenated and fed into a LSTM-based decoder to reconstruct the raw EEG signals, which helps preserve information integrity during feature extraction and disentanglement. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed FDDGNet, cross-subject and cross-dataset experiments are conducted on two public EEG-based emotion recognition datasets, AMIGOS and DREAMER. Experimental results demonstrate that FDDGNet outperforms several state-of-the-art methods and exhibits promising generalization performance on unseen domains, highlighting its potential for robust and practical emotion recognition applications. The code is available at https://github.com/yyk90/FDDGNet.

title: Constructing a clinical knowledge graph from electronic health records for enhanced decision-making and disease diagnosis
abstract: The increasing complexity of clinical data presents both challenges and opportunities for modern healthcare. This study proposes a robust framework for building a Clinical Knowledge Graph (KG) by leveraging unstructured Electronic Health Records (EHRs) and clinical notes. Using state-of-the-art natural language processing tools such as MetaMap and the Unified Medical Language System (UMLS), the proposed system structures heterogeneous medical data into a unified format. By analyzing demographic, symptomatic, and laboratory data, this framework enables enhanced decision-making and insights into disease correlations. Demonstrated using the MIMIC-III database, the system achieves high granularity, providing actionable intelligence for personalized recommendations and supporting predictive diagnostic models.

title: Multiple EEG channel attention based multi-task model for epileptiform activity quantification
abstract: Epileptiform activity is critical in characterizing electroencephalogram (EEG) on electrical status epilepticus during sleep (ESES). Spike-wave index (SWI) is a quantitative measure used to characterize the intensity of epileptiform activity, and it is helpful for the clinical diagnosis of ESES encephalopathy. The core of SWI calculation lies in two tasks: sleep stage determination and epileptiform activity segmentation. The current research usually focuses only on single task while the inner-connection between the two tasks is not well exploited. To address this issue, a multi-task learning method with an EEG channel attention module for epileptiform activity quantification analysis (MCAQN) is developed in this paper. It consists of a task-sharing network and two task-specific attention networks. The task-sharing network is responsible for learning the global features of EEG. And two task-specific attention networks separately focus on the task-specific information extracted from the global features by EEG channel attention module (ECA), with one dedicated to sleep staging and SWI quantification. To balance the importance of multi-tasking, a novel loss function is designed that combines semantic segmentation based SWI quantization loss and sleep stage classification loss. This multi-task learning approach allows each module to capture task-specific information while simultaneously leveraging the inherent correlations among related tasks, thereby substantially improving the overall performance. Experiments were conducted on the long-term EEG data from the Children’s Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine (CHZU) dataset. The proposed MCAQN has demonstrated obvious advantages over single-task methods and some state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. Specifically, it can quantify SWI accurately without relying on thresholds and expert experience, and the SWI error (SWIerror) is as low as 2.406 %.

title: Beyond convolution: A morphology-guided quantum-inspired attention UNet for medical image segmentation
abstract: Medical image segmentation is a core component of computer-aided diagnosis systems, but it still faces significant challenges due to diverse lesion morphologies, low contrast, and substantial noise interference. To overcome the limitations of traditional convolution and self-attention mechanisms in capturing global dependencies and modeling complex structures, this study proposes a Morphology-Guided Quantum-Inspired Attention UNet (MQAUNet). For the first time, the principles of quantum superposition and quantum entanglement are introduced into medical image segmentation. Through learnable quantum-inspired feature representations, MQAUNet enables dynamic interactions across spatial and channel dimensions, effectively enhancing the model’s adaptive modeling capability for complex lesion morphologies. MQAUNet consists of four key modules: Quasi-Quantum Dynamic Convolution (Q-QDConv), Quantum Tensor Entanglement Attention (Q-TEA), Adaptive Morphological Module (AMM), and Quantum Residual Connection (QRConnection). These modules collaboratively achieve global consistency and boundary continuity across multiple scales. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that MQAUNet achieves optimal or suboptimal performance on multiple medical image segmentation benchmark datasets, exhibiting superior robustness and generalization in low-contrast and high-noise scenarios. This study provides a novel and feasible solution for the deep integration of quantum-inspired computation and medical image intelligence, laying an important theoretical and methodological foundation for building high-precision, low-computational-complexity, and interpretable clinical segmentation models.

title: Gene-guided multimodal data fusion for cancer patient survival analysis
abstract: Cancer ranks among the leading causes of disease-related human mortality worldwide. Accurate prediction of cancer patients’ survival periods holds significant importance for formulating personalized treatment strategies. In recent years, rapid advancements in medical imaging have enabled whole-slide images (WSIs) and genomic data to provide abundant information for cancer survival analysis. However, effectively fusing multi-modal data to extract complementary insights remains a challenging task in existing research. To alleviate this problem, we propose a genome-guided multi-modal feature fusion (GGMF) approach for survival analysis. By leveraging a self-attention mechanism to identify key genes, GGMF emphasizes the genome’s dominant role in prediction. This process enhances the feature representation of WSIs by guiding the secondary encoding of the images with relevant genomic information. Additionally, a residual-based cross-modal interaction module is introduced to preserve both fused feature information and unimodal-specific information, improving model effectiveness. Experimental results demonstrate that GGMF outperforms multiple baseline methods on three real-world datasets, validating its effectiveness and rationality in cancer survival prediction. Our codes are made available at https://github.com/SpringIsRedSum/GGMF.

title: Modality reprogramming: Adapting frozen LLMs for multi-channel EEG classification
abstract: Emotion recognition from electroencephalogram (EEG) signals is inherently challenging due to their high dimensionality, non-stationarity, and susceptibility to noise. These characteristics, combined with limited labeled data and high inter-subject variability, hinder generalization across subjects. In this work, we investigate the use of pre-trained large language models (LLMs) originally developed for natural language processing as cross-modal learners for EEG-based emotion recognition. We propose a reprogramming-based framework that transforms EEG signals into patch embeddings, which are mapped into the token embedding space of frozen LLMs via lightweight reprogramming layers. The backbones remain unchanged during training, enabling efficient adaptation without full fine-tuning, and we evaluate our approach using several language models. Analysis conducted on both virtual (VREEG03, VREEG04) and non-virtual (SEED) EEG datasets across two-class, three-class, and four-class classification settings demonstrates the effectiveness, flexibility, and generalization ability of the proposed approach. Notably, these language models achieve higher performance in virtual environments, highlighting their effectiveness in capturing the enhanced emotional signals evoked by immersive environments.

title: A lightweight semantic decoding network with group to individual transfer learning for EEG-based visual recognition
abstract: Decoding visual semantic features from electroencephalograph (EEG) signals is crucial for cognitive neuroscience and brain–computer interfaces (BCI). However, this task remains challenging due to the tension between group-level commonality and individual-specific variability in neural responses: existing deep learning models capture generic patterns from large-scale data but fail to adapt to individual differences, while their excessive complexity hinders deployment in resource-constrained environments. Additionally, pronounced inter-subject variability and data acquisition difficulties aggravate data scarcity and limit generalization. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a lightweight Multi-scale Spatial Pyramid and Temporal U-shaped (MSPTU) network for efficient EEG semantic feature extraction. Furthermore, a new Group-to-Individual Transfer Learning (G2I-TL) framework is introduced that leverages general group cognitive concepts to obtain individual-specific decoding models. Our method significantly reduces the number of parameters while improving accuracy, circumvents the inter-individual variability issue, and effectively mitigates data scarcity. Experiments on two public datasets (OCED and EEG200) demonstrate state-of-the-art(SOTA) performance; for example, on the OCED dataset, compared with the previous SOTA method, MSPTU-TL improves accuracy by 1.67 % on the 6-class task and by 7.06 % on the 72-exemplar task. Using the proposed masked channel attention method, even with only 20 % of channels remaining, the accuracy still reaches 56.03 % for the 6-Category task and 35.76 % for the 72-Exemplar task, surpassing previous methods. This work provides a scalable solution for EEG-based visual recognition with practical BCI applications.

title: Zero-shot compound fault diagnosis with semantic graph embedding and multi-stage fusion
abstract: Zero-shot compound fault diagnosis in industrial systems is highly challenging due to the scarcity of labeled fault data and the weak generalization ability of existing models. Conventional approaches typically rely on shallow feature fusion and manually defined semantic priors, which fail to capture the intricate relationships among compound fault types. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a semantic graph embedding and multi-stage fusion framework that jointly enhances fault semantics and multimodal feature integration. A structure-enhanced semantic embedding module leverages graph convolutional networks to construct a fault relation graph, generating discriminative and physically consistent semantic representations. A multi-stage fusion network based on Transformers is further developed to hierarchically integrate vibration, current, and other sensor signals across multiple levels, achieving deep cross-modal alignment between perceptual and semantic spaces. Extensive experiments on two public benchmarks, HDU-BFDS and Paderborn, under four zero-shot diagnostic tasks demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms both classical and state-of-the-art baselines. On the most challenging task, it achieves 57.69 % accuracy, yielding an absolute improvement of 10.6 % while maintaining strong robustness under various noise conditions. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of semantic graph construction and hierarchical fusion mechanisms. Overall, the proposed approach provides an interpretable, robust, and scalable solution for zero-shot compound fault diagnosis, offering new insights into industrial fault understanding and generalizable intelligent monitoring.

title: Generalizable AI-driven cross-domain breast cancer diagnosis based on mammograms by solving Fourier transformation-based jigsaw puzzles
abstract: The performance of deep learning models for the early diagnosis of breast cancer based on mammograms often degrades when domain shifts occur. Although certain domain generalization methods can produce images with new styles for alleviating domain shifts, each produced image exhibits a single style. The present study introduces a Fourier transformation-based jigsaw puzzle (F-Jip) method which incorporates a jigsaw puzzle generation (JPG) module, a new style generation (NSG) module, and an enhanced jigsaw puzzle generation (EJPG) process to produce the enhanced jigsaw puzzles with multi-domain information. The enhanced jigsaw puzzles can guide the model to learn domain-invariant features to alleviate the influence of domain shifts for cross-domain breast cancer diagnosis. A leave-one-domain-out cross validation using six datasets which can simulate varying domain shifts encountered in clinical scenarios is used to evaluate the performance of the models. In each fold, the AUC and accuracy of the proposed model are higher than those of several state-of-the-art domain generalization models. Additionally, when compared to BI-RADS assessments of the radiologists in one dataset, the proposed model exhibits better performance for discriminating between the benign and malignant lesions, and further identifies 81.3 % patients with benign lesions in the subgroup analysis of patients with BI-RADS 4 lesions to avoid unnecessary biopsies. The experimental results indicate that the proposed model has the potentials for assisting doctors in diagnosing breast cancer.

title: Confidence-aware dual-consistency and pixel-sampled dual-contrastive learning for semi-supervised biomedical image segmentation
abstract: Biomedical image segmentation is crucial in computer-aided diagnosis, allowing for precise delineation of anatomical structures and pathological regions. However, supervised learning relies heavily on large annotated datasets, limiting its application in biomedical image segmentation. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) mitigates this limitation by leveraging both labeled and unlabeled data. Among various SSL strategies, consistency learning is the most commonly used SSL method that encourages consistent predictions under perturbations. Nevertheless, these methods often suffer from issues such as weak consistency under dual-perturbation (weak-to-strong) and poor fine-grained boundary preservation. In this paper, we propose a novel SSL consistency learning framework, CAP-CL, with a confidence-aware dual-consistency constraint and pixel-sampled contrastive learning technique for improved and robust biomedical image segmentation to address these challenges. We first introduce Adaptive Fusion Perturbation (AFP) through adaptive adjustment during training to generate high-quality weakly and strongly augmented images. Then, we propose a transcription consistency loss and a novel ensemble pseudo-labeling method to ensure intra-network and inter-network consistency under dual-perturbation, respectively. Furthermore, CAP-CL actively samples both challenging and generic negative pixel features for contrastive learning to capture fine-grained details. Moreover, Dual-confident Area Cross-Entropy (DAC) loss is proposed to maintain the robustness against pseudo-labeling mistakes and optimize training convergence. DAC loss also introduces network perturbation to reduce confirmation bias. CAP-CL is comprehensively evaluated on four publicly available segmentation datasets of three imaging modalities. It consistently outperforms competing state-of-the-art models. The source code is openly accessible at https://github.com/withNamer/CAP-CL.git.

title: Evidential learning driven breast tumor segmentation with stage-divided vision-language interaction
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most common causes of death among women worldwide, with millions of fatalities annually. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) can provide various sequences for characterizing tumor morphology and internal patterns, and becomes an effective tool for detection and diagnosis of breast tumors. However, previous deep-learning based tumor segmentation methods have limitations in accurately locating tumor contours due to the challenge of low contrast between cancer and normal areas and blurred boundaries. Leveraging text prompt information holds promise in ameliorating tumor segmentation effect by delineating segmentation regions. Inspired by this, we propose text-guided Breast Tumor Segmentation model (TextBCS) with stage-divided vision-language interaction and evidential learning. Specifically, the proposed stage-divided vision-language interaction facilitates information mutual between visual and text features at each stage of down-sampling, further exerting the advantages of text prompts to assist in locating lesion areas in low contrast scenarios. Moreover, the evidential learning is adopted to quantify the segmentation uncertainty of the model for blurred boundary. It utilizes the variational Dirichlet to characterize the distribution of the segmentation probabilities, addressing the segmentation uncertainties of the boundaries. Extensive experiments validate the superiority of our TextBCS over other segmentation networks, showcasing the best breast tumor segmentation performance on publicly available datasets.

title: Evaluating large language models for real-world perioperative clinical consultation
abstract: The rise of medical large language models (LLMs) has highlighted the need for effective evaluation in real-world clinical scenarios. However, current assessment methods, such as medical examinations and question answering, are inadequate for fully evaluating medical LLMs, particularly in perioperative clinical consultations, which involve complex, multiturn dialogs. In this paper, we propose an automated evaluation framework to assess the capabilities of LLMs in perioperative consultation, and we refer to the proposed framework as PCAEF (automated evaluation framework for perioperative consultation). Specifically, PCAEF consists of two main components. First, we develop a perioperative patient simulator using LLMs, which incorporates comprehensive contexts, emotional states, relevant topics, and normalized behaviors. This simulator generates test data that closely align with authentic clinical scenarios through interactions with the baseline LLMs. Second, we introduce a ranking-based evaluator designed to assess the performance of baseline models that utilize chain-of-thought (CoT) mechanisms. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of PCAEF. Additionally, by applying this framework, we establish a benchmark to evaluate commonly used LLMs for perioperative consultation.

title: STESNN: Spatio-temporal enhancement spiking neural networks for epilepsy detection
abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG), as an important tool for epilepsy detection, plays a crucial role in the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of epilepsy. The existing intelligent epilepsy detection methods struggle to accurately and comprehensively extract the spatio-temporal features of EEG signals, which limits their performance. In this paper, taking advantage of the powerful spatio-temporal information processing capabilities of spiking neural networks, we propose a spatio-temporal enhanced spiking neural network (STESNN) model and apply it to epilepsy detection. The STESNN model is a dual-path architecture composed of a spiking convolutional neural network and a feedforward spiking neural network, which can simultaneously extract the spatial and temporal features of EEG signals and effectively enhance the detection of epileptic activity in EEG signals. In epilepsy detection applications, the EEG data enhancement methods and the importance-based channel selection method are used to improve the model detection performance while reducing the computational cost. The experimental results on the CHB-MIT dataset show that the proposed STESNN model exhibits higher accuracy in the epilepsy detection task compared with traditional machine learning-based methods and deep learning models, providing strong technical support for early diagnosis of epilepsy. In addition, experiments on the large-scale TUSZ v1.5.2 clinical corpus further demonstrate that STESNN can generalize well to more heterogeneous EEG data.

title: FA-STTM: A hybrid Transformer-Mamba network for motor imagery EEG classification
abstract: The brain–computer interface (BCI) offers transformative solutions for individuals with neural impairments, with motor imagery electroencephalogram (MI-EEG) widely applied in various BCI applications. However, the limited performance and generalizability of MI-EEG decoding remain significant challenges. In this paper, we propose a frequency-based attention spatial-temporal Transformer-Mamba network, named FA-STTM. We first design a wavelet-based spatial attention and a group-wise channel attention to emphasize task-relevant oscillation band features. Next, we develop a Transformer-Mamba module to extract global dependencies and accelerate training. Finally, we replace traditional fully connected layers with Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks to enhance representational power. The experimental results demonstrate that, in subject-dependent evaluations, our method achieves state-of-the-art performance both with data augmentation (BCICIV-2a: 82.9 %, BCICIV-2b: 87.81 %) and without data augmentation (BCICIV-2a: 77.89 %, BCICIV-2b: 86 %). Furthermore, in the challenging subject-independent evaluations, FA-STTM also demonstrates outstanding decoding performance (BCICIV-2a: 61.13 %, BCICIV-2b: 77.04 %). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt to combine the Mamba and Transformer architectures in EEG decoding. The comparative studies demonstrate that the Transformer-Mamba design outperforms traditional Transformer architecture in terms of decoding accuracy, stability and training speed. Extensive qualitative and visualization experiments further highlight the superior performance and interpretability of our model.

title: Integrating channel priors and shared pattern learning for enhanced motor imagery EEG classification
abstract: Brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) represent an emerging paradigm for direct communication and control between the brain and external devices. Electroencephalography (EEG)-based motor imagery (MI) has become a cornerstone of non-invasive BCI applications, enabling individuals with motor impairments to interact with assistive technologies. Nevertheless, the decoding performance of current EEG-based MI systems remains suboptimal, mainly due to insufficient exploitation of spatial information and the lack of explicit modeling of shared temporal dynamics across intra-trial segments. This paper proposed a Channel Prior-Enhanced and Shared Network (CPESNet) for MI EEG classification. On the one hand, prior knowledge is utilized to select MI-related channels to supplement channel information. On the other hand, a structure with shared fully connected layers is designed to extract shared patterns across multiple windows within a single trial, making the model lightweight and efficient. Experimental results show that the CPESNet achieved classification accuracies of 85.88 % on BCI Competition dataset IV 2a and 92.96 % on the High-Gamma Dataset. Ablation studies validate the contribution of each core module, and visualization of shared-layer parameters reveals that the early MI phase exhibits the strongest discriminative neural signatures, highlighting its pivotal role in intent decoding. These findings offer actionable insights for the design of efficient, interpretable, and high-performance MI-BCI systems.

title: Pseudo-sample enhanced fault diagnosis method for unmanned underwater vehicles based on graph adversarial modeling and metric constraints
abstract: Thruster failures pose a threat to the navigation safety of unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs) in complex marine environments. However, due to the influence of test conditions and fault randomness, the inter-class imbalance leads to the difficulty in diagnosis. To address this issue, a pseudo-sample enhanced fault diagnosis method is proposed by introducing metric constraints into a graph adversarial model. Firstly, this method constructs a feature-consistent pseudo-sample generation model based on graph adversarial modeling and improves the modeling ability of the model for complex association features between samples by mining the potential topology in the data. Based on this, a joint optimization strategy combining adversarial loss and feature space metric loss is designed, which makes the generated pseudo-samples closer to the real data and improves the model robustness under imbalanced data. Experimental tests using the vibration data of real UUV thrusters, along with comparisons against multiple baseline models, are conducted. The results show that the proposed method achieves superior diagnostic performance and stability across different operating conditions.

title: A survey on feature selection techniques for biomedical data: Methods and applications
abstract: Feature selection is a crucial preprocessing step in biomedical data analysis, aiming to reduce dimensionality, mitigate overfitting, improve classification performance, and enhance interpretability. However, the complex nature of biomedical data, including high dimensionality, limited sample sizes, noise, redundancy, heterogeneity, and class imbalance, poses significant challenges to traditional feature selection methods. This survey provides a comprehensive and structured overview of feature selection methods in biomedical applications. We classify existing approaches into four major categories: filter, wrapper, embedded, and hybrid methods. Beyond these four, we also discuss granular computing frameworks as a complementary line of work for uncertainty-aware biomedical analysis. We further discuss evaluation criteria that extend beyond predictive accuracy to encompass clustering performance, stability, and robustness, which are essential for clinical translation. In addition, we summarize benchmark datasets and representative applications across genomics, medical imaging, and brain network analysis. Finally, we outline key challenges and promising future directions, including enhancing stability, integrating multimodal data, and developing interpretable feature selection frameworks tailored to clinical practice. This survey aims to serve as a comprehensive reference for researchers and practitioners advancing feature selection techniques in biomedical data analysis.

title: State of health prediction of lithium-ion battery degradation using adaptive gated dual attention unit neural Wiener process
abstract: The performance degradation of lithium-ion batteries is influenced by various uncertain factors; their capacity decay can be regarded as a two-stage stochastic process in which change points and temporary capacity recovery are observed. Although existing degradation models can capture the nonlinear characteristics of the process, they often overlook the impact of two-stage stochasticity, particularly the change points and short-term fluctuations. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a battery degradation framework that integrates change-point dynamics with the nonlinear modeling capability of neural networks and the Wiener stochastic process. An Adaptive Gated Dual Attention Unit (AGDAU)–neural Wiener model is introduced to enhance attention to historical hidden states, enabling effective responses to change points and short-term fluctuations in the two-stage degradation process. First, the Expectation–Maximization algorithm is employed to estimate the parameters of the stochastic process, accurately characterizing degradation across the full battery cycle. Next, a degradation model based on AGDAU is established, in which the drift coefficients are adaptively updated. Finally, the transition probability density function of the capacity degradation trajectory is derived to achieve state-of-health prediction. Through single-step and multi-step prediction experiments on two battery datasets, the proposed AGDAU-Wiener Process demonstrates superior performance compared to traditional Wiener processes and possesses the physical interpretability that neural network methods lack, providing an effective solution for state-of-health prediction of lithium-ion batteries.

title: Fault diagnosis for the gas-path system of an engine test bed based on multi-modal signals
abstract: The aerospace engine test bed, as a pivotal equipment for evaluating engine reliability, necessitates rigorous monitoring of its health state to ensure the safe operation of the engine. The multi-point, multi-modal sensor information in the test bed's gas-path system is characterized by complexity and variability. Traditional fault diagnosis methods often struggle with issues such as labor-intensive threshold setting, frequent false alarms, and missed detections. Inspired by the self-attention mechanism, a dynamic aware diagnosis network (DADN) is proposed based on multi-modal sensor fusion. Firstly, DADN employs shift-aware attention to focus on a small number of critical points (offset sampling) in the sensor signal so that the discriminative local temporal features are extracted. Secondly, dynamic pooling tricks are employed to score the channel-wise features over the duration and generate fixed-length abstract representations. Shift-aware attention and dynamic pooling constitute a temporal feature learning pipeline from “fine-grained localization” to “global dynamic pooling”. Finally, multi-point, multi-modal sensor signals are fed into the DADN to capture inter-sensor interactions and fault-related patterns, thereby achieving accurate fault identification in the gas-path system. Experimental results demonstrate that DADN exhibits superior diagnostic accuracy and robustness, highlighting its potential for advanced fault diagnosis in an engine test bed's gas-path system.

title: CDMI-NTDI: Cancer driver module identification via network topology and deep interaction features
abstract: Cancer driver module identification, i.e., the detection of functionally coherent gene sets based on protein-protein interaction networks, represents a critical bioinformatics challenge for elucidating cancer pathogenesis. Current methodological limitations stem from inherent network incompleteness and noise in protein-protein interaction network data, which arise from technological constraints in sequencing. To address this issue, recent approaches have incorporated gene–miRNA interaction networks to enhance relationship reliability. However, the intrinsic sparsity of gene–miRNA interaction networks creates substantial analytical barriers to extracting meaningful biological information. This study introduces a novel computational framework that employs autoencoder architecture to extract latent gene-gene associations from sparse gene-miRNA networks. Concurrently, we develop an innovative influence evaluation metric to quantitatively assess gene functional importance within the weighted protein–protein interaction network. Comparative experiments against three state-of-the-art methods demonstrate superior performance in most cases regarding the recognition of established cancer-related genes, the generation of modules with higher coverage and mutual exclusivity, and more significant cancer type-specific enrichment. Most genes in the identified modules are involved in cancer-related signaling pathways or previously validated as oncogenic in clinical literature. These findings validate our method’s capacity to uncover biologically relevant driver modules from noisy, incomplete network data.

title: A time-frequency interpretable framework for bearing fault diagnosis via global channel-region information interaction and weight-CAM
abstract: The structure integrating the advantages of convolutional local feature extraction and Transformer-based global feature analysis exhibits distinct strengths in bearing fault diagnosis. However, there is often noise interference in actual working conditions, and such structures typically require large-scale training datasets to maintain performance, which poses a significant limitation in fault diagnosis scenarios. Additionally, the decision principles of these structures cannot be explored, and interpretability remains insufficient. To address these challenges, an interpretable fault diagnosis framework is proposed, wherein channel-level and region-level feature information are jointly optimized. A variable bandwidth filter module is first designed for signal preprocessing, with spectral attention heat maps generated via filter channel weight mapping. Joint distributed self-attention is employed to perform interactive weighting across regional and channel dimensions, thereby reducing model parameters. A multi-head weighted link classification layer is developed for feature classification, with inherent interpretability embedded. Based on this, Weight-CAM method is designed to obtain accurate post-hoc activation maps without invoking original model computations. Experimental results show that the proposed model can maintain classification accuracy in the presence of noise, limited samples, and the need to cross speeds. Through the incorporation of variable bandwidth filtering and weighted link layers, spectral heat maps and post-hoc activation maps are utilized to cross-locate model focus in both time and frequency domains, validating the interpretability of the framework.

title: EEGDiffuser: Label-guided EEG signals synthesis via diffusion model for BCI applications
abstract: The limited availability of labeled task-related electroencephalography (EEG) data continues to hinder progress in brain-computer interface (BCI) research. Acquiring and annotating EEG signals under specific experimental conditions is often labor-intensive and time-consuming, creating significant challenges in scaling data collection and ensuring model robustness. To alleviate this constraint, we propose EEGDiffuser, a diffusion-based generative model designed to synthesize EEG signals conditioned on task labels. EEGDiffuser formulates EEG synthesis as a reverse stochastic process guided by learned score functions, progressively refining Gaussian noise into structured signals. To ensure that the generated samples align with specific experimental conditions, a conditional guidance mechanism is introduced to incorporate label information during generation. By modeling key neurophysiological characteristics of EEG, EEGDiffuser is able to generate realistic and label-consistent EEG signals. Empirical evaluations across diverse tasks and decoder architectures demonstrate that incorporating synthetic signals consistently improves decoding performance, even in low-resource scenarios. On three benchmark datasets (FACED, BCIC-IV-2a, and BCIC2020-3), EEGDiffuser yields a relative improvement of 4%–6% in over real-data-only baselines and consistently outperforms existing EEG synthesis methods. Further analysis shows that the generated EEG data preserve neurophysiologically relevant patterns, such as emotion-related topographies and motor imagery activation distributions, comparable to those observed in real data collected under specific conditions. EEGDiffuser highlights the potential of diffusion-based generative modeling to facilitate data-driven EEG research and enable the investigation of neurophysiological patterns in BCI applications.

title: DSTMNet: A dual spatiotemporal modeling network for EEG-based emotion recognition
abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG)-based emotion recognition methods are gaining attention due to their robustness and reliability, especially compared to techniques that rely on facial expressions or speech signals. However, fully exploiting the spatiotemporal information embedded in EEG signals remains a significant challenge. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Dual Spatiotemporal Modeling Network (DSTMNet) aimed at effectively capturing both spatial and temporal dependencies in EEG data through data-level and feature-level spatiotemporal modeling. In data-level spatiotemporal modeling, an equidistant azimuthal projection is utilized to map the three-dimensional (3D) spatial coordinates of EEG electrodes onto a two-dimensional (2D) plane. These coordinates are discretized on a fixed-size high-resolution spatial grid, and contour-aware interpolation is employed to generate dense brain activity maps at each time step. The maps are stacked along the temporal axis to form a video-like volumetric representation, encoding the brain’s topological structure and the temporal dynamics of EEG signals. In feature-level spatiotemporal modeling, the information compressor based on 3D convolution, the local information aggregator based on 3D convolution attention, and the global information interactor based on multi-head self-attention are used to compact embedded features, acquire short-range informational representations, and capture long-range informational representations, respectively. This hierarchical representation of EEG information enhances the network’s ability to learn discriminative features. Experimental evaluations further confirm its effectiveness, achieving recognition accuracies of 98.4% on the MAHNOB-HCI dataset and 49.6% on the SEED-VII dataset.

title: Contrastive coarse-to-fine medical segmentation with prototype guidance and dual-granularity fusion
abstract: Recent advances in the Segment Anything Model (SAM) have demonstrated remarkable zero-shot segmentation and interactive editing capabilities in general computer vision. However, adapting SAM to medical imaging remains challenging due to substantial gaps in imaging physics, contrast distributions, and structural priors between natural and medical images. Achieving optimal performance typically requires extensive fine-tuning on large-scale medical datasets and high-quality manual prompts. To address these limitations, we propose CCF-SAM, a parameter-efficient adaptation framework for medical segmentation. With the SAM image encoder frozen, CCF-SAM constructs a coarse-to-fine, two-stage pipeline: a standard decoder first generates a coarse prior mask, which is then refined by a Contrastive Prototype Refiner that softly disentangles foreground/background tokens and enhances their discriminability via token-level contrastive learning. An EMA-based prototype memory accumulates stable semantic anchors across images, and a cross-attention re-embedding module injects the enhanced prototypes into spatial features to drive fine-grained decoding. The framework trains only the prompt encoder, the mask decoder, and the newly added lightweight modules, substantially reducing training costs while ensuring reproducibility. Comprehensive evaluations and ablations on multiple representative 2D medical segmentation benchmarks show that CCF-SAM consistently outperforms classical CNN/Transformer baselines and recent SAM-based approaches. Qualitative results further indicate superior recall and boundary consistency on small or low-contrast lesions, validating a prototype-guided, progressive refinement paradigm for adapting SAM to medical imaging. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/KKKKAAAAIIII/CCF-SAM.

title: EEG-TFX: An interactive MATLAB toolbox for EEG feature engineering via multi-scale temporal windowing and filter banks
abstract: This paper presents an intelligent Electroencephalogram (EEG) analysis platform (EEG-TFX) that provides a comprehensive solution for EEG signal processing. The platform adopts a modular design, integrating data preprocessing, time-frequency segmentation, feature extraction, model training, and visualization functions. It supports flexible configuration of time windows, frequency band segmentation, and multiple filter order selections. The platform offers various feature extraction methods, including entropy-based features and other popular EEG features, together with multiple classification algorithms, such as artificial neural networks, support vector machines, and decision trees. In addition, the system supports user-defined function extensions. It enables joint feature processing, dynamic visualization, and result export, making it suitable for multiple neuro-computing research fields such as brain-computer interfaces, neural rehabilitation, and EEG-based emotion recognition. EEG-TFX significantly enhances the efficiency and reliability of EEG signal analysis by providing standardized workflows, offering a convenient and integrated tool for related research. The toolbox is open-source and available at: https://github.com/Xin-qy/EEG-TFX.

title: HMFCDA: Hierarchical deep learning with semantic embeddings for CircRNA-disease association prediction
abstract: Recent studies have revealed the crucial roles of circRNAs in human disease development, highlighting their significant potential as diagnostic biomarkers.
