However, conventional biological experiments for identifying circRNA-disease associations remain time-consuming and labor-intensive. To address this limitation, this study proposes a novel hierarchical multimodal fusion framework, termed HMFCDA, which integrates hierarchical deep learning with semantic embeddings to predict potential circRNA-disease associations. The framework first employs a transformer model to encode primary vector representations from circRNA sequences, which are subsequently refined through a graph attention network to extract deeper features. Simultaneously, semantic representations for diseases are generated using word embedding techniques. The circRNA deep features and disease semantic embeddings are fused to form a joint representation, which is finally fed into a Random Forest classifier for association prediction. Evaluated on the benchmark CircR2Disease dataset, HMFCDA achieved an average prediction accuracy of 93.88% and an AUC of 0.9767 under 5-fold cross-validation, significantly outperforming existing methods. Furthermore, case studies demonstrated that 18 of the top 20 predicted circRNA-disease associations were corroborated by recent literature evidence. These results underscore the efficacy of HMFCDA as a powerful computational tool for circRNA-disease association identification, providing reliable candidates and valuable insights for subsequent experimental validation.

title: Affine non-negative discriminative representation for biomedical image classification
abstract: Biomedical imaging plays a vital role in modern healthcare by supporting accurate diagnosis and informed clinical decision-making. Although recent advances in artificial intelligence have significantly improved biomedical image analysis, persistent challenges remain, including high data variability, limited availability of annotated samples, and the need for transparent and interpretable classification models. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel classification framework termed affine non-negative discriminative representation-based classification (ANDRC) for robust biomedical image recognition. In the proposed framework, a non-negativity constraint is imposed on the representation coefficients, which enforces the test sample to be reconstructed as a purely additive combination of training samples. By preventing subtractive contributions induced by negative coefficients, this constraint encourages stronger contributions from homogeneous samples while naturally suppressing misleading representations from heterogeneous ones, thereby enhancing both interpretability and discriminative stability. In addition, an affine constraint is incorporated to effectively model the intrinsic structure of data distributed over a union of affine subspaces, which commonly arises in real-world biomedical imaging scenarios. The resulting optimization problem is efficiently solved using the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers, ensuring stable convergence and computational efficiency. Extensive experiments conducted on multiple biomedical image classification benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed ANDRC method consistently outperforms several state-of-the-art approaches. These results highlight the effectiveness of ANDRC in handling data variability and label scarcity, as well as its potential for practical deployment in biomedical image analysis.

title: UP2D: Uncertainty-aware progressive pseudo-label denoising for source-free domain adaptive medical image segmentation
abstract: Medical image segmentation models face severe performance drops under domain shifts, especially when data sharing constraints prevent access to source images. We present a novel Uncertainty-aware Progressive Pseudo-label Denoising (UP2D) framework for source-free domain adaptation (SFDA), designed to mitigate noisy pseudo-labels and class imbalance during adaptation. UP2D integrates three key components: (i) a Refined Prototype Filtering module that suppresses uninformative regions and constructs reliable class prototypes to denoise pseudo-labels, (ii) an Uncertainty-Guided EMA (UG-EMA) strategy that selectively updates the teacher model based on spatially weighted boundary uncertainty, and (iii) a quantile-based entropy minimization scheme that focuses learning on ambiguous regions while avoiding overconfidence on easy pixels. This single-stage student-teacher framework progressively improves pseudo-label quality and reduces confirmation bias. Extensive experiments on three challenging retinal fundus benchmarks demonstrate that UP2D achieves state-of-the-art performance across both standard and open-domain settings, outperforming prior UDA and SFDA approaches while maintaining superior boundary precision.

title: An exergy-related fault diagnosis framework based on fault-agnostic meta-learning for industrial multimode batch processes
abstract: To adapt to the diversity of consumer demand and fierce market competition, the manufacturing industry is increasingly shifting towards implementing flexible production systems. Variability in working modes, scarcity of fault data, differences in data distribution among varying batches, and underutilization of energy consumption information have led to poor universality and low diagnostic accuracy of traditional machine learning-based fault diagnosis methods. To solve the above problems, this work proposes an exergy-related fault diagnosis framework based on fault-agnostic meta-learning (FAML) for multimode batch processes. First, the exergy-related variables are selected and transformed into image data as the input of the diagnosis model. Then, based on model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) and the Inception module, we develop the FAML network that makes meta-learns an unbiased initial model by preventing it from overfitting in diagnostic tasks and improving its training stability. Finally, the FAML-based fault diagnosis framework is applied to a real hot strip mill process (HSMP). The experimental results show that FAML has higher diagnostic accuracy than other methods for different modes and batches.

title: Intelligent fault diagnosis based on TimeGAN with channel-temporal attention module
abstract: Underwater flexible manipulators are critical for precise ocean operations, and their safe operation relies on effective fault diagnosis. However, their operational environment makes it difficult to obtain high-fidelity fault monitoring datasets, resulting in class distribution skew that severely compromises diagnostic reliability. This imperative underscores the critical need for robust generative models capable of synthesizing high-fidelity temporal sequences with physical consistency. Traditional generative models, however, face two main challenges in generating time-series data: insufficient capture of temporal dependencies and low feature discrimination across channels. To overcome the aforementioned limitations, the Channel-Temporal Attention Module (CTAM) was proposed, it was integrated with the Time-series Generative Adversarial Network (TimeGAN) to form CTAM-TimeGAN, aiming to enhance the generation capability of temporal data. The CTAM enhances representational capacity through coordinated multi-dimensional feature fusion, which when synergistically integrated with the TimeGAN framework, generating high-quality fault signals for underwater flexible manipulators while optimizing diagnostic classification efficacy, thus effectively resolves class-imbalance challenges. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, the experiments were conducted by collecting fault data from an underwater flexible manipulator. The experimental results show that the diagnosis accuracy of the CTAM-TimeGAN method increases by 15.00 % at an imbalance ratio of 10:1, 21.05 % at 25:1, and 41.98 % at 50:1. When compared to four commonly used time series data augmentation methods, the results demonstrate that CTAM-TimeGAN achieves the highest accuracy increment across all comparison algorithms under various imbalance ratios. Thus, this paper presents an effective solution for fault diagnosis in underwater flexible manipulators under data imbalance conditions.

title: Handling mislabeled data in fault diagnosis: A graph-assisted random forest approach
abstract: Label information plays a critical role in both supervised and semi-supervised learning-based fault diagnosis methods. However, mislabeled data can significantly degrade the classification performance of the resulting fault diagnosis model. To address this challenge, a graph-assisted random forest (GARF) approach is proposed in this paper, aiming to mitigate the adverse effects of mislabeled data in fault diagnosis. The core of this approach is a spectral clustering matching (SCM)-based method for identifying incorrect labels, leveraging the independence of the graph structure from sample labels. Identified mislabeled samples are subsequently stripped of their incorrect labels and treated as unlabeled data. Subsequently, a graph-based semi-supervised learning (GSSL) algorithm is employed to infer corrected labels for these samples, using the underlying graph topology to enable effective label correction. Following this, a random forest (RF) classifier is trained on the rectified dataset to establish the GARF-based fault diagnosis model, facilitating real-time fault diagnosis. The proposed method is validated using monitoring data from a hardware-in-the-loop high-speed train simulation platform. Experimental results show that the GARF method outperforms multiple existing approaches across key metrics, including accuracy, recall, F1-score, and computational efficiency.

title: Dual-stream symbiotic architecture: Mitigating rotational speed domain feature distribution shift for adaptive bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: The field of rotating machinery bearing fault diagnosis has been persistently confronted with the fundamental challenge of feature distribution displacement attributable to rotational velocity variations. This investigation introduces the “Dual-Stream Symbiotic” architecture, which establishes an adaptive diagnostic paradigm transcending distinct rotational velocity domains. The methodology implements a bifurcated processing framework for extracting complementary feature representations: the spectral representation pathway synergistically integrates Fast Wavelet Transform with a Transformer encoder to facilitate precise characterization of signal frequency attributes, while the time-frequency mapping pathway employs Gramian Angular Field nonlinear transformations coupled with a deep spatiotemporal residual network to elucidate non-stationary, temporally-variant signal phenomena. The methodology incorporates an innovative multi-head cross-attention mechanism, which facilitates dynamic feature interaction across disparate domains through a meticulously engineered head-to-head interconnection topology, thereby establishing a bidirectional knowledge transfer conduit between spectral and time-frequency representations. Comprehensive empirical evaluation demonstrates the methodology’s exceptional efficacy: the approach achieves a mean classification accuracy of 98.69% on the CWRU dataset, surpassing state-of-the-art methodologies by 0.78 percentage points. In the most challenging velocity variation scenarios of the HIT dataset, the model maintains robust diagnostic performance with an accuracy of 91.54%, and a mean accuracy of 97.45% across all sixteen experimental configurations, outperforming extant methodologies by a substantial margin of 14.26 percentage points. T-SNE visualization analysis corroborates the methodology’s significant capacity for extracting rotational velocity-invariant discriminative features, thereby providing both theoretical foundations and practical implementations for addressing domain adaptation challenges in bearing fault diagnosis applications.

title: Temporal-filter enhanced prediction of whole-brain neural activity using the physiology-aligned latent variable model
abstract: Understanding the neural mechanisms behind intelligent behaviors in nematodes requires a comprehensive framework that integrates connectome data with recordings of all neuronal activities. However, obtaining full membrane potentials for all labeled neurons is challenging, and even in C. elegans, which has only 302 neurons, current calcium imaging techniques typically capture just over half of these labeled neurons in vivo. Existing advances primarily focus on using spatial correlation across the whole brain to causally predict unknown neuronal activities by using measured activities of half-numbered neurons, but they struggle to achieve high prediction accuracy. By introducing a quasi-independent temporal coding property of populational neurons in living brains, e.g., C. elegans, we establish the Temporal-Filter and Physiology-Aligned Latent Variable Model (TF-PALVM), a new algorithmic leap that synergizes the spatial connectome structure with temporal coding functions of individual neurons to infer the electrical activities of the entire neural ensemble. This model employs an autoencoder network with temporal kernels, rather than relying on spatial correlations, refined to reflect individual neuronal temporal coding functions and predict their future temporal activities, while embedding experimentally derived synaptic weights into a biologically coherent framework. When tested, our model demonstrates unprecedented reconstruction accuracy, surpassing existing models by approximately 75 % in the worm holdout evaluation and 51 % in neuron holdout performance. Moreover, it precisely predicts synaptic polarities, with 75 % of them to be excitatory, matching experimental excitatory synapse data. It is also able to identify the top neuron pairs with the most influence on behavioral correlations, consistent with previous experimental research. Our TF-PALVM stands as a transformative tool for neuroscientific exploration, capable of predicting missing neuronal activity with high fidelity. The success of the model confirms that the temporal response history of individual neurons contains more valuable information than the population network in predicting their present and future responses to sensory inputs. It offers a scalable approach to potentially unravel the complexities of larger, more intricate brains.

title: MAP-GR: medical aware prompt and graph-guided reasoning for enhanced medical visual question answering
abstract: Medical Visual Question Answering (Med-VQA) refers to the task of automatically generating accurate answers based on medical images and corresponding questions. It plays a critical role in computer-aided diagnosis.However, it still poses significant challenges in interpreting subtle pathological visual cues and complex clinical semantics.To address these challenges, this paper proposes the MAP-GR model, which integrates a Medical-Aware Prompt (MAP) and Graph-guided Reasoning (GR). Compared with the cross-modal prompts of UNIDCP [22], MAP initializes prompt vectors through entities extracted by PubMed NER, enhancing the localization of fine-grained lesions. In contrast to the latent prompt enhancement approach of LaPA [23], GR directly empowers the model with the ability to reason about complex organ-disease relationships and nuanced semantics embedded in clinical questions via a Graph Attention Network (GAT). On the VQA-RAD, SLAKE, and VQA-2019 datasets, the overall accuracy of MAP-GR reaches 79.83 %±0.15 %, 84.97 %±0.12 %, and 83.23 %±0.10 % respectively, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and robustness.

title: Adaptive neural seizure detection through intelligent EEG channel selection and dynamic feature recognition
abstract: This study introduces a convolutional neural network with dynamic channel selection-feature generation, an advanced deep learning model that combines modules of feature generation, dynamic channel selection, and a convolutional neural network to improve the classification of the epileptic state of electroencephalography signals. The proposed framework dynamically chooses the most pertinent electroencephalography channels, enhances feature extraction, and limits the impact of class imbalance effects. The experimental evaluation of a clinical electroencephalography dataset shows that our model is superior to current models in feature generation-dynamic channel selection neural networks and achieves good classification accuracy. To validate the results of the proposed method, different evaluation metrics are considered along with statistical analysis, achieving an average precision of 96% over multiple folds. Furthermore, the EEG dataset from various neurophysiological states provides insight into seizures, framing them as bifurcations in brain dynamics through nonlinear dynamics theory.

title: PAWS-net: prior-aware weakly supervised network for pulmonary disease localization and classification in CT scans
abstract: In this paper, a two-stage diagnostic framework, PAWS-Net, is proposed, which leverages a novel pseudo supervision strategy to alleviate common challenges in weakly supervised lung CT analysis, including annotation scarcity at the nodule level, incomplete feature learning and poor discrimination between nodules and background regions. Specifically, the framework cascades a lung nodule detection network with a disease classification network, where pseudo-label masks are generated to guide attention of the classifier toward potential lesion regions, thereby enhancing both discriminative capability and learning efficiency. Simultaneously, an efficient heterogeneous module (EHM) is introduced in the backbone of the detection network, incorporating dimensionality reduction and heterogeneous multi-branch convolution structures to efficiently capture shallow lesion features with improved robustness. In the neck part, a sparse selective attention (SSA) module is employed, which utilizes multi-scale dilated convolutions to construct sparse receptive fields, directing attention to critical areas while suppressing background noise. Moreover, the classification network adopts a CNN-BiLSTM hybrid structure to jointly model intra-slice spatial features and inter-slice contextual dependencies across CT sequences, thereby enhancing the ability to perceive lesion morphology and improving multi-disease recognition accuracy. Experimental results show that the proposed PAWS-Net achieves State-Of-The-Art (SOTA) performance under weakly supervised conditions, reaching an accuracy of 82.5% on the TriPulmoCT dataset, which outperforms other advanced models by a notable margin and confirms its effectiveness for lung CT-based disease diagnosis.

title: FedPSAWA: Federated personalization with state aware weighting aggregation for cross subject seizure prediction
abstract: Random variations in electroencephalogram (EEG) signals are usually regarded as useless noise, but in the emerging positive noise learning paradigm, these noises can be considered as useful information. Inspired by this, we proposed FedPSAWA, a personalized federated framework with state aware weighted aggregation, which utilizes the differences between subjects as structured positive noise to enhance global adaptability. To address the imbalance among samples, the data augmentation method based on physiology aware (PADA) reconstructs the signal through discrete wavelet transform, enriching the EEG characterization while retaining the specific features of the subjects. To better learn the differences between subjects, QBFormer is an attention bridge transformer based on query features, which selectively extracts noise elastic prediction patterns through query-based attention. We verified on a multi-center EEG dataset that FedPSAWA can effectively convert inherent randomness into beneficial learning signals, achieving better accuracy, interpretability and robustness in federated seizure prediction.

title: Digital twin-driven gearbox fault diagnosis with model-expandable incremental learning
abstract: A gearbox fault diagnosis method integrating digital twin and dynamic expansion incremental learning is proposed, which effectively addresses the challenges of data sparsity and continuous identification of new faults in industrial scenarios. A 3D digital twin model of the gear transmission system is constructed, and ADAMS software is utilized to simulate the gear meshing dynamics, generating high-fidelity simulation data. Innovatively, the Wasserstein distance is employed to measure the feature distribution discrepancy between virtual simulation data and real data, with cross-domain feature alignment achieved through a shared feature extraction network. To tackle the catastrophic forgetting issue in incremental learning, a two-stage dynamic expansion mechanism is designed: In the feature learning stage, the feature extractor is expanded and an auxiliary classifier is introduced to enhance the retention of old knowledge; in the classifier learning stage, a joint sample replay strategy is adopted to balance old and new categories, combined with channel pruning to control model complexity. Experiments on the HUST gearbox fault dataset show that the method achieves an average accuracy of 85.69% across 7 incremental tasks, outperforming the best baseline by 2.21%, and reduces the parameter count by 63% at a pruning rate of 0.5, significantly improving the sustainable diagnostic capability of industrial equipment.

title: Dynamic neural networks in biomedical applications: A review from embedded systems to AI-driven interventions
abstract: Dynamic Neural Networks are redefining biomedical intelligent systems by bridging mathematical control theory and clinical translation. Rooted in differential formulations originally developed for nonlinear system identification, Dynamic Neural Networks extend beyond static learning to capture continuous-time feedback, memory, and adaptation—core properties of living physiological systems. This review unifies theoretical and applied developments of Dynamic Neural Networks across biomedical domains, highlighting their capacity to model, identify, and control complex biological dynamics. Using the PRISMA methodology, publications from 2015–2025 were systematically analyzed to map the evolution of recurrent, differential, and hybrid neural architectures across four major application areas: physiological signal monitoring and interpretation, intelligent control systems in therapeutic devices, drug delivery and pharmacological regulation, and personalized medicine with predictive diagnostics. The reviewed works demonstrate how Dynamic Neural Networks-based frameworks enable context-aware interpretation of biosignals, adaptive control in prosthetics and exoskeletons, and data-driven precision in clinical decision support. Notably, a differential neural identifier for fetal ECG monitoring is presented as a case study, exemplifying how continuous-time learning can reconstruct hidden cardiac dynamics from single-channel abdominal recordings—achieving accurate morphology preservation and noise rejection with demonstrated suitability for embedded or resource-constrained fetal monitoring scenarios. Across applications, Dynamic Neural Networks consistently exhibit advantages over static architectures in terms of adaptability, feedback integration, and temporal modeling capability, which are critical properties for real-time biomedical systems. While fully deployed embedded implementations remain limited to selected studies, the reviewed evidence indicates strong algorithmic suitability and growing feasibility for embedded and edge-AI realization. The findings confirm that Dynamic Neural Network–based identifiers, controllers, and predictors form the computational foundation for next-generation intelligent healthcare, advancing the convergence of theoretical dynamic modeling, embedded artificial intelligence, and adaptive therapeutic intervention.

title: Cross-domain semantic compensation via spatial–frequency decoupling for robust medical image segmentation
abstract: Cross-domain information offers different perspectives on the image, and can enhance the intelligent image segmentation model's understanding of image semantics. In this study, we propose a Combined Spatial-frequency Domain Information for Medical Image Segmentation Network (SDMNet), which can improve the medical image seg-mentation performance by cross-domain semantic compensation. Specifically, SDM-Net decouples task-relevant high-frequency and low-frequency information in the frequency domain to compensate for spatial semantics. To align Spatial-frequency domain multimodal features, we design a Progressive Cross-Modal Semantic Interactor (PCSI). Moreover, we propose a Semantic Bidding Integration Strategy (SBIS) that can adaptively select and fuse feature maps containing the richest semantics using a novel bidding approach. Last but not least, we construct a large Bone Marrow Cell Segmentation Image Dataset (2025 BMCS) for training intelligent bone marrow cell segmentation models and promoting related techniques. Extensive experiments conducted on five public medical image benchmarks and the 2025 BMCS dataset demon-strate that SDMNet consistently surpasses current state-of-the-art approaches, high-lighting its superior adaptability and domain-specific representation capability. Our code and 2025 BMCS dataset will be available at https://github.com/chasingone/SDMNet.

title: A survey on large language models from general purpose to medical applications: Datasets, methodologies, and evaluations
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated surprising performance across various natural language processing tasks. Recently, medical LLMs enhanced with domain-specific knowledge have exhibited excellent capabilities in medical consultation and diagnosis. These models can smoothly simulate doctor-patient dialogues and provide professional medical advice. Most medical LLMs are developed through continued training of open-source general LLMs, which require significantly fewer computational resources than training LLMs from scratch. Additionally, this approach offers better patient privacy protection than API-based solutions. Given the above advantages, this survey systematically summarizes how to train medical LLMs based on open-source general LLMs from a more fine-grained perspective. It covers (a) how to acquire training corpus and construct customized medical training sets, (b) how to choose an appropriate training paradigm, (c) how to choose a suitable evaluation benchmark, and (d) existing challenges and promising research directions are discussed. This survey can provide guidance for the development of LLMs focused on various medical applications, such as medical education, diagnostic planning, and clinical assistants. Related resources and supplemental information can be found on the GitHub repository.

title: ADML: Asymmetric deformation-guided mutual learning for semi-supervised medical image segmentation
abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) has achieved remarkable success in medical image segmentation, with co-training paradigms standing out among existing approaches. However, most current methods use homogeneous network architectures, where identical inductive biases can cause confirmation bias, limiting performance. Additionally, these methods treat all pixels equally, failing to fully exploit the hidden information in complex regions. To overcome these issues, we propose an Asymmetric Deformation-guided Mutual Learning (ADML) framework. ADML builds an asymmetric dual-branch system consisting of a standard convolutional network (V-Net) and a deformable convolutional network (VNet-DCN), adding diverse inductive biases to provide heterogeneous supervisory signals. The core of our framework is asymmetric deformation-guided consistency learning (ADCL), which leverages the norm of the DCN offset field to measure local deformation complexity. This allows for the creation of spatial weight maps that adaptively modify pseudo-label weights, helping reduce confirmation bias and improve the reliability of pseudo-labels. Additionally, to enable knowledge transfer between the asymmetric models, we introduce a Cross-model Dynamic Feature Bank that stores high-confidence features and enforces alignment through a maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss, achieving deep semantic coherence between the two branches. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks show that ADML surpasses state-of-the-art methods, confirming its effectiveness in lowering annotation needs and enhancing segmentation accuracy.

title: An explainable multi-view representation fusion learning framework with hybrid MetaFormer for EEG-based epileptic seizure detection
abstract: Multi-view learning (MVL), a paradigm of deep learning, has greatly facilitated the detection of epileptic seizures from electroencephalograms (EEGs) owing to its remarkable capability to learn generalization features. However, existing MVL-based seizure detection methods rely on decision strategies to aggregate the discriminative outputs of separate learners, leading to insufficient extraction of inter-view complementarity and limiting the detection performance. To address this issue, this paper focuses on two aspects and proposes a multi-view representation fusion learning framework, which enables direct information fusion at the feature encoding level. Firstly, to enhance discriminability, we construct hierarchical multi-view representations based on the Gramian Angular Summation Field and an improved Stockwell transform by introducing the spatial characteristics of EEG montages and temporal dependency dynamics. Secondly, to process both local and global features comprehensively, we propose a hybrid MetaFormer network that incorporates inverted depth-wise separable convolutions and sparsity-enhanced shifted-window attention mechanisms. Specifically, the fusion unit with cross-attention mechanisms exploits the Key and Value matrices to achieve effective inter-view information exchange. The experimental results on the public CHB-MIT and Siena datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms competing techniques in both sample-based and event-based evaluations for EEG seizure detection. In addition, an explanation module is devised based on feature importance scoring. In this way, our method enables post-hoc explanations for the multi-view fusion learning process and discriminative results utilizing topographic maps, indicating an explainable computational solution for EEG seizure detection.

title: Hi-PET: A hybrid framework for resource-efficient 3D low-dose brain positron emission tomography image denoising
abstract: Positron Emission Tomography (PET) has become a widely utilized medical imaging technology for evaluating various diseases, particularly neurological disorders. While full-dose PET (F-PET) imaging ensures high-quality images crucial for clinical diagnosis, it raises significant concerns about the potential health risks associated with radiation exposure. The challenge of balancing reduced radiation exposure with maintaining diagnostic performance can be effectively addressed through the denoising of low-dose PET (L-PET) images to achieve the high quality of F-PET images. In this paper, we introduce Hi-PET, a novel hybrid framework designed to achieve resource-efficient 3D end-to-end denoising of L-PET brain images. Hi-PET consists of three concise and purpose-driven modules: a diffused cascade generation mechanism, a diffused multi-scale discrimination process, and a resource-efficient 3D scalable overlapped sliding-patch approach. This framework represents the first demonstration of the advantages of a hybrid model that combines the efficient multi-scale discriminative capabilities of the Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) with the high-quality, iterative and stable generation process of the Diffusion Model for enhanced L-PET image denoising. A novel Pareto-efficient dynamic optimization process is proposed to bridge the GAN-based and the Diffusion-based pipelines, effectively regulating noise diffusion during both the generation and discrimination stages. We have evaluated Hi-PET on three datasets, including two independent and one mixed dataset, benchmarking against 10 state-of-the-art models. Experimental results confirm that Hi-PET achieves efficient, 3D end-to-end L-PET image denoising, setting new benchmarks across multiple metrics. Building on the Hi-PET framework, an ultra-fast L-PET image denoising system was developed with a user-friendly interface and visualization capabilities.

title: The double-edged sword: A critical review of foundational medical datasets for AI benchmarks, biases, and the future of equitable healthcare
abstract: The advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionized medical diagnostics and treatment. Large-scale public datasets are fueling research in this field. Therefore, this systematic review is a comprehensive analysis of 13 foundational medical datasets. It evaluates the characteristics, performance metrics, and inherent biases of datasets across medical imaging, electronic health records, and genomics. The published literature is systematically reviewed to categorize these datasets, with a focus on performance metrics for everyday machine learning tasks. Additionally, this research documents evidence of systemic bias and limitations that affect model generalizability and clinical equity. Our analysis reveals compelling evidence that significant limitations temper the remarkable progress of algorithms. It has been frequently observed that AI models suffer dramatic accuracy drops when tested beyond their training distribution, with the Area Under the Curve consistently declining from 0.95 to 0.63. The research also identified consistent patterns of systemic bias that threaten the equitable application of healthcare. This bias stems from unrepresentative sampling, subjective annotation practices, label noise, and Natural Language Processing-derived ground-truth labels. Our findings demonstrate the urgent need for a paradigm shift in the development of medical applications. The AI and medical communities must prioritize generating diverse datasets and mitigating systematic bias. This study provides evidence-based recommendations and a technical toolkit to address these challenges and reduce any health disparities.

title: Prototype-driven expert voting for pseudo-label selection with dual-balanced loss for imbalanced medical image classification
abstract: Medical image datasets inherently suffer from class imbalance, label scarcity, and intra-class heterogeneity. Under semi-supervised learning, pseudo-label selection remains a central research focus. Class prototypes constructed in the latent space have been studied for pseudo-label selection, particularly because sub-class prototypes can effectively represent within-class heterogeneity in medical imaging datasets. However, since sub-class prototypes are constructed using a relatively small number of samples, they may lead to local optima during prototype updating and usage. In addition, loss weight rebalancing is commonly used to mitigate attention bias in model. Existing methods tend to focus exclusively on improving the minority class, without taking into account ambiguous samples, which are often difficult to learn and contain valuable information. Here, a prototype-driven framework PDMatch is proposed, incorporating Prototype-Driven Expert Voting (PDEV), Majority-class Pseudo-label Under-Sampling (MPUS) and Dual-Balanced Loss (DBL). First, an Expert Prototype Set is constructed, and hierarchical updating is proposed to sufficiently capture the feature distributions. PDEV then generates and filters pseudo-labels through prototype-driven voting, where multiple candidate sub-class prototypes are jointly considered. Second, MPUS offers a concise post-processing strategy that reduces imbalance in the pseudo-label distribution. Finally, Dual-Balanced Loss rebalances loss weights to jointly account for class distribution and sample difficulty. Comprehensive experiments are conducted on three datasets with distinct imbalance structures, demonstrating that our model addresses inherent data challenges and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple metrics. Additionally, we compare our model with clinical expert assessments to underscore its practical value in real-world applications. Source code is available at https://github.com/wang-su-lei/PDMatch .

title: Hierarchy-aware graph neural network and inverse-variance reinforcement learning for drug recommendation
abstract: Drug recommendation (DR) based on artificial intelligence plays a crucial role in healthcare research, offering precise and effective drug prescription suggestions for doctors. However, existing methods typically model DR as a sequential task, overlooking the complex correlations among medical entities present in electronic medical records (EMRs). To this end, we propose a novel DR model that integrates a hierarchy-aware graph neural network (GNN) with inverse-variance (IV) reinforcement learning (RL). Specifically, we represent patient and drug information using a knowledge graph, and employ a hyperbolic space-embedded GNN to encode the hierarchical structure among graph nodes. We propose an IV-RL mechanism to reduce excessive exploration of the model on inefficient or noisy data. By incorporating IV into the RL framework, the model can more efficiently sample from the training data, thereby enhancing learning performance. Extensive experiments, on the widely-used MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, and eICU, datasets demonstrate that our proposed method achieves superior performance and exhibits reliable DR capabilities. We believe that our proposed method provides a promising solution for accurate and effective DR, and opens up new opportunities for further research.

title: 3MU-Net: A multi-layer, multi-view and multi-modal segmentation model for PET/CT images of lung tumors
abstract: Multimodal medical images provide reliable and accurate information on the lesion categories, which is essential for diagnosing lung cancer. In medical images, the adequate extraction of lesion cross-modal features and lesion contextual semantic information is a key issue. 3MU-Net is proposed by this paper, which is a Multi-layer, Multi-view and Multi-modal lung tumors segmentation model. The main contributions of 3MU-Net are as follows: Firstly, CMformer uses parallel CNN branch and Transformer branch to learn cross-modal medical image features, which builds cross-modal pixel dependencies between global features and local features. Secondly, Cross-view Context-aware Processor is designed, there are four Deep-Shallow Feature Enhancement Modules and a Cross-view Attention Module in Cross-view Context-aware Processor. Deep-Shallow Feature Enhancement Module uses a bidirectional learning method to guide the information interaction between shallow-level features and deep-level features, which reduces the semantic information gap between adjacent layers. In addition, the Deep-Shallow Feature Enhancement Module aggregates coarse-grained semantic features and fine-grained detailed features. Cross-view Attention Module is used to obtain multi-scale lesion information through multi-view feature extraction, which extends the diversity of spatial features in the lesion area. Finally, the effectiveness of 3MU-Net is validated on a clinical multimodal lung medical image dataset. The results for Miou, Dice, Voe, Rvd, Acc, and Recall are 90.97%, 95.23%, 93.87%, 94.13%, 97.97%, and 94.45%, respectively. It is great significance for lung tumors segmentation. Code is available at: https://github.com/xiaoniu1030/ 3MU-Net.

title: WSTC: Task-adaptive medical vision–language model with semantic tokens and dynamic alignment
abstract: Recent medical vision–language models enable zero- and few-shot transfer, yet still depend on handcrafted prompts and task-specific heads. To address these limitations, we introduce Weakly Semantic-aware Task Conditioning (WSTC), a lightweight, plug-and-play framework that endows frozen vision–language models with strong adaptability across classification, retrieval, and segmentation. WSTC contains two modules: (i) the Weakly Semantic-Aware Module, which distills task cues from image patches into image-derived semantic tokens, without text-side prompt engineering or prompt tuning, and (ii) the Task-Conditioned Dynamic Alignment Module, which dynamically generates projection matrices to align vision–language embeddings under task guidance. Built on a frozen UniMedCLIP backbone, WSTC adapts to new tasks without tuning the backbone and requires a moderate trainable parameter budget for adaptation. Across both zero-shot and few-shot regimes, our method UniMedCLIP augmented with WSTC consistently outperforms strong frozen vision–language models (CLIP, MedCLIP, BioViL, PubMedCLIP, UniMedCLIP) and further surpasses adapter baselines such as Tip-Adapter and Meta-Adapter. These results highlight WSTC as a practical solution for scalable medical vision–language models under extreme data scarcity.

title: A two-step transfer learning approach for railway point machine fault diagnosis under small sample conditions
abstract: Fault diagnosis technology based on Transfer Learning (TL) has been widely investigated, as it enables knowledge transfer from related domains to the target domain, thereby reducing the need for large amounts of labeled data in the target domain. In the railway industry, Railway Point Machines (RPMs) are essential track-connection devices. However, due to the scarcity of fault data for RPMs, the accuracy of RPM fault diagnosis remains low. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a Two-step Transfer Learning (TSTL) method for RPM fault diagnosis. First, a small set of target-domain samples transformed by continuous wavelet transform (CWT) is used to construct a transition dataset, which is fed into a Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) to generate synthetic samples. Then, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with a top-down attention mechanism is employed to perform the first phase of TL from the source domain to the generated domain. Next, the parameters of selected frozen layers in the transferred CNN are retained to conduct the second phase of learning from the generated domain to the target domain. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 98.7% accuracy for fault diagnosis across different positions on the same RPM, and 95.6% accuracy across different RPMs at the same position.

title: Structure-aware fine-grained instance segmentation for fetal brain ultrasound images
abstract: Fetal brain ultrasound segmentation remains challenging due to complex morphology and low-contrast imaging. Existing deep learning methods often lack anatomical awareness and spatial consistency, resulting in inaccurate boundaries, particularly for small structures, and they typically segment only a limited set of anatomical structures. To overcome these issues, a structure-aware fine-grained instance segmentation framework is proposed. The framework performs instance-level detection and mask prediction, enabling fine-grained segmentation of 25 anatomical structures across five standard planes. Specifically, a structure-aware overlap metric is proposed to mitigate the misclassification of small structures caused by conventional Intersection-over-Union based positive/negative sample assignment. Based on this metric, an improved non-maximum suppression algorithm is developed accordingly to enhance small-structure detection. A fine-grained segmentation head with an enlarged receptive field is designed to preserve essential details of anatomical structures. The proposed structure-aware Laplacian regularization strategy further refines the spatial consistency of masks and boundary accuracy through graph Laplacian smoothing. Additionally, a domain-adaptive generative augmentation strategy based on Stable Diffusion with Low-Rank Adaptation is applied to synthesize anatomically diverse fetal brain ultrasound images and improve segmentation model generalization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms existing baselines on fetal brain ultrasound segmentation.

title: SAM2-driven dual-teacher framework using hierarchical cross-slice context for semi-supervised 3D medical image segmentation
abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) has emerged as an effective paradigm to alleviate the dependency on large-scale annotated data for 3D medical image segmentation. Large-scale foundation models, such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM), exhibit strong generalization on natural images. However, exploiting volumetric context efficiently in 3D data remains difficult, and transferring foundation models directly to medical imaging often yields substantial performance degradation due to the domain gap. In this paper, we propose HCCP-SAM2, a semi-supervised framework that integrates Hierarchical Cross-Slice Context Modeling and Class-Aware Prompting with SAM2 for 3D medical image segmentation. First, we introduce a Hierarchical Hybrid Attention (HHA) mechanism. This hierarchical design efficiently fuses cross-slice context while preserving both fine-grained features and maintaining computational efficiency. Second, we design a Class-aware Promptable Embedding (CPE) module that automatically generates high-quality prompts for the SAM2, significantly enhancing pseudo-label reliability. Third, we propose an Uncertainty-guided Hybrid Distillation (UHD) strategy, which enables the student network to dynamically learn from the SAM2 teacher based on its predictive uncertainty, facilitating efficient and robust knowledge transfer. Extensive experiments on multiple public 3D medical segmentation datasets demonstrate that our proposed model significantly outperforms state-of-the-art semi-supervised methods.

title: MVF-XT: An interpretable multi-view fusion network based on cross-attention for fMRI analysis
abstract: Deep learning models have shown promising performance in analyzing functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data for brain disorder identification. However, most approaches focus on single or dual measures with limited cross-view interaction, failing to fully capture information across time series (TS), static functional connectivity (sFC), and dynamic functional connectivity (dFC). Moreover, interpretability relies primarily on qualitative visualization rather than quantitative assessment. Thus, we propose MVF-XT, an interpretable multi-view fusion Transformer that integrates all three fMRI measures through explicit cross-view interaction. Unlike conventional patch embedding designed for images, we introduce connectional patch embedding (CPE) that preserves the ROI-aligned semantic structure of functional connectivity matrices. Based on CPE, a static-dynamic cross-attention (SDCA) module is designed to enable bidirectional information exchange between sFC and dFC, allowing them to mutually enrich each other. The TS view is processed through a temporal Transformer to capture global temporal dynamics. These three view-specific representations are then concatenated and fed to a classification head for final prediction. To understand how the model makes these predictions and to validate the neurobiological plausibility of learned patterns, we introduce two quantitative interpretability methods: Difference Alignment (DiA) correlates model decisions with group-level connectivity differences, while Physiological Relevance (PR) assesses associations with behavioral measures. MVF-XT achieved the highest classification accuracies of 77.20%, 88.12% and 60.54% on an in-house dataset (Obesity) and two publicly available datasets. For interpretability analysis on Obesity, DiA and PR quantitatively demonstrate that MVF-XT better captures neurobiologically relevant patterns than existing methods, achieving correlations of r=0.29 with group differences and r=0.10 with body mass-index.

title: A review of image-based sensorless force estimation in robotic-assisted medical interventions
abstract: The recent advancements in surgical robots highlight the critical importance of accurately sensing force feedback. At present, the realization of force feedback by robots mainly relies on force sensors, but there are many limitations in the use of force sensors in the field of surgical robots. For this reason, researchers have conducted studies on image-based force estimation methods, especially those combining deep learning with vision. These image-based force estimation methods have received increasing attention due to their great potential in force feedback in robotic surgery. Therefore, this paper aims to review and summarize these image-based force estimation methods, point out the current challenges and future development trends in this field, inspire more researchers to devote themselves to this research field, and promote the further development of this field.

title: Semantic alignment brain diffusion: Decoding realistic visual perception from fMRI
abstract: Recent advances in image generation have enabled the reconstruction of realistic natural images from brain activity, marking a major step forward in decoding visual content. However, due to the brain’s complex visual representations, fMRI noise, and data scarcity, existing methods struggle to preserve semantic fidelity between reconstructions and original stimuli. To address this, we propose Semantic Alignment Brain Diffusion (SABD), a novel three-stage framework for semantically accurate visual reconstruction. We leverage a pre-built image feature library to mimic human cognitive priors and improve semantic accuracy. First, we align fMRI patterns with image semantic space via cross-domain contrastive learning. Second, we retrieve category priors for the aligned fMRI embeddings using the nearest-neighbor search in a pre-built image prior library. Finally, the pre-trained versatile diffuser is used to generate high-fidelity perceptual images based on the retrieved semantics and the initial reconstruction. Experimental results demonstrate that SABD achieves reliable natural image reconstruction and surpasses existing advanced methods in both qualitative and quantitative evaluations.

title: Strengthen the weak, align the strong: A federated enhanced iterative learning framework for cross-machine fault diagnosis
abstract: In industrial fault diagnosis, privacy regulations and commercial confidentiality hinder cross-client data sharing, leading to decentralized data silos across different enterprises. Federated Learning (FL) offers a promising paradigm to address this issue by enabling collaborative model training without raw data exchange, thereby overcoming the fundamental barrier of data inaccessibility. Nevertheless, practical deployments face two key challenges: (i) non-IID feature distributions and (ii) client-local missing-label fault modes. These challenges limit the effectiveness of conventional parallel federated aggregation, motivating a more interactive communication paradigm among clients. Hence, we propose a Federated Enhanced Iterative Learning (FedEIL) framework for cross-machine fault diagnosis, which adopts an iterative federated communication scheme that enhances information exchange and alleviates feature shifts caused by non-IID distributions. Moreover, we propose a Progressive Weighted Fusion (PWF) algorithm that adaptively adjusts aggregation weights to enhance feature extraction and global generalization, thereby improving recognition under client-local missing-label fault types. Experiments on multiple industrial datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior cross-machine accuracy under client-local missing-label fault types while preserving data privacy, outperforming competing state-of-the-art FL approaches, and demonstrating its superiority for cross-client deployment in Internet of Things (IoT) scenarios.

title: FFK-net: A feature fusion-based kolmogorov-arnold network for liver tumor segmentation
abstract: Liver tumor segmentation plays a crucial role in the diagnosis and treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma. However, due to the blurry boundaries of liver tumors and their significant variations in shape, size and location, achieving accurate and automated tumor segmentation remains challenging. To address these challenges and achieve precise segmentation of liver tumors in complex CT images, we propose a novel feature fusion-based Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (FFK-Net) for automated segmentation of liver tumors in CT images. Specifically, the proposed framework incorporates a Tokenized KAN (TK) block within the encoder-decoder structure to reduce model complexity and enhance computational efficiency. Additionally, a Multi-DwConv and Spatial Attention Module (MSAM) is designed and incorporated into the skip connections to extract global contextual information of liver tumors and enhance features pertinent to liver tumor segmentation. To further enhance the edge features of liver tumors, a comprehensive feature fusion region is configured at the deepest level of the network. Extensive experiments conducted on the LiTS and MSD datasets demonstrate that FFK-Net effectively segments liver tumors from CT images, achieving superior accuracy compared to other state-of-the-art methods.

title: CARDxnosis: Anatomico-clinical knowledge-driven explainable network with multi-domain information fusion for ECG diagnosis and report generation
abstract: Electrocardiography (ECG) is indispensable for diagnosing cardiovascular diseases; however, accurate interpretation remains challenging due to waveform complexity and limited annotated datasets. We propose CARDxnosis, an anatomico-clinical knowledge-driven deep learning framework, that integrates anatomical lead grouping with attention mechanisms to capture clinically meaningful relationships among ECG leads. The architecture employs two encoders: one dedicated to learning spatio-temporal patterns from raw signals, and another that extracts quantitative waveform descriptors and frequency-domain representations generated through Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD). A cross-attention fusion module integrates these complementary encodings into a unified representation. Moreover, explainable AI guidance is incorporated into the training process, wherein model learning is augmented through the use of region-level annotations of abnormal ECG segments. This guidance, validated on a subset of strategically annotated data, demonstrates that embedding interpretability within the optimization framework enhances both predictive accuracy and clinical trust, although its broader application remains constrained by substantial annotation requirements. Additionally, the framework incorporates an automated ECG report-generation scheme powered by large language models (LLMs) that translate predictions into structured human-readable clinical interpretations. Validated across four benchmark datasets, CARDxnosis achieves multilabel accuracies of 78.73% (CPSC), 70.69% (Chapman), 35.78% (Georgia), 53.09% (PTBXL), and multiclass accuracies of 82.24% (CPSC), 95.17% (Chapman), and 67.69% (Georgia). Visualizations using t-SNE and Grad-CAM further confirm that the model learns robust and clinically interpretable features. Despite the challenges of full clinical integration, this work provides a reliable and explainable foundation for automated ECG analysis.

title: Scribble consistency match and pixel-level prototype contrastive calibration for weakly supervised medical segmentation
abstract: In medical image segmentation tasks, fully annotated training data are expensive and scarce. In contrast, scribble annotations, as a form of weakly supervised labeling, are more accessible than full annotations and have a wide range of applications in medical image analysis. However, due to the sparsity of scribble annotations, training segmentation models with limited annotations still faces considerable challenges. This paper proposes a novel framework, FW2SS (From Weak Scribble to Strong Segment), which employs Scribble Consistency Match and Pixel-Level Prototype Contrastive Calibration for image segmentation. The Scribble Consistency Match technique integrates consistency learning of both network and input perturbation, dynamically generating pseudo-labels to supervise predictions across different perturbed views, effectively enhancing the model’s ability to learn shape information. The Pixel-level Prototype Contrastive Calibration technique uses high-confidence pixels predicted by the weakly perturbed view to construct feature prototypes, which are then calibrated against the pixel features from the strongly perturbed view through contrastive learning. This technique improves inter-class separability and intra-class consistency to enhance boundary detail segmentation. The method is evaluated on two public datasets, ACDC and MSCMRseg, and the experimental results demonstrate a significant improvement in segmentation performance.

title: GraphPharm-X: A cross-modal graph transformer for context-aware drug interaction extraction from clinical text
abstract: Interaction detection based on clinical literature is important to pharmacovigilance and precision medicine. Nevertheless, the modern methods have difficulties with the complex semantic relationships of the drugs and their molecular mechanisms in unstructured text. GraphPharm-X is the proposed novel cross-modal graph transformer that combines both biomedical knowledge graphs and context-rich text embeddings to extract drug interactions in medicine through context-specific and representative text embeddings, respectively. This model is based on the molecular graph representations, pharmacokinetic rule encodings, and sentence-level semantic contexts and combines them with the help of a graph-guided attention mechanism. GraphPharm-X achieves state-of-the-art results based on the MEDLINE abstract and DrugBank entity annotation using the SemEval-2013 DDI corpus and is known to produce a 94.2% F1-score on known drug pairs and generalizes well to unknown interactions. The graph-guided attention module is effective in doing that, matching molecular structures with interaction triggers and where they are specific in detection of mechanism-specific interaction as inhibition of metabolism, competitive absorption, and synergy. The model is proved to be practically useful to automated pharmacovigilance systems by experimental support in a variety of clinical applications. Our strategy is 12.3% better than baseline transformer models with computational efficiency to implement in clinical information systems.

title: DCFANet: Merging dynamic context clustering mamba and context-to-focus attention for medical image segmentation
abstract: Motivation: Medical image segmentation has become indispensable for clinical diagnosis, preoperative planning, and anatomical investigation. However, existing methods often fail to accurately delineate tiny lesions with multiple targets, complex morphologies, and indistinct boundaries. The core issue lies in their insufficient modeling of fine-grained local spatial relationships and inadequate integration of cross-scale semantic information. These deficiencies prevent the models from capturing subtle structures and edges, ultimately reducing segmentation accuracy. Description: To address the above problems, we propose a medical image segmentation method, DCFANet, based on dynamic context clustering Mamba and context-to-focus attention, which enhances local spatial modeling and cross-scale semantic integration to capture complex boundaries and fine structural details. Specifically, the dynamic context clustering Mamba module mainly comprises the local-global information aggregation module and the dynamic context clustering layer. First, the local-global information aggregation module can adaptively fuse fine-grained textures with high-level semantic features to enhance the representation of lesion boundaries and microscopic structures. Second, the dynamic context clustering layer dynamically partitions image tokens into subregions and performs adaptive clustering within each subregion. This enables region-specific feature interactions that preserve local spatial consistency and capture subtle structural variations. Finally, the context-to-focus attention module can achieve precise alignment and semantic fusion of features between the encoder and decoder. Results and conclusion: Extensive experimental evaluations on five diverse medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate that DCFANet consistently achieves superior performance compared to existing methods, validating its wide applicability and exceptional generalization ability.

title: FMIN: A flexible multimodal iterative fusion network with geometry-aware positive noise alignment for drug–target interaction prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interactions (DTI) and binding affinities (DTA) is crucial for accelerating drug discovery. While multimodal deep learning methods have shown promise, existing approaches suffer from rigid architectures that require predefined modality sets and cannot handle missing data, as well as superficial fusion mechanisms that fail to capture complex inter-modal relationships. Moreover, conventional methods treat inter-modal variance as detrimental noise, discarding valuable complementary information. To address these limitations, we propose FMIN, a Flexible Multimodal Iterative fusion Network with Geometry-Aware Positive Noise Alignment for drug-target interaction prediction. FMIN employs a flexible cross-attention mechanism that accommodates any number of input modalities and remains robust to missing data by dynamically skipping unavailable modalities. Its iterative fusion module progressively refines feature representations through multiple layers, capturing higher-order interactions between modalities. Additionally, we introduce a geometry-aware alignment strategy that reframes inter-modal variance as positive-incentive noise, leveraging parallelotope volume minimization to preserve beneficial modality diversity while ensuring semantic consistency. Extensive evaluations on four benchmark datasets show that FMIN achieves competitive performance in both DTI classification and DTA regression tasks, with superior performance in challenging leave-one-out scenarios and strong robustness to missing modalities. Case studies demonstrate FMIN’s practical utility and interpretability in identifying novel drug candidates.

title: Random graph construction-based hierarchical attention multi-task graph convolution network for sEEG SOZ identification
abstract: Stereoelectroencephalography (sEEG) is a key technique for accurately identifying the seizure onset zone (SOZ) in refractory epilepsy. Existing studies predominantly rely on specific cortico-cortical evoked potential (CCEP) response patterns from sEEG to construct graph data for network training. This limits the trained network to relying on one-sided response patterns within specific frequency bands for SOZ representation, thereby leading to suboptimal performance. In this paper, we propose a random graph construction method that builds graphs by randomly selecting combinations of node features across different frequency bands and connectivity relationships derived from the response patterns of different brain regions, thereby enabling the model to leverage diverse response patterns for learning SOZ-related representations. Moreover, to fully exploit the rich information inherent in diverse epilepsy-related tasks for SOZ identification, we propose an upstream-downstream multi-task learning (MTL) framework. Current studies on EEG-based epilepsy MTL have primarily focused on constructing complex shared networks. However, directly applying these methods as upstream MTL frameworks may result in an inability to capture important detailed information from upstream inner tasks, as well as the complementary information between tasks. To address the above issue, we further propose a hierarchical attention multi-task graph convolution network (HAMTGCN), where the upstream network, hierarchical attention MTL (HAMTL), designs attention blocks to capture important detailed information within each task and introduces shared representation weighting to facilitate the complementary information exchange between tasks. This design enables the downstream task to benefit from comprehensive epilepsy-related information learned from the upstream HAMTL for SOZ identification. Extensive experiments and thorough analyses are conducted on a self-built sEEG epilepsy dataset to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method not only achieves superior performance in identifying the SOZ for each patient, but also exhibits notable interpretability and generalizability, highlighting the potential clinical applicability of the proposed method.

title: Cross-sensor collaborative distillation with dynamic competitiveness balancing for fault diagnosis under imbalanced missing data
abstract: Multi-sensor fault diagnosis often suffers from imbalanced missing data rates, which can bias learning toward sensors with higher data availability and degrade diagnostic performance. This paper proposes a cross-sensor collaborative distillation framework with dynamic competitiveness balancing to address this problem. The framework transfers shared diagnostic knowledge across sensors through signal-level logit alignment and semantic-level prototype and distribution matching, while a competitiveness balancing mechanism adaptively regulates sensor contributions during training based on their relative learning progress. By suppressing the dominance of low-missing-rate sensors and preventing the marginalization of high-missing-rate sensors, the proposed method enables balanced multi-sensor representation learning. Experiments on drive motor fault diagnosis datasets demonstrate improved accuracy and robustness under uniform and non-uniform missing data conditions compared with existing methods.

title: DELTAT-SNN: An efficient dynamic execution latency tuning through adaptive timestep SNN for patient-specific multifunctional seizure monitoring
abstract: Medical edge devices for seizure monitoring contribute to ensuring patient safety. These devices face energy limitations due to being battery-powered. Neuromorphic systems based on Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), which are more energy-efficient than commonly used Artificial Neural Network (ANN)-based systems, address these energy limitations. However, such systems currently face challenges in spike-based encoding, timestep optimization and multifunctional integration with detection and prediction. This paper presents a neuromorphic system to address these problems. The electroencephalogram (EEG) signal is processed by Level Crossing (LC)-sampling, enabling spike-based encoding while facilitating integration into neuromorphic systems due to its simple and efficient sampling architecture. The SNN is trained with a Dynamic Execution Latency Tuning through Adaptive Timestep (DELTAT) algorithm, which effectively reduces the timestep, thereby reducing the execution latency of the system and enhancing the cross-validation efficiency. The multifunctional SNN accelerator is implemented based on a reuse strategy, which decreases computations and resource overhead, further reducing power consumption and latency. We evaluate DELTAT-SNN on the CHB-MIT dataset, achieving a 60.27% reduction in training time and a 90% reduction in timestep. We further conducted experiments on the Siena and Kaggle datasets to evaluate the model’s generalization ability, achieving competitive performance compared to ANNs. Validated with Artix-7 FPGA, the SNN accelerator can achieve a power consumption of 0.181 W, a latency of 5.77 ms, and an energy consumption of 1.04 mJ for multifunctional seizure monitoring.

title: DSBRD: A dual-stream neural network based on novel residual convolution and dynamic pre-activation convolution for bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Mechanical bearing fault diagnosis is crucial for the safe and stable operation of industrial systems. However, in the face of noise or redundant information interference in real-world industrial environments, existing diagnostic methods still face limitations in terms of the autonomy of core fault feature extraction, flexibility of nonlinear mapping, and comprehensiveness of feature fusion. Therefore, this paper proposes a dual-stream neural network (DSBRD) based on novel residual convolution and dynamic pre-activation convolution. By integrating core components such as the proposed Residual Convolution (ResConv), Dynamic Pre-Activation Convolution (DPAConv), and Dual-Stream Feature Fusion Structure (DFFS) into the basic building units (DSBRD layer) of the network backbone, the model effectively enhances the robustness of diagnostic performance. Specifically, ResConv autonomously captures the core fault features most contributive to the diagnostic task through separation and recombination mechanisms. Meanwhile, DPAConv performs dynamic nonlinear mapping based on the specificity of different local fault modes through dynamic pre-activation operations, strengthening the model’s ability to express complex nonlinear relationships. Finally, DFFS leverages two novel convolutions to form the DSBRD layer, aiming to achieve multi-level feature fusion and abstract representation through feature channel dimension transformations (expansion and compression). Comparative experiments with the latest methods on mechanical bearing fault datasets and component fault diagnosis datasets demonstrate that DSBRD offers competitive performance, strong anti-interference robustness, and task generalization ability. Additionally, ablation experiments fully validate the contribution of the core components.

title: BANet: A network based on bridge structures and attention mechanisms for EEG decoding
abstract: In recent years, deep learning techniques for motor imagery (MI) electroencephalography (EEG) decoding have shown great potential for advancing brain–computer interfaces (BCI). However, non-linearities and subject differences in EEG signals negatively impact the robustness, applicability, and generalization of MI-EEG decoding, hindering BCI development. This paper proposes a novel network based on Bridge structures and Attention mechanisms (BANet). Inspired by transformer architectures, BANet incorporates multiple innovative Bridge blocks to extract temporal features of EEG signals from both local and global perspectives. These blocks model complex temporal relationships, enabling BANet to leverage information from diverse angles and enhance decoding performance. Additionally, attention mechanisms and inception architecture are employed to focus on and extract EEG features across multiple dimensions and scales, further optimizing the utilization of temporal-spatial features. In various validation experiments, BANet demonstrates superior performance compared with recent representative deep learning methods, confirming its effectiveness in extracting local and global temporal and spatial features and its potential for developing robust BCI applications.

title: Semantically-guided dual-branch prototypical network with dynamic margin for few-shot industrial fault diagnosis
abstract: Recently, metric-based meta-learning approaches have demonstrated the potential to address few-shot fault diagnosis (FSFD). However, existing methods suffer from two main limitations: 1) single-modality reflects only a partial representation of the fault state; 2) insufficient discriminability due to inflexible margin modeling. To address these problems, this study proposes a novel semantically-guided dual-branch prototypical network (SDPN) that synergistically integrates a sensor branch for learning prototypes and a textual branch for learning semantic knowledge from fault descriptions. To improve the representation ability of prototypes, a semantic-prototype alignment module (SPAM) is designed to establish dual-modal consistency in the embedding space via a projection layer and a class-aware consistent loss. Furthermore, we propose a dynamic margin adaptation mechanism (DMAM) that calculates inter-class semantic relationships to adjust classification boundaries automatically, thereby quantifying the discriminative ability. Specifically, DMAM constructs class-level similarities between categories based on textual embeddings to generate adaptive margins, where the margin is positively correlated with the semantic similarity to enforce clearer separation. Experimental groups of varying difficulty are constructed based on the Tennessee-Eastman process and the semiconductor aluminum stack etch process. The comparative and ablation results, including mechanism analysis of SPAM and DMAM, collectively demonstrate the feasibility and superiority of the proposed method.

title: ASSDA: Adaptive subgraph sampling with dual-attention for drug-drug interaction prediction
abstract: Subgraph-based Graph Neural Network (GNN) methods have demonstrated exceptional performance in drug-drug interaction (DDI) prediction, which is crucial for avoiding adverse side effects arising from polypharmacy. However, the existing methods universally adopt predefined and static sampling strategies to construct subgraphs thus isolating the subgraph sampling from other components, which prevents the model from dynamically adjusting the sampling based on knowledge, consequently limiting the DDI prediction. In this paper, we propose a novel Adaptive Subgraph Sampling with Dual-attention (ASSDA), which establishes a co-evolution mechanism between subgraph sampling and encoding learning to adjust the sampling dynamically. Dual-attention (DA) consists of a node-level and a relation-level attention mechanism to identify key nodes and important relations within the sampled subgraphs. The former calculates the importance weights of different nodes within the same relation type, while the latter calculates the importance weights of different relation types. Furthermore, we design an Adaptive Subgraph Sampling (ASS) that iteratively feeds back the encoding results to the subgraph sampling for optimizing it, which enables ASS to adaptively extract the more relevant local graph structural information for the prediction target. Experiments on real-world drug datasets show that ASSDA achieves state-of-the-art performance.

title: Riemannian spatio-temporal graph neural network for enhanced cognitive load detection using EEG
abstract: Cognitive load detection using EEG signals is crucial for real-time performance monitoring in high-stakes environments, such as aviation, healthcare, and education. Existing methods, however, often fail to effectively capture the complex spatial and temporal dependencies inherent in EEG data. Recent approaches have leveraged graph neural networks (GNNs) for spatial modeling, but many overlook the rich covariance structure of EEG signals and neglect non-local temporal dependencies. To address these challenges, a novel framework, the Riemannian Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network (RST-GNN), is proposed for multi-class cognitive load detection based on electroencephalography (EEG). This method integrates Riemannian manifold filtering with temporal graph learning to model both spatial and temporal dynamics jointly. Specifically, EEG signals are filtered using Riemannian spatial filtering to extract discriminative covariance features, which are then represented as nodes in a temporal graph. A Graph-BiMap module is used to extract structured features from these nodes. A temporal attention mechanism is then applied to fuse window-level features, thereby enhancing the model’s ability to capture evolving cognitive states. Experiments on two publicly available EEG datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing models across four cognitive load levels, achieving classification accuracies exceeding 96% with low inter-subject variability. These results highlight the robustness of the proposed method and its effectiveness for reliable cognitive load detection.

title: Enhancing glioma segmentation with tumor-aware reconstruction: A two-step prompt-constrained approach
abstract: Accurate segmentation of glioma sub-regions from multi-modal MRI is essential for diagnosis, treatment planning, and prognosis assessment in neuro-oncology, yet it remains challenging due to the heterogeneous appearance and complex boundaries of tumors. To address this issue, we propose a novel two-step prompt-constrained framework that integrates tumor region reconstruction and segmentation to improve glioma segmentation performance. Specifically, the reconstruction branch is designed to capture prompt-constrained tumor priors, while the segmentation branch leverages the encoded prior features to enhance region discrimination. Based on this framework, we further develop two variants with UNet and UNETR backbones, incorporating prior-enhanced mechanisms to improve detail awareness and suppress false positives. Extensive experiments on the BraTS 2023 dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves overall better performance than standard one-step models and backbone-only baselines in terms of Dice score and Hausdorff distance. Visual comparisons show that our method effectively reduces internal tumor misclassification and external tissue over-segmentation while producing more precise boundary delineation. In addition, ablation studies confirm that the two-step design alleviates feature interference between reconstruction and segmentation tasks and performs better than shared-encoder one-step architectures. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides an effective and robust solution for automated glioma segmentation and highlights the potential of integrating prior information into medical image segmentation. Our code is available at https://github.com/JosephXing/pe-net.

title: Curvilinear structure-preserving unpaired cross-domain medical image translation
abstract: Unpaired image-to-image translation has emerged as a crucial technique in medical imaging, enabling cross-modality synthesis, domain adaptation, and data augmentation without costly paired datasets. Yet, existing approaches often distort fine curvilinear structures, such as microvasculature, undermining both diagnostic reliability and quantitative analysis. This limitation is consequential in ophthalmic and vascular imaging, where subtle morphological changes carry significant clinical meaning. We propose Curvilinear Structure-preserving Translation (CST), a general framework that explicitly preserves fine curvilinear structures during unpaired translation by integrating structure consistency into the training. Specifically, CST augments baseline models with a curvilinear extraction module for topological supervision. It can be seamlessly incorporated into existing methods. We integrate it into CycleGAN and UNSB as two representative backbones.
