Comprehensive evaluation across three imaging modalities: optical coherence tomography angiography, color fundus and X-ray coronary angiography demonstrates that CST improves translation fidelity and achieves state-of-the-art performance. By reinforcing geometric integrity in learned mappings, CST establishes a principled pathway toward curvilinear structure-aware cross-domain translation in medical imaging.

title: MM-DLFA: Multi-modal deep-layer fusion with local pyramid aggregation for Alzheimer’s disease classification
abstract: Accurate Alzheimer’s disease (AD) classification requires effective integration of complementary structural and metabolic information, yet many existing multimodal methods still insufficiently exploit deep cross-modal interactions and multi-scale local evidence. To address this issue, we propose Multi-Modal Deep-Layer Fusion with Local Pyramid Aggregation (MM-DLFA), an end-to-end framework that jointly leverages structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI), fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET), and a small set of structured clinical variables. MM-DLFA employs a dual-stream 3D backbone, a Deep-Layer Fusion (DLF) module for high-level cross-modal interaction with clinically conditioned channel modulation, and a Local Pyramid Aggregation (LPA) module for enhancing shallow multi-scale discriminative cues through top-down aggregation and lightweight attention. We evaluate MM-DLFA on three binary classification tasks (AD vs. CN, AD vs. MCI, and CN vs. MCI) under a complete-case multimodal setting on the combined ADNI-1 and ADNI-2 cohort, and further assess cross-dataset generalization using the ADNI-2 to ADNI-1 protocol. Under five-fold cross-validation, MM-DLFA achieves ACC=96.36±1.69% and AUC=98.81±1.14% on AD vs. CN, exceeding the strongest competing method by 1.53 percentage points in ACC and 0.17 percentage points in AUC. In the cross-dataset setting, MM-DLFA further obtains ACC=94.07±5.02% and AUC=98.79±1.72% on AD vs. CN, improving over the best baseline by 1.48 percentage points in ACC and 0.33 percentage points in AUC. The proposed method also delivers consistently strong performance on AD vs. MCI and CN vs. MCI, while interpretability analyses highlight brain regions that are consistent with established AD-related structural and metabolic alteration patterns.

title: Classification of Native and non-native songs, neutral music, and resting state of human brain from EEG-based auditory evoked potential using explainable features
abstract: Auditory evoked potentials (AEPs) provide a non-invasive method for studying auditory processing, with uses in cognitive monitoring and biomedical applications. Although there have been studies of music-based EEG paradigms, a clear connection between AEP features and interpretable neurophysiological mechanisms that differentiate complex auditory categories, such as familiarity and linguistic content, remains lacking. To address this gap, this study proposes an interpretable EEG-based framework for classifying native songs, non-native songs, neutral music, and resting states using physiologically meaningful features extracted from electroencephalographic signals, including time and time-frequency domain representation. The interpretability of the proposed framework is achieved at the feature level, where selected features and their importance are directly associated with known brain rhythms and cortical functions. These auditory categories facilitated the study in examining how familiarity, novelty, and emotional engagement distinctly influenced auditory evoked potentials. The findings indicate that delta brain rhythms can serve as markers for identifying AEPs to auditory stimuli, an exploration conducted for the first time to our knowledge. The extracted features show distinct cortical engagement patterns during music-evoked activity. Using this, we reliably distinguish native songs, non-native songs, neutral music, and resting-state activity, with an average accuracy of 97.5% using a random forest classifier. Empirical mode decomposition further reveals intrinsic mode functions that enable precise identification of the P300 component within auditory evoked responses. The framework achieved 76.36% average accuracy across all binary LOSO comparisons with SVM, peaking at 84.86% for native vs. resting tasks. The proposed framework can monitor delta-band cortical responses during music listening, which can aid meditation, neurofeedback, and rehabilitation by tracking auditory engagement and relaxation.

title: Scale-aware modulation network for unsupervised medical anomaly detection
abstract: Unsupervised Medical Anomaly Detection (UMAD) aims to detect focal abnormalities by learning only from normal samples. However, previous methods heavily rely on static feature extraction and uniform reconstruction paradigms, failing to handle the extreme scale variations of medical lesions, which lead to significant performance degradation. To address this issue, we propose a Scale-Aware Modulation Network (SAMN). We designed a Scale-Aware Modulation Module (SMM), which utilizes a differential scale-aware scoring module to dynamically incorporate results from different receptive fields, thereby adapting to different abnormal scales. Additionally, we employed a Feature-Enhanced Bottleneck (FEB) to refine the fused encoder features through spatial and channel attention, and combined the Scale-Sensitive Mixture of Experts (SSMOE) to restore the normal patterns of specific scale anomalies. We evaluate our work on three datasets. SAMN achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) results on the Brain Tumor and ISIC datasets, outperforming SOTA methods by 3.34% and 2.35% respectively, while maintaining competitive performance on the RSNA dataset.

title: The fault diagnosis design based on concatenated neural network with self-attention mechanism and data preprocessing
abstract: Prognosis and health management(PHM) for machine is a crucial area in automation technology, which is continuously focused on as the model training and data manipulation is swiftly developed. Traditional model for PHM generally consists of diverse aspects like vision, acoustics, and feature division, which require reinforcement on specific methods employed by model. Motivated by this situation, a concatenated model of convolutional neural network(CNN) as well as multi-layer artificial neural network(MLNN) and bidirectional long short-term memory(BLSTM) network is proposed in this paper, where both local features and temporal patterns in the dataset are learned, as an improved alternative of traditional learning methods. In the construction process, the dataset is manipulated by covariance analysis to screen out input features with certain relevance. Then in the CNN design, convolution layers dealing with the product of kernel functions are proposed, with pooling layers inserted to scale down the size of input width, thus speeding up the learning process. Simultaneously, BLSTM, spanned by memory units, is designed in reversed temporal directions, where the self-attention mechanism(SAM) is embedded to incorporate temporal units by the designed weight matrix at attention head. To synthesize the learning process, algorithms to accommodate the proposed models are summarized afterwards. Moreover, the predictive ability of proposed models is tested and compared with existing NN models and ML algorithms via the statistical metrics in the diagnosis of a turbofan engine and optical fiber, respectively. The comparison results have shown that the robustness for nonlinear approximation and fault detection of machine systems is strengthened considerably by proposed models.

title: Automatic chronic kidney disease classification using enhanced gated recurrent unit model
abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) affects approximately 800 million people globally and causes gradual loss of kidney function, which leads to severe health complications. CKD diagnoses traditionally rely on clinical assessments such as blood tests, urine tests, biopsy, and imaging tests. Although effective, these approaches can be costly, time-consuming, and dependent on clinician expertise, which may limit early screening and accurate decision-making. Therefore, intelligent automated data-driven approaches are required to support timely, accurate and efficient CKD detection. In this study, we proposes an automated Deep Learning (DL)--based method for CKD classification. Initially, the CKD dataset is collected from the University of California Irvine (UCI) Machine Learning Repository. A Stacked Autoencoder (SAE) is used to select relevant features from the dataset. Following, the selected features are inputted into a proposed Enhanced Gated Recurrent Unit (EGRU) model to classify whether the data is CKD or Non-CKD. In the EGRU architecture, the tanh activation function is replaced with the ReLU to enhance the performance. Furthermore, The Improved Clouded Leopard Optimization (ICLO) algorithm is used to fine-tune the hyper-parameters of the EGRU model, ensuring optimal predictive performance. The proposed method is implementation using Python. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 98.75%, precision of 98.03%, recall of 100%, specificity of 96.66%, and F1-score of 99%, outperforming other approaches. The proposed method provides an efficient and reliable decision-support system for automated CKD detection.

title: SCPLoc: A weakly-supervised multi-instance learning framework for protein subcellular localization and heterogeneity profiling in single-cell immunofluorescence images
abstract: Protein subcellular localization is a key determinant for deciphering protein functions, and analyzing localization heterogeneity at the single-cell level enables a high-resolution perspective for functional elucidation. However, existing deep learning approaches are primarily developed for multicellular immunofluorescence images, where the coarse granularity of image-level protein subcllular location annotations and the long-tailed distribution of categories lead to limited prediction accuracy and application of the single-cell protein localization. In this study, we proposed a dual-branch deep learning model, named SCPLoc, for single-cell protein localization prediction based on weakly-supervised multi-instance learning with separate branches for global image-level and local single-cell predictions. To address the limitation of weak annotation for cells, we designed a class-aware adaptive trimming mechanism for pseudo-label refinement, which enhanced single-cell supervision through dynamically optimizing signals. In addition, an asymmetric loss and a consistency regularization strategy for feature perturbations were incorporated to mitigate the effects of annotation noise and class imbalance, as well as to enhance the feature robustness. Experimental results demonstrated that the SCPLoc achieved state-of-the-art performance, reaching a new record with a 58.36% mean average precision on the Kaggle 2021 benchmark test and reducing the cross-dataset fluctuation rate to 1.4%, improving both accuracy and robustness. Moreover, the built model was used to analyze single-cell protein localization heterogeneity and functional profiles in two independent datasets, providing a precise and generalizable computational tool for the single-cell heterogeneity profiling.

title: Adaptive gated diffusion model network for asymmetric modalities applied to cross-domain fault diagnosis
abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis technology based on multimodal signal fusion has demonstrated performance superior to that of single-modal approaches. However, in real-world industrial scenarios, target devices often fail to capture multimodal data as comprehensively as in laboratory settings due to cost or deployment constraints, resulting in missing modalities. Simultaneously, domain shifts caused by varying operating conditions further exacerbate the failure of models. To address this issue, this paper proposes an adaptive gated diffusion model network (AGDMN), in which the source domain contains labeled multimodal data, while the target domain has only unlabeled partial-modal data. AGDMN first performs feature extraction and disentanglement, separating shared and private features across modalities and domains to facilitate subsequent feature fusion and cross-modal generation. Then, a conditional diffusion model is trained on the source domain, using vibration features as conditions to learn the complex mapping for generating high-fidelity sound or current features. In the target domain, this model uses vibration features as input to reconstruct missing features. An adaptive gated fusion module is designed, which includes a task-aware scoring network that dynamically evaluates the contribution of each modality to the diagnostic task. Combined with a cross-modal attention mechanism, it generates adaptive gating weights to achieve robust weighted fusion of features. Experimental results on three cross-condition tasks demonstrate that the AGDMN model achieves superior performance.

title: Towards robust multimodal fault diagnosis of electromechanical systems with limited labeled data via cross-modal self-contrastive learning
abstract: Multimodal signals with comprehensive and complementary information have been successfully applied in fault diagnosis of electromechanical systems. However, the scarcity of labeled multimodal signal data, coupled with inevitable distribution shifts, poses a significant challenge to the effective training of multimodal diagnostic models. Moreover, the availability of all modalities cannot always be guaranteed during extended inference periods, which can further induce significant performance degradation. Therefore, this paper proposes a robust multimodal fault diagnosis method with limited labeled data via a cross-modal self-contrastive learning (CMSCL) model. First, heterogeneous multimodal signals are collected and preprocessed to extract unified fault characteristics across different modalities. Then, the CMSCL model is initially pre-trained through modality-masking self-supervised learning on unlabeled signal data and subsequently fine-tuned with limited labeled data for fault diagnosis. Finally, a missing modalities completion module is designed and integrated into the CMSCL model to further address the missing modality issue. Extensive experimental results on two public experimental rig datasets and a real-world industrial dataset from different electromechanical systems demonstrate the superior accuracy and robustness of the proposed method compared with state-of-the-art approaches.

title: HMP-Net: A hierarchical multi-prior network for brain tumor segmentation integrating physics, topology, and tumor dynamics
abstract: Precise brain tumor segmentation is essential for reliable diagnosis, treatment planning, and clinical follow-up. Despite recent progress in deep learning, most existing models remain predominantly data-driven and lack mechanisms to incorporate fundamental domain knowledge, including the physics of MRI acquisition, tumor morphology, and the biological dynamics of tumor progression. To bridge this gap, we propose HMP-Net, a theory-guided hierarchical multi-prior network that explicitly embeds these principles into the feature learning process. HMP-Net integrates three complementary levels of prior knowledge: (1) a shallow physical signal encoder that models inter-modal coupling in multimodal MRI data, (2) a mid-level topological analyzer that extracts Betti number–based structural priors through differentiable approximations, and (3) a deep tumor dynamics modeler that solves reaction–diffusion equations to capture biologically plausible tumor growth patterns. Extensive experiments on the BraTS 2021 and BraTS 2018 benchmarks demonstrate that HMP-Net surpasses state-of-the-art approaches, achieving average Dice scores of 91.55% and 86.58%, respectively. Ablation studies further validate the contribution of each hierarchical prior and show that the learned parameters maintain clear physical interpretability. These results demonstrate that embedding multi-scale, domain-specific priors into deep architectures substantially enhances generalization, interpretability, and clinical relevance, offering a new paradigm for knowledge-driven medical image analysis. The code will be available at https://github.com/kanglzu/hmp_net.

title: ReSHAPe: A redundancy-reduced SHAP-based feature selection pipeline for interpretable radiomics in biomedical image analysis
abstract: Handcrafted radiomic descriptors are widely used in biomedical image analysis, but classic radiomics pipelines often suffer from high feature redundancy and an underdeveloped, weakly principled feature-selection practice, which together can impair generalization and limit model interpretability. To address this, we introduce ReSHAPe (Redundancy-Reduced SHAP-based Evaluation), a two-stage, model-aware feature selection pipeline that makes SHAP-driven selection practical for radiomics. ReSHAPe first performs redundancy pruning by removing highly correlated features using Spearman rank correlation, retaining within each correlated group the descriptor with the lower absolute skewness. It then applies SHAP-based global importance to rank the remaining features and iteratively select a compact subset; an ensemble variant aggregates SHAP rankings across multiple classifiers to promote consensus and interoperability.We evaluate ReSHAPe on three MedMNIST v2 subsets (BreastMNIST, PneumoniaMNIST, BloodMNIST) using 285 handcrafted features and five well-known classifiers (SVM, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Extra Trees, XGBoost), comparing against univariate filters (ANOVA F-test, mutual information), SHAP-only selection, correlation-based filtering, and full-feature baselines. Across datasets, ReSHAPe preserves performance while drastically reducing dimensionality; on radiomic tasks, it is consistently competitive with SHAP-only selection (performance differences typically lower than 0.03), and it remains effective in the non-radiomic multiclass setting (maximum decrease lower than 0.04). Finally, the correlation pre-filtering stage markedly reduces SHAP overhead, which would otherwise require 200 additional model training/evaluation steps when applied directly to the full feature space.

title: Medical report generation via knowledge distillation and medical keywords
abstract: Medical report generation seeks to automatically produce diagnostic narratives from medical imaging data, thereby alleviating radiologists’ workload and improving diagnostic precision. As an emerging task at the intersection of neurocomputing and medical AI, it requires not only robust multimodal understanding but also biologically inspired information processing to mimic the integrative reasoning of expert clinicians. However, current multimodal approaches often fall short in capturing the intricate semantic interplay between visual features and medical text, leading to suboptimal cross-modal alignment and insufficient incorporation of domain-specific knowledge. To address these challenges, we propose a neurocomputing-inspired multimodal signal processing framework that leverages knowledge distillation to bridge the gap between large-scale vision-language models and lightweight, deployment-ready architectures. Specifically, we transfer the global semantic alignment capabilities of models like CLIP into a compact student network, preserving multimodal coherence while significantly reducing computational overhead. To enhance domain relevance, we construct a dynamic, TF-IDF-based medical keyword dictionary that guides the model in learning fine-grained diagnostic terms. A dual-branch decoder, driven by adaptive fusion mechanisms, integrates global visual-textual embeddings with locally salient keyword semantics. Extensive experiments on the IU-Xray and MIMIC-CXR datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, validating its effectiveness and efficiency in clinical neurocomputing environments.

title: TAD-ILFD: A transformer-guided dual-branch framework for incremental fault diagnosis
abstract: In industrial systems, the continuous variation in operating conditions and the accumulation of runtime data result in an increasing number of fault categories and samples, imposing higher demands on the adaptability of fault diagnosis models. This paper presents a Transformer-based Adaptive Dual-branch model for Incremental Learning in Fault Diagnosis (TAD-ILFD), designed for general incremental diagnostic scenarios. The proposed model integrates a dual-branch CNN feature extraction module, a Transformer-based dynamic attention fusion module, and an LSTM-based temporal modeling module. This architecture effectively balances new knowledge and existing knowledge, thereby ensuring sustained stability and mitigating catastrophic forgetting. The performance of TAD-ILFD is evaluated on the publicly available CWRU bearing dataset under two incremental learning settings: increasing fault categories and expanding sample numbers. Experimental results demonstrate that TAD-ILFD significantly outperforms mainstream approaches in terms of diagnostic accuracy, model stability, and resilience to forgetting, demonstrating its robustness and broad applicability in incremental fault diagnosis tasks.

title: An enhanced SOH prediction framework for lithium-ion batteries via CVAE-GRU architecture and projection theorem fusion
abstract: Rapid and accurate State-of-Health (SOH) prediction for lithium-ion batteries is critical to guaranteeing battery safety and reliability in diverse application scenarios. To address the challenges in SOH prediction, including the difficulty in capturing strong nonlinear characteristics and the limited generalization capability of single models, this paper presents an enhanced ensemble prediction framework via the integration of Conditional Variational Autoencoders (CVAE) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU). First, a multi-model prediction ensemble consisting of ten heterogeneous base learners is established to enable multi-perspective modeling of battery degradation features. Subsequently, the outputs of these base learners are fed as conditional inputs into a nonlinear fusion module. In this module, the CVAE characterizes latent probability distributions and mitigates noise interference, whereas the GRU captures the temporal dynamics and dependencies inherent in capacity degradation, thereby realizing the collaborative modeling of nonlinear features and temporal information. Based on the above, an output layer optimization mechanism is devised using signal space orthogonal projection theory. This mechanism aligns the prediction subspace with the genuine SOH subspace, improving the stability of weight distribution and reducing model bias. Five-fold cross-validation experiments conducted on the public MIT and XJTU datasets verify that the proposed framework achieves significant performance improvements over multiple mainstream methods on both datasets, with the root mean square error and mean absolute percentage error reduced by up to approximately 20% and 10.3%, respectively. In summary, the proposed method exhibits superior performance in prediction accuracy, generalization capability and stability, which validates its effectiveness and application potential for SOH prediction under complex degradation scenarios.

title: MedLAMA: Medical lesion-aware multimodal alignment
abstract: Medical vision-language alignment, which leverages images and corresponding reports, is essential for effective medical image analysis. However, current approaches often fail to precisely align the semantics between images and texts, resulting in inaccurate or incomplete diagnoses. In this study, we present MedLAMA, a lesion-aware vision-language alignment model that utilizes rich information and image-specific knowledge from both image and text to improve alignment through contrastive learning. Particularly, we highlight the following contributions. First, we design a component extractor using an LLM to simplify disease details from reports, reducing text complexity and improving multi-lesion image interpretation with minimal information loss. Second, we introduce a knowledge injector that enhances reports with disease-specific imaging details from external knowledge bases, enabling the model to grasp disease relationships and predict unseen classes. Third, we apply a lesion-aware attention sampling to focus the model on suspicious lesion areas before image–text alignment, requiring no additional annotations and improving generalization to new categories. Fourth, we implement a new asymmetric term loss to ensure high similarity for both matched image–text pairs and same-disease pairs, minimizing false negatives. We evaluate MedLAMA on datasets such as RSNA Pneumonia, ChestX-ray14, SIIM-ACR Pneumothorax, COVIDx and CheXpert, achieving top performance in zero-shot and fine-tuned classification, with a maximum F1 score improvement of 6.32%.

title: A brain-inspired SLAM system with multi-scale spatial cell model and visual temporal memory
abstract: Brain-inspired simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) has attracted increasing attention for robust and long-term autonomous navigation. However, existing methods still suffer from limited spatial encoding capability, insufficient robustness in visual place recognition (VPR), and erroneous spatial cell reactivation in familiar scenes. To address the above challenges, this paper proposes a novel brain-inspired SLAM system. A multi-scale spatial cell model is first constructed to extend the spatial encoding range and reduce encoding ambiguity in large-scale environments, which can improve the stability of spatial representation and long-term localization. Building upon this representation, a Hierarchical Temporal Memory (HTM) inspired predictive mechanism is employed to capture temporal dependencies in visual observations, enhancing the robustness of VPR under environmental variations. Furthermore, a scene memory driven spatial cell reactivation mechanism is developed to prevent erroneous spatial cell activation in familiar scenes and enhance consistency of cognitive map construction. Extensive experiments in both simulation and real-world environments validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, which significantly improves spatial encoding capability, visual recognition robustness, and trajectory accuracy. Quantitative results on the KITTI dataset show that the proposed system reduces the absolute trajectory error (ATE) by 65% - 92% compared to ORB-NeuroSLAM, with the lowest error reaching 0.51 m. Moreover, it maintains real-time performance of at least 15 Hz and achieves trajectory topology consistency comparable to ORB-SLAM3, comprehensively confirming its reliability and superior performance.

title: Lightweight medical diagnosis via uncertainty-aware fuzzy knowledge distillation
abstract: Overcoming limitations of static models in medical image classification, this paper introduces a novel student model. It employs an efficient fuzzy logic-driven knowledge distillation approach with dynamic weighting adjustment to address the inherent uncertainty and complexity of medical disease diagnosis. Unlike traditional methods using fixed distillation weights, our approach dynamically adjusts weights based on region confidence, allowing the student model to focus more on certain areas and less on ambiguous ones, thereby improving robustness against uncertainty. We significantly address computational costs. The compact student model (7.5 MB) ensures efficiency, while Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) intelligently selects the optimal teacher model from a pool of twelve pre-trained models, balancing performance and computational load. Evaluated on a challenging dataset of 15 diverse diseases (X-ray, MRI, skin, histopathological, endoscopic), the method achieved 96.09% accuracy. The model demonstrates high operational efficiency (test time: 2.96 sec, FLOPs: 5.15B). Interpretability was ensured using T-SNE and GRADCAM visualizations. Practical utility is shown through deployment in a real-time Android application for medical professionals. Results ensure the method significant improvement in robustness and accuracy, particularly in handling uncertain or noisy regions, making it a valuable tool for medical image analysis.

title: Multi-domain and source-free domain adaptation in medical image analysis: A review
abstract: Domain adaptation has become increasingly critical in medical image analysis, as it enables models to effectively address distribution shifts arising from differences in imaging scanners, variations in patient populations, and disparities in clinical protocols. After years of development, traditional single-domain adaptation methods have reached a relatively mature stage, yet they are also approaching a bottleneck, with increasingly complex and constrained applicability. To overcome these limitations, more advanced paradigms of domain adaptation have been continuously proposed. In response to data diversity and privacy restrictions, multi-domain adaptation and source-free domain adaptation have witnessed rapid progress in recent years. The swift emergence of these methods has created a fragmented and complex landscape, highlighting the urgent need for systematic synthesis to establish a cohesive framework and guide future innovations. This paper provides a dedicated joint review and analysis of recent advances in MDA and SFDA for medical image analysis. It divides the medical image analysis pipeline into five stages and systematically examines the methods developed for multi-domain adaptation and source-free domain adaptation. Through a critical review of recent studies, several key open challenges are identified. Finally, to further advance research in this field, forward-looking research suggestions for multi-domain adaptation and source-free domain adaptation are proposed.

title: Static-dynamic variability-aware brain network classification via attention-based interaction and fusion
abstract: Static functional brain network (sFBN) and dynamic functional brain network (dFBN) characterize brain functional states from different scales, respectively. Integrating their complementary information has become an emerging direction for brain network classification. However, most existing methods often overlook the inherent variability within the two types of brain networks, thereby failing to fully exploit the complementary information during the process of static-dynamic interaction and fusion. To address this issue, we propose a static-dynamic variability-aware brain network classification method utilizing variability-modulated attention mechanisms to perform static-dynamic interaction and fusion, which consists of three main stages. In the first stage, based on the constructed sFBN and dFBN, we propose a variability calculation module that obtains node variability and graph variability by quantifying node activity and window fluctuations, respectively. In the second stage, following node-level feature extraction, we propose a node-level static-dynamic feature interaction module that utilizes node variability to modulate the cross-attention weights, emphasizing complementary information in high-variability nodes. In the third stage, after graph-level feature extraction, we propose a graph-level static-dynamic feature fusion module that utilizes graph variability to modulate the self-attention weights, focusing on discriminative information in high-variability windows. Experiments on ABIDE I and ABIDE II datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior classification accuracies of 74.68% and 73.98%, respectively.

title: Manifold-SimCLR: Self-supervised contrastive representation learning on riemannian EEG covariance manifolds
abstract: Accurate decoding of motor imaging electroencephalography (EEG) is pivotal for noninvasive brain-computer interfaces, but remains challenging due to the low signal-to-noise ratio of EEG, strong intersubject variability, and the limited availability of labeled trials. We introduce Manifold-SimCLR, a geometry-aware self-supervised framework that learns discriminative EEG representations without relying on large labeled datasets. Raw EEG segments are first converted into symmetric positive-definite (SPD) covariance matrices and mapped to the tangent space of the Riemannian manifold by a log-Euclidean transform, enabling standard Euclidean optimization while preserving intrinsic geometry. A set of novel SPD-preserving augmentations—scaling, orthogonal congruence, and log-domain jitter—generates positive pairs for a temperature-scaled NT-Xent objective. The backbone encoder combines depthwise spatial filtering, residual temporal convolutions, and hyperspherical projection, producing unit-norm embeddings suitable for contrastive learning. Training is driven by MXOptimizer, an Adam-style update that projects gradients, performs adaptive steps in the tangent space, and retracts parameters onto the manifold. After self-supervision, a lightweight classifier is fine-tuned with a small labeled subset using a joint loss that selectively activates supervised cross-entropy. The resulting pipeline is end-to-end differentiable, parameter-efficient and compatible with heterogeneous public motor image datasets, providing a principled route toward robust and label-efficient EEG decoding.

title: Information-aware optimization for enhanced feature retention in medical image segmentation
abstract: Supervised learning for medical image segmentation often suffers from the information bottleneck, where task-irrelevant semantic features are progressively lost in hidden layers. This degradation limits generalization, especially in data-scarce clinical scenarios. To address this, we propose an Information-Aware Network (IAN) that explicitly controls information retention at both architectural and supervision levels. At the architectural level, we design a lightweight feature filtering module (FFM) that selectively preserves semantic features and suppresses noise across multi-resolution decoder pathways. At the supervision level, we transform the original binary annotations into a four-class task via a binary-to-multiclass transformation with double edge augmentation (B2M-DEA), enriching the learning signal. A tailored loss function incorporating superclass IoU and adaptive re-weighting further enhances learning near ambiguous boundaries. We empirically evaluate IAN across multiple modalities—including endoscopy, ultrasound, skin lesions, and brain MRI—achieving 84.4 average Dice and outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, we quantify the intrinsic dimension of hidden feature maps, demonstrating that our information-aware design enhances latent representation capacity and mitigates information loss. IAN also generalizes effectively to 3D segmentation tasks without architectural changes, offering a practical, scalable framework for robust medical image segmentation.

title: CADI: A cross-source alignment and dynamic knowledge injection framework for medical QA
abstract: Building a question answering system with professional knowledge understanding has become a research hotspot. In highly specialized fields such as medicine, the question answering task faces challenges such as complex terminology and strong knowledge dependence, forcing most methods to rely on additional domain-specific pre-training (e.g., BioBERT) over large-scale domain corpora to improve model performance. However, such methods are costly in computing resources and time. To this end, this paper proposes a cross-source alignment and dynamic knowledge injection framework CADI for medical question answering, aimed at enhancing model performance while significantly reducing the reliance on computationally exorbitant domain-specific pre-training. The CADI framework integrates two key mechanisms to achieve effective injection and fusion of multi-source medical knowledge: (1) A Cross-source Semantic Alignment (CSA) mechanism with Siamese structure aligns medical knowledge graph embedding and language model representation, which significantly reduces semantic deviation between multi-source embeddings. (2) A Dynamic Attention Knowledge Injection Network (DAKI-Net) is designed, which can adaptively adjust the fusion weight of structured medical knowledge graph embedding and definition embedding according to the context. Experimental studies on two authoritative medical question answering datasets, COVID-QA and PubMedQA, show that the proposed CADI framework has significant advantages in accuracy, flexibility and transferability of introducing medical knowledge. Notably, in certain medical QA tasks, CADI achieves performance comparable to, or even surpassing, that of domain-specific models when built upon general-purpose language models. This provides an effective path for constructing subsequent low-resource medical question answering and significantly reducing reliance on domain-specific pre-training.

title: Cross-subject EEG-based emotion recognition leveraging multi-source domain adaptation with curriculum leaning strategy
abstract: Recent research in EEG-based emotion recognition has demonstrated that domain adaptation effectively addresses the cross-subject challenge. However, traditional domain adaptation methods relying on a single source domain may suffer from negative transfer. Moreover, the strategy for selecting target domain samples during adaptation training critically impacts performance. In this study, we propose a curriculum learning-based multi-source domain adaptation approach to enhance cross-subject EEG emotion recognition. The method first extracts multiple features to comprehensively capture temporal, spectral, and spatial information embedded in EEG signals. Subsequently, we cluster source domains into an appropriate number of groups. Then, we integrate a curriculum learning strategy with a multi-armed bandit algorithm to progressively select target domain samples from easy to hard, facilitating multi-order moment matching with source domain samples. Our method was evaluated on the SEED and the valence dimension of the DEAP dataset, achieving the state-of-the-art performance compared with existing methods.

title: Cross-regional wind–solar power generation via dynamic multi-graph fusion and semi-supervised domain adaptation
abstract: Accurate wind-solar power generation is essential for renewable-dominated power systems, yet newly built stations lack sufficient historical data for reliable model training. Cross-regional transfer from mature stations offers a practical solution but faces three intertwined difficulties: label asymmetry between source and target domains, meteorological distribution shifts across climate zones, and time-varying task-dependent inter-variable interactions. To address these challenges, this study proposes DMG-SSDA, a dynamic multi-graph fusion and semi-supervised domain adaptation framework. Three complementary graph structures—correlation, learnable dependency, and physics-informed—capture distinct forms of meteorological variable relationships, and a temporal adaptive weighting mechanism produces task-specific fused adjacencies for wind and solar separately. A shared graph-temporal generator with embedded physical constraints maps fused representations to power outputs, while a semi-supervised domain adversarial module combining temporal adversarial encoding, multi-kernel maximum mean discrepancy, and maximum entropy regularization enables stable transfer with only 10% labeled target data. Experiments on three cross-climate transfer tasks from Heilongjiang to Hainan, China, against 11 baselines show that DMG-SSDA achieves the best wind performance (MAE 0.0061, R2 0.9980) and best solar performance (MAE 0.0077, R2 0.9954) in the normalized space, reducing wind MAE by 6.2% and solar MAE by 33.6% relative to fine-tuning. Ablation studies confirm the contribution of each component, and interpretability analyses reveal physically meaningful task-specific graph patterns. The proposed framework provides an effective and interpretable solution for cross-regional wind-solar generation at data-scarce newly built stations.

title: TumorAL: Evidence-aware active learning for 3D tumor segmentation
abstract: Active learning (AL) for 3D tumor segmentation aims to reduce the annotation cost of volumetric medical data by selectively labeling the most informative samples. Although this paradigm effectively alleviates labeling demands, existing methods typically rely on softmax-based uncertainty, which only reflects prediction confidence and overlooks the two fundamental sources of uncertainty: the intrinsic ambiguity of medical images and the knowledge deficiency of deep models. Specifically, TumorAL introduces a Dirichlet-based evidential modeling scheme to enable accurate estimation of both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. Based on this, we first design an Evidence Uncertainty Learning (EUL) strategy to expose the model’s blind spots and improve the quality of uncertainty signals. Secondly, we propose a Progressive Uncertainty-Guided Selection (PUGS) mechanism that preserves sample diversity while suppressing redundancy, by evaluating informativeness, similarity, and novelty in an evidential embedding space. Lastly, we introduce an Evidential Calibration Loss (ECaLoss) to regularize model confidence by aligning probabilistic outputs with evidential strength. Experiments on BraTS2018 and Liver datasets demonstrate that TumorAL achieves competitive segmentation performance with substantially reduced annotation effort, consistently outperforming representative active learning baselines under the same labeling budget. These results highlight the effectiveness of integrating calibrated uncertainty and redundancy-aware sampling for label-efficient 3D medical image analysis.

title: EIREstimator: A python toolbox for neural mass model-based estimation of excitation-inhibition ratio changes from EEG signals
abstract: The excitation-inhibition ratio (EIR) is a key neurophysiological biomarker reflecting the dynamic balance between excitatory and inhibitory neural activities. Abnormal EIR changes are associated with neurological disorders. The neural mass model (NMM), capable of reproducing cortical dynamics with physiologically meaningful parameters, is previously used for estimation of EIR changes from electroencephalography (EEG). However, such inverse estimation requires multiple customized programming steps. To streamline this process and improve accessibility, we developed EIREstimator, a Python-based open-source software with graphical user interface (GUI) for estimating EIR changes from EEG using NMMs. We designed the GUI so that users can conduct a full analysis pipeline comprising data import, signal preprocessing, model parameter configuration, EIR dynamic estimation, and results visualization without coding. Three estimation algorithms were implemented, i.e., variational Bayesian noise-adaptive constrained ensemble Kalman filter (vbcEnKF), particle swarm optimization (PSO) and 1DCNN-BiLSTM. Using epileptic EEG as a case, we illustrated the EIREstimator’s workflow. Application to sleep EEG further confirmed its effectiveness in identifying stage-dependent EIR patterns. Evaluations with simulated data showed that PSO was more robust to initial parameter uncertainty, vbcEnKF achieved higher accuracy and stability under noise corruption, and 1DCNN-BiLSTM algorithm could substantially reduce computational time while maintaining estimation accuracy. By incorporating three complementary algorithms within a standardized workflow, EIREstimator provides an accessible and integrated platform for NMM-based EIR estimation from EEG. Our software lowers the technical barrier for three algorithms, which facilitates reproducible analysis of EIR dynamics in both pathological and physiological states.

title: HiEn: Hierarchical ensemble learning for semi-supervised medical image segmentation
abstract: Medical image segmentation has seen growing interest in developing advanced learning paradigms, driven by scarce expert annotations and heavy reliance on domain expertise. However, existing methods frequently encounter performance bottlenecks due to insufficient modeling of cross-model (student and teacher) parameter interactions and inadequate cross-domain knowledge integration between labeled and unlabeled data domains. To this end, this work proposes a hierarchical ensemble learning framework for semi-supervised medical image segmentation. We devise a hierarchical modeling paradigm with dual-teacher constraints that captures complex mapping relationships between student and teacher models. Then we derive a unified computational framework that synergistically optimizes supervised and unsupervised learning objectives, implementing an alternating parameter update strategy for end-to-end training. Extensive experiments across surgical scenarios (e.g., Fetoscopy, Endoscopy) demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance compared to other cutting-edge works. Our code is available at https://github.com/jch3rn/HiEn.

title: Cascaded deep capsule neural network with geometry-aware transformer for efficient disease identification in Golden Nutri Cereal
abstract: Pearl millet leaf disease detection remains challenging due to variability in lesion morphology, illumination conditions, and background complexity, which often limits the generalization of existing deep learning models. To address these issues, this study proposes a Cascaded Deep Capsule Neural Network with a Visual Geometry-Grounded Transformer (C-DCapsNet-VGGT) for multi-class disease identification. The framework integrates edge-preserving pre-processing, multidimensional feature extraction, knowledge-aware segmentation, and geometry-aware classification to capture both local lesion characteristics and global spatial relationships. Rather than focusing solely on peak performance, extensive ablation and robustness analyses are conducted to evaluate the contribution of each module under varying conditions, including noise, blur, and cross-region data shifts. The results indicate consistent performance improvements across configurations, demonstrating the stability of the proposed architecture in handling real-field variability. While the model achieves high classification performance, the findings highlight that gains are primarily attributed to the integration of geometric reasoning and relational context modeling. Despite these strengths, the framework introduces increased computational complexity due to its multi-stage architecture and approximately 15 M parameters, which may limit direct deployment on resource-constrained edge devices without optimization. Overall, the proposed approach provides a robust and interpretable solution for pearl millet disease detection, with a focus on generalization and reliability under practical agricultural conditions.

title: Adaptive semi-supervised meta-learning with pseudo-label for multiple working condition fault diagnosis
abstract: To address diagnostic performance degradation in industrial systems arising from scarce fault samples, limited labeled data, and significant distribution shifts across operating conditions, we propose an adaptive semi-supervised meta-learning method with pseudo-label selection (ASML). First, data-driven variable relationships are integrated with expert prior knowledge to construct an entity–relationship knowledge graph, and a relational graph convolutional network is employed to learn structured feature representations with physical and semantic constraints. Second, a center-removal-based embedding regularization mechanism is incorporated to regularize the episode-wise metric geometry, thereby stabilizing prototype estimation and improving distance-based classification under cross-condition distribution shifts. Third, pseudo-label reliability is evaluated using instance-wise margins smoothed by an exponential moving average, and a task-wise dynamic threshold is employed to filter low-confidence predictions, reducing noisy pseudo-labels and error accumulation under cross-condition shifts. Experimental results on two industrial datasets demonstrate that the proposed ASML method significantly outperforms existing semi-supervised and meta-learning approaches in diagnostic accuracy and generalization under small-sample and multi-condition scenarios.

title: YOLO-DwSimAM: An improved YOLOv11 network for insect-pest detection in rice crop
abstract: Rice is one of the most important cereal crops which supports food security to billions of people across the world. However, it is vulnerable to several insect-pest infestations which significantly damage the crop and reduce the overall yield. Traditional pest management practices aim to minimize damage of crops relying on manual field inspection, which are labour-intensive, time consuming, and prone to human error. With recent advances in deep learning, automated detection frameworks like YOLO networks, have emerged as promising tools for real-time insect-pest detection for crops. In this study, we proposed an improved lightweight network named YOLO-DWSimAM, built upon the baseline YOLOv11 architecture. In the proposed network, a simple parameter-free attention module (SimAM) and a depthwise convolution (DWConv) are integrated into a lightweight unified block, DW-SimAM, which enhances the network’s feature extraction capability with reduced trainable parameters. An insect-pest dataset, consisting of 1721 images, was acquired from different rice fields and annotated with bounding boxes to locate the instances of insect-pests within the images. With only 1.93 million trainable parameters and 4.9 GFLOPs, the proposed YOLO-DWSimAM network achieved an mAP@50 of 0.851 on the test dataset, outperforming the baseline YOLOv11 architecture by 1.19%. Additionally, the proposed YOLO-DWSimAM network demonstrated strong performance on the edge device, especially Raspberry Pi 4, for rice insect-pest detection, achieving average inference speed of 0.67 s and FPS of 1.49 using input images of size 640 × 640. These findings validated that the proposed network achieved higher detection accuracy while being computationally efficient, making it suitable for real-time insect-pest management in resource-constrained agricultural environment.

title: Knowledge-guided attention fusion of multi-paradigm EEG for depressive episode detection
abstract: Improving the generalisation of EEG-based affective computing models remains a major challenge, partly due to the often-overlooked influence of experimental paradigms on neural representations. Most existing fusion techniques implicitly assume paradigm-invariant EEG patterns, thereby limiting their robustness in real-world mental health assessment. To address this issue, we construct a multi-paradigm EEG dataset comprising recordings from 28 individuals undergoing a depressive episode and 29 healthy controls across three canonical cognitive states: eyes-closed resting, eyes-open resting, and freely viewing a motion stimulus video. Our analyses reveal paradigm-dependent discrepancies between groups, highlighting the necessity of modeling cognitive-state variability. Building on this motivation, we introduce a knowledge-enhanced attention fusion framework that dynamically allocates weights across paradigms, frequency bands, and spatial channels. This hierarchical design enables effective integration of complementary neurophysiological information, producing a more stable and discriminative latent representation. The proposed approach is evaluated using multiple deep learning backbones. Extensive comparative experiments show that our method consistently outperforms three representative fusion baselines, while requiring significantly fewer trainable parameters than concatenation-based strategies. When integrated with a Conformer architecture, the model achieves an accuracy of 85.64% and an F1-score of 84.57%, along with an approximate 60% reduction in parameter count. In addition, the learned attention distributions provide interpretable insights into how different paradigms and neural features contribute to depression recognition. Overall, this work demonstrates the importance of paradigm-aware modeling in EEG-based depression detection and presents an interpretable, generalizable fusion mechanism that enhances feature-level integration in affective neural computing.

title: Representation-aware meta pseudo labeling for medical image segmentation
abstract: Segmentation is essential for applying artificial intelligence (AI) to challenges in medical imaging, and one of the most effective approaches is the use of U-shaped architectures. These architectures, with their balanced encoder-decoder structure, have proven highly efficient in both performance and design optimization. A significant challenge in medical AI, however, lies in leveraging the vast amounts of unlabeled data, given the high cost associated with generating labeled segmentation datasets. This study introduces a novel training framework designed to maximize the utility of unlabeled data by integrating representation learning with meta pseudo-labeling techniques into U-shaped models. For part representation learning, the method proposes a combination of visual features and instructional textual information to enhance the representation ability of the low-level features generated from the encoder of models, solving the limitations of traditional contrastive learning methods. The proposed approach not only enhances model performance but also offers a seamless end-to-end training process without incurring additional inference costs, making it a practical and scalable solution for medical image segmentation. Our method establishes a new state-of-the-art, demonstrating superior performance across the ACDC, ISIC 2018, and PH2 datasets. In comparative experiments, our approach consistently surpasses prominent contemporary methods in both self-supervised and semi-supervised learning.

title: Drift-aware experience replay for continual EEG-based disease recognition
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is essential for the early detection and supportive clinical diagnosis of neurological diseases. Owing to substantial inter-subject physiological variability, cross-subject EEG signals often exhibit complex distributional shifts, which severely degrade the generalization performance of models when deployed on unseen patients. Although existing continual learning approaches attempt to preserve historical knowledge through replay buffers, they typically fail to effectively balance the statistical representativeness and spatial coverage of buffered samples, and lack mechanisms for dynamic domain shift detection and buffer management. As a result, buffer redundancy accumulates and catastrophic forgetting is exacerbated. To address these challenges, we propose Drift-Aware Experience Replay (DAER) for EEG signal classification in cross-subject incremental learning scenarios. First, through the fusion of adaptive kernel density estimation and effective volume estimation of Voronoi cells, we explicitly model the local density and spatial distribution characteristics of EEG signals, enabling statistically representative and spatially covered sample selection. Second, we design a weighted-projection-based maximum mean discrepancy metric to dynamically monitor distributional shifts between incoming data and the historical buffer, thereby achieving adaptive domain drift identification. Finally, we establish a dynamic domain creation mechanism and an optimized buffer allocation strategy that ensures balanced and efficient knowledge retention under a fixed memory budget. Extensive experimental evaluations on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy improvement of 3.88% and reduces the forgetting rate by 3.92%, validating its robustness and practical effectiveness in non-stationary physiological signal processing.

title: Adaptive self-supervised learning for retinal disease detection in optical coherence tomography images
abstract: Accurate and cost-efficient screening of retinal diseases from optical coherence tomography (OCT) images is urgently required, yet large-scale expert annotation is prohibitively expensive and often unavailable. To address this bottleneck, we propose an Adaptive Self-Supervised Learning (ASSL) framework that learns highly discriminative representations from unlabelled OCT data and demonstrates strong generalization under extreme label scarcity. ASSL introduces three synergistic components: (1) an adaptive soft-relabelling mechanism that dynamically re-weights positive and negative pairs via uncertainty-aware confidence scores, mitigating false-negative noise inherent in instance-wise contrastive learning; (2) a variance-regularised contrastive loss that simultaneously maximizes mutual information between augmentations while explicitly enforcing non-zero feature variance and minimising dimensional covariance, effectively preventing representational collapse; and (3) a lightweight self-attention-equipped ResNet-34 that amplifies micro-lesion responses without increasing inference cost. Extensive experiments on two public retinal OCT benchmark datasets demonstrate that ASSL achieves competitive performance against strong self-supervised baselines under linear evaluation and few-shot semi-supervised protocols (1% and 10% labels). Our results show that ASSL advances the state of unsupervised OCT representation learning, yielding diagnostic accuracy comparable to recent self-supervised baselines and providing a further step towards scalable and annotation-efficient retinal screening.

title: DGCNet: A deep knowledge distillation framework for accurate gastric cancer detection with attention based DeepLabv3+ segmentation
abstract: Gastric cancer remains the major global health burden due to late diagnosis and the challenge of accurately identifying subtle lesions in endoscopic images. The existing deep learning approaches show enhanced outcome; still, has issues like high computational cost, noise sensitivity, and inadequate feature discrimination. To address the limitations, this research proposed the DGCNet, which is the unified model that utilized the enhanced lesion segmentation using the transformer-based knowledge distillation. The proposed model is designed with Cross-Guided Bilateral Filtering to suppress noise by preserving structural boundaries. Lesion regions are then segmented using the Improved DeepLabv3 + (ImDL3 +) model designed with Squeeze-and-Excitation attention for adaptive channel recalibration. For final classification, the Dual-Path Shuffle Convolutional Vision Transformer (DP-SCViT) based teacher model that transfers the multi-level contextual knowledge to the lightweight LDP-SCViT student using the adaptive distillation strategy that enables the robust detection with reduced computational complexity. The experimental evaluation using the the Kvasir-SEG dataset demonstrates that DGCNet achieved 99.12% accuracy, 98.97% precision, 98.84% recall, 99.07% F1-score, 98.47% specificity, and a mean squared error (MSE) of 2.19 respectively. The results indicates the suitability of DGCNet for reliable and computationally efficient gastric cancer detection in clinical settings.

title: Identifying neuroimaging biomarkers for neurodevelopmental disorders via cross-site multimodal brain network with temporal affinity graph
abstract: Multimodal neuroimaging–based diagnosis of neurodevelopmental disorders remains challenging due to three key limitations: coarse modeling of brain region associations that obscure disease-related topology, static multimodal fusion that fails to capture dynamic neural interactions, and cross-site data biases that hinder model generalization. To address these challenges, we propose TAGS-Net (Temporal Affinity Graph with Site-adversarial Network), a structured and dynamic multimodal brain network framework that achieves unified modeling and robust cross-site learning. TAGS-Net incorporates three core strategies: (1) group-level affinity graph modeling, which enhances disease-discriminative brain topology while suppressing redundant noise through functional brain region grouping; (2) temporal affinity graph–based multimodal fusion (TAGFMN), which integrates temporal and modal attention to enable adaptive fusion of imaging, functional connectivity, and phenotypic features; and (3) site-adversarial gradient learning (SAGL), which explicitly mitigates acquisition-related site bias while enforcing consistency across graph structures and modalities. Experiments on the ABIDE and ADHD-200 datasets demonstrate that TAGS-Net consistently outperforms existing methods in diagnostic accuracy and cross-site generalization, while reliably identifying key pathological brain regions. These results suggest that TAGS-Net provides a structured, dynamic, and interpretable paradigm for multimodal neuroimaging analysis, with strong potential for clinical auxiliary diagnosis and neurodevelopmental mechanism studies.

title: Dynamic feature arbitration and synergistic attention for high-fidelity brain MRI super-resolution
abstract: High-fidelity super-resolution (SR) of brain structural MRI (sMRI) is crucial for advancing neuroimaging research and clinical applications. However, existing deep learning approaches often struggle to simultaneously recover fine textures and maintain global anatomical consistency, largely due to insufficient integration of spatial and channel information. To address these challenges, we propose a three-stage cross-fusion network for brain sMRI super-resolution, consisting of shallow feature extraction, deep feature extraction, and image reconstruction. The deep feature extraction stage is built around two key modules. First, an Adaptive Gated Cross-Fusion (AGCF) block introduces an Adaptive Gated Cross-Attention (AGX) mechanism, enabling dynamic, bidirectional interactions between spatial and channel pathways. Second, we propose a Lightweight Sliding Window Attention (Lite-SWA) block for efficient multi-branch fusion. The SWA branch focuses on fine-grained anatomical textures, while the DSConv branch provides low-cost contextual support. We then use a lightweight interleaved channel–spatial fusion (ICSF) gate to adaptively merge the two branches. Together, these designs provide a balanced representation that preserves local detail without compromising global anatomical integrity. We evaluate the proposed model on a heterogeneous cohort of 2501 subjects from eight public datasets. Results show consistent state-of-the-art performance across multiple upscaling factors. Extensive ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the proposed modules, underscoring their potential to enhance the fidelity and clinical reliability of brain MRI super-resolution.

title: A comparative analysis of modern CNN and transformer architectures for multi-class retinal disease classification with statistical validation and explainability
abstract: According to World Health Organization (WHO) data, nearly half of the more than 2.2 billion people globally suffering from visual impairment are reported to have conditions that could be prevented with early diagnosis. The importance of automatically classifying common retinal pathologies from fundus images is increasing day by day to prevent a decrease in patients' quality of life, reduce the clinical workload of specialist physicians, and improve diagnostic accuracy. However, the vast majority of current studies focus only on binary classification or do not adequately question the statistical reliability of the proposed methods. This study focuses on a multi-classification task that includes common retinal diseases such as Diabetic Retinopathy (DR), Glaucoma, and Cataract, along with a Healthy category. 4920 original fundus images from the ‘Eye Disease Image Dataset,’ labeled by expert ophthalmologists, were augmented to 16,717 using various dynamic data augmentation techniques. The study comparatively analyzes the modernized CNN architecture presented here, ConvNeXtV2-Base, the Swin Transformer Tiny architecture with a hierarchical attention mechanism, and the EfficientNetV2-S architecture for the efficiency-focused model. The data was randomly stratified to prevent data leakage, with 85% training, 10% validation, and 5% independent test sets. The performance of the models was validated using McNemar testing, Bootstrap 95% Confidence Interval (CI), AUC, and Grad-CAM-based Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods. According to experimental results, ConvNeXtV2-Base achieved the highest overall performance with 97.14% accuracy and a Macro F1 score of 96.92%. Swin Transformer demonstrated the fastest inference speed in DR diagnosis with a 100% F1 score and 11.26 ms. In the designed ablation study, the data enhancement strategy resulted in a marginal gain of 5.22% in Macro F1 score. Furthermore, the statistical superiority of ConvNeXtV2 and Swin models was confirmed (p < 0.05) by the McNemar test. In conclusion, the integration of attentional mechanisms with modernized convolutional structures obtained in line with the findings demonstrates high sensitivity in multi-class pathology diagnoses. Statistical robustness and Grad-CAM-based visual approaches confirm that the presented deep learning framework can be evaluated as a reliable auxiliary vision system in clinical decision support systems. All source code and experimental protocols of this study are publicly available on GitHub: https://github.com/mblci/Retina-Diseases-DeepLearning-Benchmark.

title: PFD-VMUNet: A position-frequency domain synergistically enhanced model for medical image segmentation
abstract: In recent years, State Space Models (SSMs) represented by Mamba have rapidly emerged in medical image segmentation due to their global perception advantages under linear complexity. As a typical pure SSM architecture, VM-UNet has fully validated the application value of such methods in medical image segmentation tasks. However, it still suffers from weaknesses such as diminished spatial correlation, insufficient detail perception, and imbalanced encoding-decoding feature fusion. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an enhanced medical image segmentation model named PFD-VMUNet. This model designs a 2D-Hierarchical Heterogeneous Positional Encoding (2D-HiPE) to mitigate the weakening of spatial correlation caused by fixed scanning mechanisms. Concurrently, it constructs a Freq-Spatial Adaptive Attention Mixer (FSAM) to enhance the model’s representation of minute lesions and boundary details. Furthermore, it introduces an Adaptive Semantic-Detail Fusion Module (ASDFM) embedded with skip connections, which dynamically evaluates the feature contributions from the encoder and decoder to allocate weights reasonably, thereby resolving the semantic-detail imbalance in conventional feature fusion and optimizing the integrity of lesion regions and the sharpness of segmentation boundaries. On the CVC-ClinicDB and ISIC2018 datasets, PFD-VMUNet achieves mIoU scores of 89.29% and 81.55%, respectively, with DSC of 94.34% and 89.84%. These core metrics significantly outperform mainstream comparison models. Meanwhile, experimental results on the Autooral dataset for canker sore segmentation and the Synapse dataset for abdominal multi-organ segmentation also verify the excellent cross-scene segmentation performance and generalization ability of the model.

title: Interpretable refinement of medical foundation-model segmentation via visual thinking states and uncertainty gating
abstract: For computer-assisted diagnosis and treatment planning, accurate medical image segmentation is essential. However, segmenters based on foundation models frequently produce coarse predictions that are insufficient for clinical use. Current approaches for improving these outputs often require full or partial backbone fine-tuning, which increases computational demands and may compromise the pretrained model’s generalization ability, while many refinement methods do not explicitly address output-side correction. We propose VTS-MedSAM, a compact and parameter-efficient refinement framework based on a frozen MedSAM backbone, to overcome these limitations. This method uses visual thinking states as structured intermediate cues that capture region, boundary, and correction information to guide output-side residual refinement. These thought maps are supervised through a multi-task auxiliary objective, compressed into a latent state, and used to guide an uncertainty-gated residual update that applies corrections in ambiguous regions while avoiding over-correction in confident areas. We evaluate VTS-MedSAM on BUSI, ISIC-2018, and Decathlon-Lung, with additional within-modality validation on TN3K, ISIC-2017, and MSD Task09 Spleen CT. The proposed framework delivers consistent improvements over the coarse MedSAM baseline, increasing Dice from 93.25% to 94.33% on BUSI, from 92.44% to 96.14% on ISIC-2018, and from 71.10% to 82.11% on Decathlon-Lung. VTS-MedSAM demonstrates enhanced robustness to imperfect bounding-box prompts and achieves competitive performance against representative same-setting baselines while training only a compact refinement stage. These results demonstrate that frozen foundation-model segmentation can be enhanced through an interpretability-oriented post-hoc refinement mechanism, providing an efficient path toward higher-precision medical segmentation without full backbone fine-tuning.

title: RPA-former: A relative position-aware transformer with temporal tokenization for motor imagery EEG decoding
abstract: Motor imagery EEG decoding remains challenging due to the low signal-to-noise ratio, non-stationarity, and complex temporal dependencies of EEG signals. While convolutional neural networks are effective in capturing local temporal patterns, they are limited in modeling long-range interactions among EEG segments. Transformer-based models alleviate this limitation; yet, their performance depends strongly on how positional information is represented. In this paper, we propose RPA-Former, a relative position-aware Transformer with temporal tokenization for motor imagery EEG decoding. The proposed framework first converts EEG trials into token sequences through convolution-guided temporal tokenization, enabling effective extraction of local temporal features. The token sequence is then processed by a Transformer encoder with learnable relative positional bias in self-attention, allowing the model to capture pairwise temporal relationships among EEG tokens explicitly. By combining local feature extraction with global relation-aware sequence modeling, RPA-Former learns more discriminative representations for motor imagery classification. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves strong and competitive performance compared with existing baseline methods. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/DurraniBit/RPA-Former

title: COPC-Net: A collaborative optimization and prototypical contrastive network for semi-supervised medical image segmentation
abstract: Medical image segmentation is critical for advancing intelligent diagnostic and therapeutic interventions, however, precise expert annotations remain scarce. Consequently, semi-supervised learning has emerged as a significant research avenue in the field of medical image analysis in recent years. Nevertheless, current semi-supervised approaches, such as the mean teacher (MT) model, often encounter challenges related to feature distribution shifts between labeled and unlabeled data, stemming from inconsistencies in supervision signals. This issue constrains the further performance enhancements. To mitigate this issue, we design the Collaborative Optimization and Prototypical Contrastive Network (COPC-Net). The framework consists of three interrelated components. Initially, a dual-path decoupled prediction head is proposed to structurally differentiate between supervised and unsupervised signals, enabling dual-path collaborative optimization based on uncertainty. Subsequently, a prototypical contrastive learning strategy is constructed to generate class prototypes from reliable feature-level samples. This approach aligns feature distributions by utilizing prototypes as anchors, thereby enhancing feature discriminability. Furthermore, Class-Adaptive Entropy Filtering (CAEF) module is integrated to dynamically assess class difficulty based on prediction entropy and to adjust thresholds accordingly, thereby improving the pseudo-label reliability. Experiments conducted on multiple publicly available datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance under severely limited annotation budgets. Notably, with only 10% labeled data, the DSC on ACDC dataset reaches 91.20%, comparable to that of a fully supervised U-Net model. These findings substantiate the effectiveness of our method in utilizing unlabeled data, offering a viable solution for medical image segmentation in low-label scenarios.

title: DCCD: Dual-contrastive channel disentanglement for single-source domain generalization in medical image segmentation
abstract: Deep learning models for medical image segmentation often exhibit poor generalization performance due to domain shifts stemming from variations in imaging devices and protocols. Single-Source Domain Generalization (SSDG), which learns from only one source domain, offers a practical solution, particularly in the medical field. However, existing SSDG methods, especially channel-disentangling techniques, primarily address stylistic variations via contrastive learning between original and style-transformed images. These approaches often neglect the equally critical anatomical-structural shifts and discard potentially valuable residual structural information present in style features. Motivated by these observations, we propose Dual-Contrastive Channel Disentanglement (DCCD), which reformulates channel disentanglement from a style-only problem into a dual-shift modeling problem. Specifically, DCCD introduces a geometric transformation branch alongside the conventional style branch, creating a dual-branch architecture explicitly designed to handle both style and spatial shifts. This architecture is optimized using two complementary decoupling contrastive losses that encourage representations to be simultaneously style-robust and spatially-adaptive. Furthermore, we design a residual structure gain (RSG) module that utilizes latent structural cues from the disentangled style features to enhance the primary structure representation. We evaluate DCCD on multi-domain optic cup/disc segmentation (retinal fundus images) and prostate segmentation (T2-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging) benchmarks. Our method achieves state-of-the-art average Dice Similarity Coefficients (DSC) of 84.23% and 84.04%, respectively, demonstrating significant improvements over existing state-of-the-art methods.

title: Selective medical intelligence: Optimising AI-based breast cancer diagnosis classification through adaptive data filtering
abstract: Neural-network classifiers trained on small cytology datasets are vulnerable to overfitting when redundant morphometric predictors are retained. This study evaluates a mutual-information (MI) feature-pruning pipeline for fine-needle aspiration (FNA) breast cytology classification and extends safe-pruning arguments from squared-loss regression to categorical prediction under cross-entropy loss. Experiments were conducted on controlled synthetic datasets and on the Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer (WDBC) benchmark, which contains samples and FNA-derived nuclear features. On WDBC, MI filtering with threshold retained features and preserved full-data performance, with mean accuracy changing from to and ROC–AUC from to across seeds. The benefit was larger under reduced-data conditions: in the regime, accuracy increased from to and recall from to , while in the regime, recall increased from to , F1-score from to and accuracy from to . Synthetic experiments showed the same pattern, with pruning providing the largest gains when sample size was small and redundant-feature burden was high. SHAP analyses indicated that pruning concentrated attribution on cytologically plausible descriptors of nuclear size and boundary irregularity. These findings support MI-guided pruning as a reproducible preprocessing and interpretability aid for small-sample FNA cytology benchmarks, although validation on contemporary independent cohorts is required before clinical utility can be claimed.

title: CBP: Learning shared cognitive basis space and connectivity patterns for cross-cognitive-task brain dynamics modeling
abstract: Understanding the brain dynamics underlying diverse human cognitive tasks is crucial for advancing brain–computer interface technologies. However, two key challenges remain: (i) brain dynamics induced by different tasks exhibit substantial heterogeneity, and (ii) models must be interpretable, with components that can be directly linked to specific brain regions and task variables. To address these challenges, we propose an interpretable framework, termed CBP, which introduces cross-task shared and task-invariant constraints to enable unified modeling of brain dynamics across multiple cognitive tasks, supported by both theoretical analysis and empirical validation. Notably, CBP uncovers a stable set of cognitive bases and connectivity patterns in the human brain. Extensive quantitative evaluations and perturbation analyses demonstrate the robustness and reliability of these findings. Leveraging these findings, CBP generalizes effectively across multiple cognitive datasets, achieving accurate prediction of behavioral variables while providing mechanistic interpretability by identifying the key cognitive bases and connectivity patterns that drive these behaviors. Overall, CBP offers a principled framework for interpreting and predicting underlying neural mechanisms across diverse cognitive scenarios. The code is available at https://github.com/aaa493/CBP.

title: Neural advection-diffusion equation for long-term climate dynamics
abstract: Climate and weather prediction has traditionally relied on computationally demanding numerical simulations grounded in atmospheric physics, yet deep-learning approaches are emerging as transformative alternatives. Existing methods, however, are often purely data-driven and physics-agnostic, lacking explicit physics-aware structures and struggling to generalize. To address these challenges, we present the Physics-Aware Tensor Field Neural PDE (PA-TFNP), a forecasting framework that embeds rotation-equivariant tensor-field neural operators directly on the sphere, couples them with a numerically rigorous gradient operator based on spherical transforms and physically consistent boundary treatment, and augments the learned dynamics with diffusion terms derived from the atmospheric primitive equations. These innovations enable our model to achieve superior performance through physics-aware inductive biases and efficient learning.
