The proposed PA-TFNP achieves state-of-the-art performance in global and regional weather prediction, outperforming ClimODE by 78.92% on global hourly data while using significantly fewer parameters. On regional forecasting tasks, our model achieves consistently strong performance with a comparable number of parameters.

title: CARE-FL: Fair collaborative learning for rare disease detection in decentralized healthcare
abstract: In federated medical imaging, rare classes typically constitute less than 10% of the aggregate training data yet impose the most demanding diagnostic requirements, a fundamental tension that size-proportional aggregation cannot resolve. By assigning contribution weights proportional to dataset volume, conventional methods systematically suppress the influence of nodes rich in rare-class data, yielding globally accurate but class-inequitable models. This study introduces a unified Quality–Samples–Rarity (QSR) aggregation framework for decentralized federated learning that replaces size-proportional weighting with class-level fairness-aware mechanisms. The framework decomposes aggregation into three components and realizes them through two complementary instantiations, each specialized for a distinct operating regime. Decentralized Federated Learning with Multi-Criteria Distribution-Aware Aggregation (DFed-MCDA) applies pure per-class inverse-frequency rarity weighting to upweight nodes holding globally scarce samples. Class-Aware Rare-disease Equitable Federated Learning (CARE-FL) measures how much each node’s local training improves rare-class prediction beyond the current aggregated model and applies this improvement as an additive quality boost; the additive formulation reduces to standard size-proportional weight whenever the quality signal is uninformative, providing a structural lower bound on aggregation behavior. Because the aggregation weights depend only on validation-derived quality scores and sample statistics rather than on model internals, the framework is model-agnostic and applies to any architecture. Extensive experiments on four standard benchmarks and three medical imaging datasets show that the proposed framework improves accuracy by 2.1 percentage points and minimum F1 by 6.0 percentage points on histological tissue classification, and worst-case class F1 by 4.7 percentage points on retinal imaging, consistently outperforming FedAvg across all evaluated settings.

title: RGST: A relation-guided semantic transformer for dual-view drug–disease association prediction
abstract: Drug–disease association (DDA) prediction is a practical computational approach for accelerating drug repositioning. Although graph-based methods have achieved notable progress, several challenges remain. First, heterogeneous biomedical similarities are dense and noisy. Directly converting these similarities into graph edges may introduce spurious neighborhoods under sparse supervision. Second, existing predictors do not sufficiently model typed heterogeneous relations, limiting their ability to capture relation-specific semantics and long-range dependencies. Third, multi-source representations are often fused coarsely, which weakens multi-granularity representation learning. To address these issues, we propose RGST, a Relation-Guided Semantic Transformer for dual-view DDA prediction. RGST constructs two complementary heterogeneous graph views via Top-K sparsification and threshold-based edge filtering. This design preserves informative neighborhoods. RGST further initializes node features with truncated singular value decomposition (SVD)-derived structural priors and topological degree information. A head-wise relation-biased self-attention mechanism distinguishes drug–drug, disease–disease, and directional drug–disease association relations. Base, local, and global semantic representations are then fused through node-wise attention. Cross-view attention and contrastive alignment preserve complementary information across views, while a pairwise interaction predictor with focal loss addresses class imbalance. Experiments under a unified five-fold re-evaluation protocol show that RGST achieves the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and area under the precision–recall curve (AUPR) across all five benchmark datasets, with maximum improvements over the strongest competing baselines of 6.49 and 6.66 percentage points, respectively. These results indicate that RGST provides an effective framework for robust ranking-based drug–disease association inference.

title: Learning from semantic ambiguity: A dual-noise robust framework for EEG partial label emotion recognition
abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG)-based emotion recognition suffers from unreliable supervision: annotators disagree about subtle affective states, and EEG signals are inherently noisy. When formulated as partial-label learning (PLL), this setting reveals two complementary needs: (i) a semantically grounded way to generate candidate labels for benchmarking, and (ii) a robust learner under the coupled effect of label ambiguity and feature corruption (“dual-noise coupling”). For (i), we introduce a corpus-informed semantic-affective prior for candidate-label construction by fusing GloVe vectors with ANEW affective ratings. This representation injects corpus-derived semantic information into EEG-based PLL and supports candidate-label distributions that better preserve inter-emotion relatedness. For (ii), we develop PANA-PL (Prototype-Aligned Noise-Augmented Partial-Label Learning), an EEG-oriented PLL framework that aligns prototype-based and classifier-based predictions via a stop-gradient KL objective to provide geometric cues for disambiguation. To mitigate low-SNR issues, PANA-PL further uses a controlled, mixup-inspired noise augmentation strategy that regularizes feature learning while keeping candidate labels fixed. Experiments on four SEED-series datasets (SEED, SEED-IV, SEED-V, and SEED-VII) show that PANA-PL achieves leading or competitive performance against selected reproducible PLL baselines under the same controlled protocol and two candidate-label generation scenarios, with statistically significant improvements confirmed on some dataset–distribution combinations.

title: An improved multi-instance learning model with clinical-guided cross-attention for postoperative early recurrence prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma using histopathological images
abstract: Objectives: This study focuses on the early recurrence prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), a prevalent and life-threatening liver cancer, following surgical resection. Addressing the challenges posed by postoperative recurrence, particularly in early stages, is pivotal for improving patient outcomes. Our aim is to develop a computer-aided diagnostic tool that integrates clinical data and whole slide images (WSIs) within a multimodal learning framework to enhance prediction performance. Methods: Given the direct correlation between tissue structure in WSIs and patient prognosis, combined with the complementary nature of comprehensive patient profiling derived from clinical data, we propose an innovative multimodal fusion approach. Traditional methods, whether based solely on WSIs or multimodal fusion (e.g., CT/MRI and clinical data), have limitations. To overcome the challenges associated with WSI-based methods, we introduce tumor annotation-guided early recurrence probability heatmaps (ER-ProbMaps) to extract robust features relevant for early recurrence prediction. For multimodal fusion, our method incorporates clinical-guided cross-attention mechanisms to facilitate seamless integration of clinical data and WSI features. Findings: The results demonstrate that our proposed Improved Multiple Instance Learning (Improved MIL) model, which leverages ER-ProbMaps, outperforms all unimodal methods. Specifically, when compared to the state-of-the-art unimodal method, our model achieves a significant AUC increase of 1.6% and an ACC increase of 17.7%. Furthermore, in comparison with multimodal fusion methods, our Improved MIL model with Clinical-Guided Cross-Attention (Improved MIL-CGCA) surpasses all multimodal approaches. Notably, when benchmarked against the state-of-the-art multimodal method, our model exhibits an AUC improvement of 3% and demonstrates superior performance. These findings underscore the critical role of integrating clinical data and WSIs within a multimodal learning framework for enhanced early recurrence prediction in HCC. Novelty: This research introduces a novel multimodal learning framework that integrates clinical data and WSIs, leveraging tumor annotation-guided ER-ProbMaps and cross-attention mechanisms for improved early recurrence prediction in HCC. Our findings emphasize the importance of considering both imaging and clinical data for accurate and reliable predictions, fostering a significant advancement in the field of computer-aided HCC diagnosis and management.

title: Bio-inspired spiking encoders for Alzheimer’s disease staging via longitudinal multi-modal neuroimaging
abstract: Multimodal learning from longitudinal neuroimaging is essential for early Alzheimer’s disease (AD) diagnosis, yet conventional recurrent models often struggle with irregular temporal dynamics and high-dimensional noise inherent in clinical data. This paper presents BiTSNN, a bio-inspired temporal spiking neural network that processes T1-MRI, T2-MRI, and resting-state fMRI trajectories via parallel leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) encoders with differentiable, modality-specific decay factors, enabling adaptive integration of multi-modal evidence over heterogeneous time horizons. A missingness-aware masking mechanism and an atlas-informed ROI-Activity encoding are further incorporated as design explorations. The learned feature space is evaluated via KMeans++ clustering and Hungarian matching; the CN/MCI/AD groups represent disease-severity stages rather than distinct pathological subtypes. Experiments on ADNI demonstrate a five-seed averaged accuracy of 52.8% and AUC of 0.603, outperforming LSTM and Transformer-based encoders in both accuracy and cluster-label concordance. A controlled no-spike ablation confirms that discrete spike dynamics are the primary source of supervised gains (p<0.05, five seeds), and membrane accumulation acts as a phenomenological analogue of pathological burden rather than a literal proxy. BiTSNN offers a biologically grounded and parameter-efficient alternative to conventional recurrent architectures for longitudinal AD diagnosis.

title: DCIA-SOH: Degradation-causal invariant adaptation for cross-dataset battery state-of-health prediction via uncertainty-guided pseudo-labeling
abstract: Accurate battery state-of-health (SOH) estimation across heterogeneous charging protocols remains a fundamental obstacle to deploying data-driven battery management systems. This difficulty arises because networks trained on one dataset tend to encode protocol-specific artefacts as spurious predictors of capacity fade, instead of capturing the underlying electrochemical degradation signals. To address this challenge, a Degradation-Causal Invariant Adaptation framework, DCIA-SOH, is proposed for cross-dataset state-of-health prediction using only unlabeled target samples. The framework integrates four jointly trained modules coordinated by a four-stage physics-aware curriculum. A Dynamic Degradation-Causal Disentanglement (D2CD) module minimises the mutual information between causal and domain-specific subspaces. A Dynamic Environment Expansion Invariant Risk Minimisation (DEE-IRM) module constructs up to twelve training environments by combining source protocols with pseudo-labeled target data. An Uncertainty-Guided Pseudo-Labeling (UGPL) module selects trustworthy target samples through Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout variance. An Uncertainty-Reweighted Hierarchical Prototype (URHP) module aligns degradation representations across domains. DCIA-SOH is evaluated on four cross-domain transfer tasks that span three public lithium-ion datasets and is compared against eleven baselines. It attains the lowest error on every task, reducing the mean absolute error on Task A by 30.8% relative to GroupDRO and by 22.9% relative to the strongest Task A baseline, CiPhy-SOH.

title: SIM-Unet: A spatial interaction mamba network for multimodal MRI segmentation of multiple brain tumor types
abstract: Brain tumors (BTs) are a class of severe diseases, and their accurate segmentation is of great importance for radiotherapy planning and treatment response assessment. However, due to the complex morphology of brain tumors, the heterogeneity of MRI data, and the highly imbalanced voxel distribution among different tumor subregions, automatic segmentation methods still face significant challenges in fine-grained modeling and generalization capability. This paper proposes SIM-Unet, a segmentation network for multiple brain tumor types. Specifically, a multi-encoder architecture is adopted for feature extraction, thereby avoiding information loss caused by a single encoder that learns only shared inter-modality features. Furthermore, by incorporating medical priors, a cross-modal feature fusion strategy is designed to effectively integrate global semantic information while preserving modality-specific local discriminative features. In addition, a Spatial Interaction Mamba module is introduced, which performs parallel modeling of feature sequences along the axial, coronal, and sagittal directions, compensating for the insufficient spatial interactions of single-sequence modeling in three-dimensional scenarios. To address voxel imbalance and boundary ambiguity across different brain tumor types and their subregions, a joint loss function based on voxel weighting and boundary constraints is proposed to enhance segmentation accuracy in complex regions. Experiments on multiple public datasets and a single-center external validation cohort demonstrated that SIM-Unet achieved superior segmentation performance and maintained relatively stable external validation performance under the imaging and preprocessing conditions evaluated in this study. Its generalizability across different centers, scanners, and imaging protocols requires further validation.

title: Tri-HGNet: A feature-driven dynamic hypergraph framework for medical image segmentation
abstract: Accurate segmentation of medical images is crucial for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning. Although existing methodologies have made significant progress in this domain, they still face challenges in dynamically capturing multi-scale, high-order semantic relationships that are tightly coupled with image content. To address this issue, we propose a feature-driven dynamic hypergraph construction approach—Feature-Driven Dynamic Hypergraph Topology—and design the Tri-HGNet framework based on it. Unlike models that rely on static or structurally adaptive graphs, the core design of Tri-HGNet lies in a heterogeneous hypergraph structure that reconstructs three structurally distinct topologies in parallel during each forward pass, according to the evolving semantic features in intermediate layers. This mechanism is realized through three complementary hyperedge construction strategies: (1) global k-NN hyperedges for capturing long-range dependencies; (2) local window hyperedges for fine-grained boundary and texture delineation; and (3) semantic prototype hyperedges to enforce cross-region category consistency. These heterogeneous information sources are integrated within a symmetrically normalized hypergraph convolution framework. Extensive experiments on three challenging public datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of Tri-HGNet. Notably, it achieves a competitive 84.23% Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) on the Synapse multi-organ CT dataset—on par with the strongest baselines—while yielding significant improvements in polyp and dermoscopic lesion segmentation tasks. Our work offers a flexible and effective graph-based modeling framework for medical image segmentation.

title: Reasoning towards endpoints: A two-stage, evidence-augmented method for training-free clinical trial outcome prediction
abstract: Clinical trial outcome prediction involves predicting whether a trial is successful by analyzing its components before the trial begins. However, existing methods are training-based, which struggle to generalize to clinical trial scenarios not encountered during training due to the limited availability of annotated data. They also neglect the relationships among trial status, primary endpoints, and outcomes, resulting in discrepancies between predicted outcomes and prespecified trial endpoints. This paper proposes a Two-stage Evidence-based and Endpoint-guided Method (TEEM) for training-free clinical trial outcome prediction. Specifically, the TEEM decomposes clinical trial outcome prediction into two sub-tasks: clinical trial status prediction and primary endpoint prediction. It employs a two-stage mechanism that integrates the sub-tasks. In the first stage, TEEM leverages multiple Large Language Model (LLM) agents and an evidence-based retrieval-augmented generation mechanism to identify key factors contributing to trial status. In the second stage, an endpoint-guided agent is introduced to ensure alignment between predicted outcomes and prespecified trial endpoints. Extensive experiments on the TOP dataset demonstrate that TEEM outperforms both the state-of-the-art training-free Plan-and-Solve method and the training-based LIFTED method.

title: Domain generalization meets mutual bi-attention: A novel approach to drug-target prediction
abstract: Deep learning-based drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction models have demonstrated promising predictive performance. However, due to the notorious distribution shift issue, well-trained DTI models often fail to generalize effectively in real-world applications. While some domain adaptation (DA)-based methods have been proposed to address this issue, they typically require access to source data, which is often impractical in realistic scenarios due to privacy concerns or data transmission costs. Consequently, the DA-based methods frequently fail without the source data. This motivates us to incorporate domain generalization (DG) into the DTI prediction. To achieve this goal, we’ve designed an innovative DG-DTI model and established a corresponding generalization bound to support it theoretically. Specifically, DG-DTI employs a mutual bi-directional cross-attention mechanism to align the data representations of drugs and proteins, followed by an attention-based pooling module to extract domain-invariant interaction features. Experimental results on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that our model attains state-of-the-art generalization performance in accuracy for novel drugs and targets, even without DA.

title: Adaptive hierarchical graph learning and fusion for brain disease identification
abstract: Adaptive graph learning methods based on functional brain network analysis have become a promising direction for detecting mental and neurological disorders, as they can flexibly obtain task-optimized functional representations guided by data labels. However, the existing methods typically only adaptively capture the single-scale information, ignoring the hierarchical property of the brain. This not only limits the perspective of the graph learning but also does not conform to the prior knowledge of the brain in biology. In addition, when faced with multi-scale brain functional representations, existing methods lack an effective fusion strategy to integrate them. To address the above issues, we propose AHGLF, a novel adaptive hierarchical graph learning and fusion framework for identifying brain diseases. We aim to construct the learnable hierarchical graph in an interpretable manner and use a comprehensive fusion strategy to integrate information at different scales. Specifically, we first innovatively develop an adaptive graph generation process, which cyclically uses a Transformer-based graph generator and an orthogonal clustering-based clustering layer in sequence to generate graphs of different scales, thereby simulating the hierarchical property of the brain. After that, we design a novel fusion strategy to comprehensively integrate multi-scale information according to the scale-specific uniqueness, cross-scale similarity, and inter-scale interaction. We evaluate our method extensively on the REST-meta-MDD and ABIDE-I datasets. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method exhibits better identification performance and maintains interpretability.

title: CoJDA-Net: A contrastive joint domain adaptation network for reliable fault diagnosis of high-speed train bogies under variable operating conditions
abstract: The reliability of bogie transmission systems is paramount for the safe operation of high-speed trains. However, developing robust data-driven fault diagnosis models remains challenging due to distribution shifts caused by variable operating conditions and the scarcity of labeled data. Although existing deep domain adaptation methods effectively align global distributions, they often neglect the discriminability of features within specific classes, leading to fuzzy decision boundaries and intra-class confusion during transfer tasks. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel transfer learning framework termed the Contrastive Joint Domain Adaptation Network (CoJDA-Net). This method synergizes a Convolutional Neural Network backbone with a dual-alignment strategy to ensure both domain invariance and class discriminability. Specifically, Joint Maximum Mean Discrepancy is employed to align the joint distributions of deep features and classifier predictions across domains. Complementing this, a pseudo-label-guided Supervised Contrastive Learning module is introduced to explicitly minimize intra-class variance and maximize inter-class separability in the target domain, thereby resolving the confusion near decision boundaries. Extensive experiments conducted on the laboratory-scale BJTU-RAO bogie dataset demonstrate that CoJDA-Net achieves superior diagnostic performance, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art methods. The framework exhibits robust generalization capabilities in challenging cross-speed and cross-load scenarios, providing a promising solution for the intelligent condition monitoring of railway transportation systems.

title: Physics-augmented federated continual learning for rotating machinery fault diagnosis
abstract: Rotating machinery fault diagnosis increasingly relies on distributed vibration data that cannot be centralized due to privacy constraints. Federated learning provides privacy-preserving collaboration, yet practical deployments must continually accommodate emerging fault classes and drifting operating conditions, which often cause catastrophic forgetting and negative transfer. We propose Physics-Augmented Federated Continual Learning (PA-FCL), a federated class-incremental continual learning framework that injects vibration-signal physics through spectral-consistent replay. PA-FCL combines (i) a spectral-consistent signal generator for condition-specific, data-free replay without sharing raw measurements, (ii) condition-aware knowledge distillation weighted by physical similarity (e.g., speed/load) to mitigate negative transfer, and (iii) a frequency-regularized optimization strategy that stabilizes diagnostic spectral features over time. Experiments on three public rotating-machinery datasets (CWRU, JNU, and XJTU) show that PA-FCL improves accuracy by up to 22.06% and reduces forgetting by 46.83% compared with representative federated learning baselines. The results suggest that PA-FCL provides a promising approach for federated continual learning on non-stationary vibration signals.

title: CMCA: A cluster matching based class-incremental unsupervised domain adaptation method for bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: In variable-condition bearing fault diagnosis, target condition data often arrive incrementally over the bearing service lifecycle. To address this, we introduce a class-incremental unsupervised domain adaptation (CI-UDA) framework that jointly aligns domains under varying label spaces while preserving knowledge across incremental time steps. Existing sample-based shared class filtering and pseudo-label assignment methods overlook the uncertainties introduced by inter-domain differences and lack a holistic, class-level decision-making approach. This leads to inaccurate shared class identification, low-precision supervisory signals, and suboptimal solutions. This paper proposes cluster matching to address these issues. Our method first calibrates the source model’s latent space via augmented source domain training, then clusters target domain features, and optimally matches these clusters to class labels using a designed matching protocol. This provides clear, precise supervision signals for the target data. Our approach is validated on three datasets, achieving an average diagnostic accuracy exceeding 95% and outperforming existing methods.

title: Annotation noise-aware semi-supervised and domain adaptive learning for 3D medical imaging
abstract: Obtaining annotated data for medical image segmentation is a labor-intensive and costly task, due to the need for per-pixel labeling. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) offers a promising solution by utilizing a small amount of labeled data and large-scale unlabeled data. However, most SSL techniques assume labeled and unlabeled data share the same distribution, which is often not the case in real-world settings where domain shifts between datasets are common. Additionally, noisy labels, arising from annotator errors, pose significant challenges, particularly in medical image analysis. While SSL, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA), and noisy label handling are crucial to clinical applications, current methods typically address these issues separately. In this work, we propose a unified framework that simultaneously tackles SSL, UDA, and noisy label learning. Our approach introduces two key modules: Frequency-Aware Feature Transformation (FAFT) and Adaptive Memory Cross-Attention (AMCA). FAFT transforms encoder features into the frequency domain, separating them into low- and high-frequency (HF) components. We introduce controlled noise to HF components, which capture object edges, and exchange them between labeled and unlabeled data, helping the model learn robust high-frequency representations less sensitive to noisy annotations. To enhance SSL and UDA in a unified manner, we utilize AMCA, which intervenes in the training process of labeled data by incorporating unlabeled data into the learning process. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate the superior performance of our method in both clean and noisy label scenarios.

title: Electrical impedance tomography system enabled breast cancer detection using firefly shepherd optimization based deep convolutional neural network
abstract: Breast Cancer (BC) is considered the leading cancer in women. Despite the availability of various detection methods, accurately identifying BC using Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) data remains a significant challenge. This difficulty arises from the complex nature of EIT data, which makes it hard to extract and interpret features reliably for early cancer detection. The major issue addressed is the challenge of accurately detecting BC at an early stage, which is crucial for improving patient survival rates. Thus, an effective technique is designed employing Firefly Shepherd Optimization (FSO) based Deep Convolutional Neural Network for BC detection. FSO is introduced by amalgamating the Firefly Algorithm (FA) with the Shuffled Shepherd Optimization Algorithm (SSOA). From the segmented result, feature extraction is performed. Then, the cancer detection process is done utilizing a Deep CNN classifier. By extracting features, namely image-level as well as segment-level features, the performance of the model is effectively increased by reducing the computational complexity. Moreover, the extraction of unique and important features enables the classifier to generate accuracy in an optimal way through the fitness measure. Furthermore, FSO-based Deep CNN acquired maximal performance employing measures such as accuracy, specificity, and sensitivity of 96.48%, 97.93%, and 97.48%.

title: A physics-guided contrastive multi-view clustering framework for unsupervised fault diagnosis of rotating machinery
abstract: To address the insufficient fault-discriminative information of single-modality signals and the lack of reliable supervision in unlabeled rotating machinery diagnosis under complex operating conditions, this study proposes a Physics-Guided Contrastive Multi-View Clustering (PhyCMVC) framework. Specifically, homogeneous multi-view inputs are constructed from raw signals in the time, time-frequency, and graph domains to enhance feature diversity and complementarity. A multi-branch feature extraction backbone is developed to learn view-specific representations, where a bidirectional long short-term memory network captures temporal dependencies, a convolutional neural network extracts time-frequency spatial patterns, and a graph attention network learns structural relationships. To unify heterogeneous embeddings, a cross-modal contrastive fusion module achieves representation alignment and fusion across views. Beyond purely data-driven learning, a physics-informed consistency regularization term incorporates fault-related physical mechanisms into clustering optimization, and a deep divergence-based clustering loss enables end-to-end optimization. Experimental results on four diagnostic tasks constructed from the Southeast University dataset and the Xi’an Jiaotong University gearbox dataset demonstrate that PhyCMVC achieves the best diagnostic performance, with ACC values averaged over 20 runs of 95.2% on the full-task Southeast University setting, 93.4% on the comprehensive Xi’an Jiaotong University gearbox task, 99.5% on the SEU-Gear task, and 99.1% on the SEU-Bear task. These results verify its effectiveness and robustness across diverse operating conditions.

title: A spatio-temporal neural relation extraction model for end-to-end brain directed network mapping
abstract: Fast and reliable electroencephalography (EEG)-based directed network estimation is crucial for characterizing directed and causal brain interactions in real-time applications such as brain-computer interfaces and closed-loop interventions. This study introduces Deep Neural Network Directed Network Estimation (DeepNNetDNE), a high-efficiency end-to-end framework for EEG brain network estimation that leverages a Spatio-Temporal Neural Relation Extraction (STNRE) model to directly infer network interactions from brain signals. The trained model learns the underlying rules governing relational representations from large-scale data and serves as a generalized neural relation extractor for end-to-end estimation of directed networks from new brain signals across different scenarios (e.g., different numbers of channels and data lengths). The proposed DeepNNetDNE exhibits superior capacity to extract network patterns from noisy EEG signals while significantly reducing computational cost compared to benchmark methods. Additionally, DeepNNetDNE better captures default mode network patterns during the resting state, with network hubs more consistent with empirical knowledge; and further reveals network reorganizations during motor imagery in post-stroke hemiplegic patients, characterized by lateralization toward the uninjured hemisphere as a compensatory mechanism, which may serve as an indicator for assessing motor function. DeepNNetDNE distinguishes itself by eliminating the need for instance-level prior assumptions, explicit modeling, and hyperparameter tuning required in existing network analysis methods, thereby demonstrating strong potential in real-time directed network analysis.

title: Enhancing cross-dataset EEG microstate decoding: A frequency-band dependent framework with bidirectional long short-term memory network
abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) microstate analysis serves as a critical tool for investigating dynamic brain networks. However, limited robustness in cross-dataset applications significantly constrains model generalizability and clinical utility. This issue arises because microstates in different frequency bands exhibit distinct responses to data heterogeneity, yet this critical factor lacks systematic investigation and quantification, resulting in an absence of theoretical guidance for optimal frequency band selection in fields such as brain-computer interfaces. To address this gap, this study proposes a novel deep learning evaluation framework, utilizing standardized data preprocessing and multi-model comparisons to systematically investigate the topological stability and classification performance of microstates in the theta, alpha, and beta frequency bands across datasets for the first time. We integrated three independent, publicly available EEG datasets and employed a sequence-to-sequence model based on bidirectional long short-term memory networks to achieve efficient cross-dataset classification of four canonical microstates. Our key findings demonstrate that alpha-band microstates exhibit exceptional cross-dataset robustness, characterized by highly stable topological structures (within-class correlation ranging from 0.894 to 0.933) and cross-subject classification accuracy exceeding 91%. In the most challenging cross-dataset validation scenario, the classification accuracy of alpha-band microstates reached a peak of 85.12%, significantly outperforming theta (62.85%) and beta (79.04%) bands. Compared to state-of-the-art methods, our approach improved cross-dataset classification performance by 16.93%. In sum, our study quantifies the stability advantage of alpha-band microstates for the first time, providing a robust theoretical and methodological foundation for frequency band selection strategies, with direct implications for brain-computer interfaces and closed-loop neuromodulation systems.

title: Cascaded projection-based motor imagery EEG decoding for brain-computer interfaces
abstract: Motor imagery, as a key brain–computer interface paradigm, has been extensively applied in brain–computer interface scenarios. However, accurate electroencephalogram (EEG) decoding remains a significant challenge due to EEG non-stationarity and low signal-to-noise ratio. These factors undermine the reliability and efficiency of brain–computer interface systems. To address this issue, we introduce a motor imagery EEG decoding method that involves three key steps: EEG signal reconstruction, multi-scale feature extraction and dimensionality reduction. In particular, we propose a novel feature extraction method AFSCRTS, which incorporates adaptive filter bank selection block and time–frequency domain-based feature extraction framework to extract multi-scale features. Besides, an adaptive weighted spatial discriminant projection (AWSDP) is adopted to reduce dimensional redundancy while maintaining superior classification performance. When AWSDP is applied, the model successfully mitigates the challenge of high dimensionality, while maintaining the same high level of accuracy. The proposed AFSCRTS is validated on binary classification tasks of three typical datasets, achieving average accuracies of 90.39%, 92.04% and 74.35%. In addition, when evaluating AFSCRTS on four-class tasks, our method also achieves superior classification results, which validates that AFSCRTS delivers outstanding performance in EEG decoding. Our work provides distinct advantages over most baseline approaches, which contributes to the further development of brain–computer interfaces.

title: Twist3DNet: A multiscale bidirectional 2D-3D information fusion prognostic classification network for hypopharyngeal cancer
abstract: Hypopharyngeal carcinoma is a malignant tumor with a concealed location and is difficult to detect in the early stages. Accurate prognosis assessment of hypopharyngeal cancer can help doctors develop reasonable treatment plans. Given that MRI is a primary modality for early-stage hypopharyngeal carcinoma detection, developing an AI-powered prognostic assessment system for hypopharyngeal cancer MRI examinations demonstrates substantial clinical value. However, hypopharyngeal cancer MRI adopts vertical-axis acquisition with larger slice gaps, resulting in lower pixel density along the vertical axis compared to coronal and sagittal axes. This poses a challenge for traditional 2D or 3D intelligent neural networks to adequately extract features from hypopharyngeal cancer MRI images. To this end, we propose Twist3DNet, a multiscale bidirectional 2D-3D information fusion prognostic classification network for hypopharyngeal cancer. We design a bidirectional fusion module, BT Block, to bidirectionally fuse the context from 2D Branch and 3D Branch. We propose a module, 3D M Module, with multiple receptive fields to capture global and local information in MRI images. We validate our method on the hypopharyngeal cancer dataset, BraTS2018 dataset and 3DLSC-COVID dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves exceptional performance on these datasets, achieving mF1 scores of 75.78%, 89.09%, and 89.87%, respectively. Furthermore, a comparative analysis reveals that our method can effectively transform 2D networks into 2D-3D hybrid networks, surpassing the performance of corresponding 3D networks. We have made our code available. The code is available at: https://github.com/yk1842/Twist3DNet.

title: ICRD: Self-supervised medical multimodal representation learning with intra-modality contrastive learning and replaced token detection
abstract: In medical multimodal learning, due to the heterogeneity of multimodal data, different types of data require distinct preprocessing and feature extraction methods, leading to semantic inconsistency across modalities in the representation space, which hinders effective representation learning. Therefore, multimodal alignment is necessary to maintain information consistency between the representations of different modalities. However, most existing works primarily focus on inter-modality alignment while ignoring the inherent misalignment within each modality, resulting in insufficient multimodal alignment. Additionally, the fused multimodal representations learned by the model often exhibit insufficient robustness when facing modality noise, which directly influences the performance of subsequent fine-tuning. To address these issues, a model based on self-supervised medical multimodal representation learning with intra-modality contrastive learning and replaced token detection (ICRD) is proposed. Specifically, for the extracted image and tabular representations, intra-modality contrastive learning is designed and combined with inter-modality contrastive learning to compensate for the limitations of the latter, improving the multimodal alignment. Furthermore, after fusion, a novel self-supervised task called replaced token detection for the multimodal representations is proposed, which jointly optimizes the model with other self-supervised tasks during pre-training to further enhance the robustness of the multimodal representations when facing corruption in tabular data. Experimental results on large-scale and small-scale medical image–tabular datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of ICRD, consistently outperforming previous methods, including supervised single-modal, supervised multimodal, self-supervised single-modal and self-supervised multimodal. In the frozen fine-tuning setting, the AUC of ICRD can achieve 92.85% on Enlarged Cardiomediastinum and 90.52% on Cardiomegaly, and 87.68% on BrEaST, obtaining a significant performance improvement.

title: A tri-view adaptive decomposition framework for intelligent fault diagnosis of industrial machinery via fluctuation–structure representation of non-stationary signals
abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis under varying operating conditions remains challenging because non-stationary mechanical signals usually contain heterogeneous diagnostic information in different forms. A central challenge is to organize complementary multi-view representations while distinguishing fault-sensitive fluctuations from slowly varying structural context. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Tri-view Adaptive Decomposition Framework (TADF) for non-stationary fault diagnosis. First, a diagnosis-oriented tri-view embedding strategy is developed to construct temporal, spectral, and induced temporal-spectral collaborative branches in a shared latent space. The aligned latent states are then decomposed into branch-specific fluctuation states and coordinated structural states, providing structured inputs for subsequent collaborative encoding. Second, a Tri-view Adaptive Decomposition Encoder (TADE) is designed to refine transient fault-sensitive fluctuations while progressively accumulating structure memories across branches. Finally, an adaptive fusion module integrates branch-wise diagnostic evidence and fused fluctuation-structure information for final classification. Cross-condition experiments conducted on the wind turbine gearbox dataset and the bearing dataset show that TADF achieves competitive cross-condition diagnostic performance compared with representative fault diagnosis models.

title: A comprehensive survey on crack detection and classification: Methods, challenges, and future directions
abstract: Automated crack detection and classification have become essential components of data-driven structural health monitoring systems. In recent years, advances in machine learning and deep learning have significantly accelerated research on vision-based crack inspection, leading to a rapidly expanding body of literature. This survey provides a comprehensive review of peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2026, focusing on computational methods for crack detection, classification, and segmentation in concrete structures. The reviewed works are examined from a machine learning perspective, encompassing preprocessing strategies, feature representations, learning paradigms, network architectures, and evaluation indicators. Particular attention is given to the transition from traditional approaches based on handcrafted features to modern deep learning methods. In addition, the survey identifies key methodological trends, including the predominance of supervised learning, the higher prevalence of image-level classification relative to pixel-level segmentation, and the growing interest in lightweight and deployment-oriented architectures. The analysis further highlights persistent challenges in the literature, such as dataset bias, limited generalization across domains, annotation scarcity, and insufficient cross-dataset evaluation. Based on these findings, the survey outlines future research directions, emphasizing weakly and self-supervised learning, robust cross-dataset validation, fine-grained crack characterization, and model designs tailored for real-world deployment.

title: Neural network-based dynamic functional connectivity estimation for motor imagery decoding from EEG
abstract: Accurate decoding of motor imagery (MI) from electroencephalography (EEG) signals is critical for building reliable brain–computer interface (BCI) systems. However, existing approaches often struggle to capture complex, non-stationary neural interactions due to limited modeling of dynamic inter-regional dependencies. In this work, we propose FMICNet, a novel deep learning framework that integrates dynamic functional connectivity (FC) modeling into the feature space of EEG signals via mutual information estimation. Unlike conventional methods that estimate static FC from raw sensor space, FMICNet models nonlinear, time-varying dependencies directly between learned feature representations. Specifically, we design a neural mutual information estimator to capture dynamic connectivity between channel-wise feature maps, enabling task-adaptive and interpretable representations. FMICNet is trained using an alternating optimization strategy that jointly updates the MINE-based connectivity estimator and the classification network. Experiments on three benchmark EEG motor-related datasets, including two motor imagery datasets and one motor execution (ME) dataset, demonstrate that FMICNet achieves the best average performance across datasets and shows improvements over strong baseline methods. Ablation studies confirm the importance of dynamic FC modeling and mutual information-based estimation. Our findings from the MI experiments suggest that incorporating feature-space mutual information modeling provides a principled and effective approach for enhancing the performance and interpretability of EEG-based MI decoding.

title: EfDIC-BrainNets: EEG-fNIRS dynamic interactive causal brain networks for emotion recognition
abstract: Bimodal joint analysis via electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) has attracted considerable attention in affective computing. Nevertheless, most existing fusion methods are limited to simple feature concatenation. They fail to effectively capture the complex interactions between modalities and the nonstationary nature of brain connectivity during emotional processing. These limitations hinder improvements in emotion recognition performance. To address this issue, we propose a novel framework centered on constructing EEG-fNIRS dynamic interactive causal brain networks (EfDIC-BrainNets) for accurate emotion recognition. Specifically, we introduce an intermodal relationship modeling strategy that leverages neurovascular coupling to bridge the heterogeneity between EEG and fNIRS and introduce a time-varying conditional Granger causality algorithm to dynamically track nonstationary causal dependencies between signals throughout emotional fluctuations. Accordingly, EfDIC-BrainNets are constructed to characterize fine-grained, evolving interactions between modalities. To effectively learn discriminative representations from these brain networks, we further develop an edge-oriented spatiotemporal graph convolutional network for emotion recognition. Comprehensive experiments on the public dataset ENTER show that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 99.51% in a four-class emotion recognition task, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art baseline approaches. This study provides a novel perspective on EEG-fNIRS bimodal fusion and an effective framework for constructing dynamic causal brain networks for emotion recognition.

title: A MONAI-based software framework for architecture–task analysis in 3D medical image segmentation
abstract: Neural architectures for three dimensional medical image segmentation are often compared under heterogeneous pipelines, which makes it difficult to separate the effect of model design from implementation details. This paper presents an open source software framework, built on MONAI, that provides a unified pipeline for training, evaluating, and visualising multiple 3D segmentation architectures across anatomically diverse tasks. The framework standardises orientation, resampling, intensity normalisation, patch based training with 643 crops, sliding window inference, and per class evaluation. It includes a registry of ten MONAI implementations, covering compact convolutional networks (UNet, BasicUNet, BasicUNet++, SegResNet, HighResNet, Attention U Net, DynUNet, VNet) and transformer based models (UNETR, Swin UNETR). A central per class metric aggregator computes present case macro Dice, micro pooled precision, recall, F1, and boundary metrics (95th percentile Hausdorff distance and mean surface distance) without storing per case predictions. A whole volume visualisation module generates full volume overlays that juxtapose ground truth and predictions from all models on the same slice. We illustrate the framework on five Medical Segmentation Decathlon tasks (Brain tumor, Heart, Hippocampus, Hepatic Vessel, Spleen). Under a unified, resource constrained regime with 643 patches and moderate augmentation, compact convolutional networks define a strong efficiency frontier. SegResNet achieves the highest mean present case macro Dice averaged across tasks (0.797), closely followed by BasicUNet (0.795) and BasicUNet++ (0.789), while transformer models (UNETR, Swin UNETR) reach 0.679–0.765 despite two to six times larger parameter counts. Per task winners are BasicUNet for Brain tumor (0.721) and Spleen (0.964), SegResNet for Heart (0.947) and Hepatic Vessel (0.486), and BasicUNet++ for Hippocampus (0.876). To examine whether this conclusion depends on the default crop size, we add a targeted 963 patch sensitivity analysis on Spleen and Hippocampus using BasicUNet, SegResNet, UNETR, and Swin UNETR. The larger patch regime does not reverse the ranking among these representative models: compact CNNs remain ahead on both tasks. On Hippocampus, compact CNNs improve slightly at 963 while transformer models marginally degrade, maintaining a consistent CNN advantage across both patch regimes. The software is released as a MONAI-based Python implementation under the MIT License at https://github.com/ReflectIQBusiness/monai-arch-benchmark.git. The repository includes configuration files, a small unit test suite, an example experiment script, and a requirements.txt file to support reproducible installation and easy adaptation to new datasets. It provides a practical tool for architecture–task analysis, enabling researchers and practitioners to benchmark new models, reproduce results, and study inductive biases under realistic 3D segmentation constraints.

title: Rare fault diagnosis using federated learning driven by client access mechanism
abstract: Diagnosing rare faults in mechatronic equipment is challenging because each client has only a limited number of fault samples. Federated learning (FL) can be used to jointly train fault diagnosis (FD) models for each client. In cases where clients with rare fault samples also suffer from poor-quality issues, existing FL methods cannot work since rare fault features cannot be well extracted. Some powerful clients may have a large volume of poor-quality samples unrelated to the rare fault, which will further complicate the extraction of rare-fault features. If they cannot provide additional innovative information for the feature extraction of other faults, it is unnecessary for them to participate in the federation. This paper focuses on designing a client access mechanism for FL to guarantee that only clients with innovative information can participate in the federation. Adequate contribution to decision-making, rather than sample size, is used to evaluate innovation, which helps guide the client access mechanism for FL. By this means, a powerful client without innovation is not allowed to participate in the federation to prevent the negative impacts of redundant information on the feature extraction of rare faults. Innovation evaluation guides the federation aggregation strategy, ensuring that clients with more innovation-related insights into rare faults can play a more significant role in the federation process. This advantage of the proposed method also enables clients without historical samples of rare faults to diagnose rare faults. Experimental results in FD for motors demonstrate that even rare fault samples polluted by strong noise can contribute significantly to the federation model. The proposed method’s FD accuracy can be improved by 18.92% compared with the traditional method.

title: Reinforced open-set domain adaptation with a trainable generalized extreme value model for fault diagnosis
abstract: Accurate fault diagnosis under varying operating conditions is crucial for reliable and safe maintenance of rotating machinery. In practical industrial scenarios, diagnosis models are often required to transfer knowledge from a labeled source domain to an unlabeled target domain with domain shifts, while previously unseen fault modes may appear. This cross-domain open-set fault diagnosis (COSFD) problem is challenging since conventional closed-set models tend to misclassify unknown target samples into known source classes. Existing COSFD methods still face two limitations. First, extreme value theory-based domain adaptation (DA) methods typically rely on numerical parameter estimation, making them difficult to update the extreme value model together with the evolving deep feature distribution during network training. Second, transferability-based sample weighting strategies may produce suboptimal sample-selection decisions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a reinforced open-set DA (ROSDA) method. Specifically, a parameter-trainable generalized extreme value (GEV) model is integrated into the DA framework to estimate open-set probabilities, with its constrained parameters optimized by gradient descent. A reinforcement learning-based sample selector is constructed to progressively remove target unknown-class samples through long-term cumulative rewards, thereby improving sample-selection reliability and alleviating negative transfer. The retained target samples are then incorporated into adversarial DA to enhance shared-class alignment while preserving unknown-class separability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art DA methods.

title: Bearing fault diagnosis under mixed noise conditions via transferable ensemble residual shrinkage network and adaptive cost-sensitive learning
abstract: Recently, various fault diagnosis methods have been developed to combat data noise. However, factors like varying working conditions and random noise cause inconsistent signal-to-noise ratios across samples, resulting in unsatisfactory diagnosis results. Therefore, a bearing fault diagnosis method under mixed noise conditions via transferable ensemble residual shrinkage network (TERSN) and adaptive cost-sensitive learning (ACSL) is proposed in this work. The core of the TERSN is a transferable ensemble algorithm that dynamically adjusts the weights of the training samples according to their varying levels of training difficulty, ensuring that greater attention is given to misclassified samples during training. The updated weights are used for constructing an adaptive weighted cross-entropy loss function to support ACSL, enabling base classifiers of the TERSN to concentrate on samples with higher noise levels and effectively minimizing the impact of mixed noise. The base classifier of the TERSN employs an anti-noise residual convolutional network with improved selective kernel convolution module (ISKCM) and global parametric rectifier linear unit, where the ISKCM improves the diagnosis performance under mixed noise conditions. Experimental validation demonstrates that the proposed approach outperforms comparison approaches for fault diagnosis under mixed noise conditions. Specifically, the diagnosis accuracies of the proposed approach are 96.18% and 92.67% on the two bearing datasets, and are 2.34% and 2.40% higher than those of the best comparison approaches (93.84% and 90.27%) on the two datasets. Furthermore, the generalization performance of the proposed method is further verified on a gearbox dataset.

title: Coyote and Badger pine cone optimization-based Hierarchical scale convolutional neural network for multi-cancer detection using different image modalities
abstract: Early detection of various cancer types continues to be a significant challenge in oncology owing to the diverse nature of tumor biology. Conventional approaches to cancer diagnosis often focus on a single cancer category and primarily utilize standalone data modalities, including imaging techniques and biomarker analyses. This leads to delayed diagnoses, misclassification, and limited screening effectiveness. Thus, this research proposes a Coyote Pine Cone Optimization enabled Hierarchical Scale Convolutional Neural Network (CPCO_HSNet) based on medical image modalities, such as histopathological and microscopic images. Initially, histopathological images associated with breast, colon, and oral cancer detection are enhanced through a Guided Filter-based denoising process. Subsequently, blood cell segmentation is conducted using a Feedback Attention Network (FANet) that incorporates contour loss and constrained focal loss mechanisms. Following segmentation, feature extraction is performed by deriving texture and structural characteristics using Directional Local Extrema Patterns (DLEP) and Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) features. Finally, cancer detection is done by Hierarchical Scale Convolutional Neural Network (HSNet), and it is trained with the proposed Coyote Pine Cone Optimization (CPCO). Here, CPCO is designed by combining Coyote and Badger Optimization (CBO) and Pine Cone Optimization Algorithm (PCOA). The same processing framework is utilized for microscopic images in cervical cancer detection. Experimental results indicate that the CPCO_HSNet model attains an Accuracy of 96.64%, a True Positive Rate (TPR) of 95.72%, and a True Negative Rate (TNR) of 96.85%, demonstrating its effectiveness in cancer classification and diagnosis.

title: PHM-LLM: A cross-modal pre-trained LLM for bearing fault diagnosis and remaining useful life prediction
abstract: In recent years, deep learning has significantly advanced fault diagnosis and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction in prognostics and health management (PHM) through the end-to-end feature extraction of deep neural networks. However, most existing models in PHM are task-specific and scale-limited, which lead to noticeable performance bottlenecks in practical applications. Specifically, they exhibit poor generalization under data-scarce conditions and limited scalability when data are sufficient. Although self-supervised pre-training can alleviate these issues, its benefits remain constrained by the availability of vibration data and computational resources. To address these challenges, this paper introduces PHM-LLM, a novel cross-modal learning framework that adapts pre-trained large language models for bearing PHM. By fusing vibration signals and expert prompts through bidirectional cross-attention and Prompt-as-Prefix, PHM-LLM adapts pre-trained language representations to signal feature learning. During fine-tuning, it demonstrates strong generalization and scalability without additional domain pre-training. Extensive experiments on five benchmark datasets, including intra-condition and cross-condition evaluations for fault diagnosis and cross-bearing RUL prediction, demonstrate improved few-shot performance and sustained benefits from increasing training data relative to the evaluated small-scale DNN baselines. These results indicate that PHM-LLM exhibits generalization and data-scaling benefits analogous to those motivating foundation models within the evaluated PHM settings.

title: SegFlux: Physical morphology flow and analytical routing for volumetric medical image segmentation
abstract: Volumetric segmentation networks aggregate three-dimensional context, yet the spatial evolution of anatomical cross-sections remains indirectly constrained. We propose SegFlux, a compact framework that decomposes inter-slice variation into physical transport and morphological events. A residual encoder-decoder predicts direct segmentation logits, while two decoder-scale branches estimate signed distance states, bidirectional in-plane displacements in millimetres, and spacing-scaled events. Transportability-aware morphological routing uses an analytical contribution ratio with stopped gradients to combine the geometric candidates. Bounded multiscale residuals then correct the segmentation logits while preserving the direct prediction at initialization. Independently trained models are evaluated on AMOS22 liver CT, LiTS liver and tumor CT, and ACDC cardiac MRI. SegFlux achieves an AMOS22 five-fold outer-test Dice of 0.9642 ± 0.0039 and a Dice of 0.9618 ± 0.0051 on the untouched ten-case hold-out cohort. Its five-fold LiTS outer-test mean Dice scores are 0.9683 ± 0.0024 for whole liver, 0.8356 ± 0.0125 for tumor, and 0.9019 ± 0.0066 for macro Dice; ACDC is evaluated on its held-out test partition with a mean Dice of 0.9257. Component, spacing, routing, and capacity comparisons support the proposed design. With 12.17 million parameters in its AMOS22 configuration, SegFlux suggests the potential benefit of explicit geometric modeling alongside learned volumetric features under the evaluated protocols.

title: Fidelity without sharing: Source-free domain adaptive super-resolution for clinical ultrasound
abstract: While ultrasound image super-resolution (SR) offers significant clinical value, the deployment of a well-trained model is challenged by distribution and degradation variations due to the unavailability of source data. In this paper, we propose UNIT, an UNsupervised Image Translation framework for source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) in ultrasound image SR, which performs target-to-source image translation guided by the priors embedded within the source-trained SR model, aiming to achieve high-fidelity SR reconstruction under unseen domain shifts and unknown degradations in clinical deployment. Specifically, our style alignment module calibrates the style of target-domain inputs using source-domain representations distilled from the intermediate layers of the source-trained model. Our anatomy consistency mechanism simultaneously preserves structural invariance during this transfer by enforcing similarity against varied degradations. Finally, our content-style matching module aligns the output distribution with that of the corresponding inputs, ensuring domain-consistent SR reconstruction. UNIT is evaluated on two public datasets and two in-house hospital datasets. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UNIT yields high-fidelity SR predictions on the target domain even when the source domain is inaccessible, narrowing anatomical (SSIM) and fine-grained (HFEN) performance gaps to 0.02 and 0.04, respectively. Furthermore, UNIT consistently outperforms state-of-the-art SR techniques across three distinct cross-domain scenarios, achieving a mean PSNR improvement of 1.60 dB. UNIT presents an effective and robust solution for unbiased clinical SR deployment, revealing the potential for accurate downstream diagnosis.

title: A Federated Universal Domain Generalization Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Global Prototype Alignment and Decision Boundary Collaborative Optimization
abstract: The health status of industrial sensors often determines whether production equipment can operate effectively over the long term. In recent years, the development of federated domain generalization diagnosis methods has not only ensured data privacy among different industrial sectors, but also effectively addressed domain shifts in cross-condition diagnosis. However, due to drastic changes in industrial environments, differences in label spaces across different domains frequently occur. Therefore, this paper focuses on a practical and novel industrial diagnosis scenario, namely federated universal domain generalization, and proposes a diagnostic framework based on Global Prototype Alignment and Decision Boundary Collaborative Optimization (GPA-DBCO) to effectively identify private classes and unknown faults. First, by introducing domain-adversarial training and prototype alignment, the model is guided to learn domain-invariant feature representations that are insensitive to changes in working conditions. Second, a cross-client unknown fault prototype library is constructed on the server side to simulate potential unseen new fault types, thereby training a universal classifier. Finally, a distance–entropy-based joint optimization strategy for decision boundaries is designed, enabling the model to accurately identify common faults, private faults, and unknown faults simultaneously when deployed in an unknown target environment. Experiments were conducted on a sensor dataset from a nickel flash smelting furnace system, and the results verified the superiority and effectiveness of the GPA-DBCO diagnostic method.
